2000-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-leven-sa.titel: [Collected finds from Nasjonalbiblioteket 2000: news items, announcements, lists]

2000-virgin-larkin-virgin-encyclopedia-o.medium: Virgin Books in association with Muze UK, London

2001-01-01-globalguest-inoffizielles-gae.medium: globalguest.com/gb/TOUT – guestbook of the fan site jackieleven.com
2001-01-01-globalguest-inoffizielles-gae.kurz: The fan site's “Unofficial Jackie Leven guestbook” began on 01.01.2001 with a test entry by the webmaster (“PT”, Italy) and collected almost 100 entries by the end of 2001.
inhalt: The fan site's “Unofficial Jackie Leven guestbook” began on 01.01.2001 with a test entry by the webmaster (“PT”, Italy) and collected almost 100 entries by the end of 2001. At first fans praise the new site, which they say they found through the eGroup mailing list; organiser Mick Nolan is thanked, and the webmaster is addressed as “Paul”. He replies himself, for instance on the quality of the RealAudio samples (deliberately low, to encourage purchase) and with a forwarded message from Deborah Greenwood (24.08.2001) explaining the delays with the Haunted Valley CD *Munich Blues* and the bootleg *Deep in the Heart of Nowhere* (live at The Greys) by new British CD licensing procedures.

The entries trace the concert year: a tour with Andy White and Michael Weston King in Belgium and the Netherlands (AB Brussels, Assen, Eindhoven, Haarlem/Solingen relocation), Fareham, Winchester (Tower Arts Centre, 06.04.), Kirkcaldy (Path Tavern, 14.06.) and Dundee (15.06.), the Mirror Man concerts, a free concert on Southsea Common (29.07.), the 12 Bar Club with three new songs, Southampton, Leicester (The Musician), Jim's Cafe in Colne, two evenings at the Edinburgh Fringe, Stockholm and the German tour in October with Ron Sexsmith (Bremen, Bielefeld, Krefeld, Münster, Frankfurt, Hannover), with memories of the stage stories about Heineken, the “Schweinehund” and Sting's alleged helicopter crash. Fans from Australia recall performances in the Barossa Valley and at WOMAD, and a New Zealand visit in November is announced. A former DJ and stage manager at London's Dingwalls (1979–83) calls Doll by Doll a crowd favourite; fans ask about the announced Doll by Doll reissues and a best-of. The musician Chris Connelly writes from Chicago that Leven's songs saved him; Ecki Stieg links to a German interview on grenzwellen.com, and Liam Carson announces his interviews for the Irish Examiner and Irish News on the Ireland tour. On 09.12. a fan reports on the Christmas concert in Milford with the “Girls” (The Stornoway Girls).

2001-02-19-jackieleven-com-new-release-g.autor: Webmaster jackieleven.com (with a quotation from the Cooking Vinyl newsletter)

2001-04-10-hot-press-lorraine-sammelreze.kurz: The double review sets Jimmy Mac Carthy's “Lorraine” against Leven's “The Right To Remain Silent”.
inhalt: The double review sets Jimmy Mac Carthy's “Lorraine” against Leven's “The Right To Remain Silent”. Stokes judges Leven distinctly more favourably: he appreciates the combination of older and modern sound forms and the linguistic assurance of the songs.

2001-06-28-the-independent-always-look-o.kurz: Interview in a London pub (“Railway Tavern”) a few days before the release of *Creatures of Light and Darkness* (3 July 2001), which Martin counts as the 21st album of a 30-year career.
inhalt: Interview in a London pub (“Railway Tavern”) a few days before the release of *Creatures of Light and Darkness* (3 July 2001), which Martin counts as the 21st album of a 30-year career. Leven says that as a schoolboy in Glenrothes he won the Scottish Round Table essay competition (topic: the career he wanted – he wanted to travel the world with a guitar), shortly before becoming the first pupil in the country to be expelled from school for drug possession. There follow the LSD years, Madrid under Franco, divided Berlin, Doll by Doll as a “defeat” he still carries, the 1983 mugging with the loss of his falsetto, heroin together with his then girlfriend and, from that, the CORE Trust (funded by Shirley Porter's Westminster Council, supported by Princess Diana). Leven says Diana asked him to sing after a charity lunch – his way back into music; later he also sang for the aged Laurence Olivier. He explains “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” (a mining community with 14 churches and one pub, allegedly the highest male suicide rate in Europe, voices of laid-off shipyard workers), his studio method of withholding the other tracks from musicians, his own whisky “Leven's Lament” and a Bly men's gathering in the Highlands on the subject of grief. Overall tone: respectful, with a sense for Leven's contradictions.

2001-07-03-rolling-stone-de-creatures-of.kurz: Leven as a “hounded Iron John and king of the restless”: a calm, coherently produced album with more detached lyrics, including memories of his late father (“My Spanish Dad”, “Rainy Day Bergen Women”) and “Exit Wounds” with a quotation from Elizabeth I. Praise for the songwriting, mockery of “art poser” David Thomas…
inhalt: Leven as a “hounded Iron John and king of the restless”: a calm, coherently produced album with more detached lyrics, including memories of his late father (“My Spanish Dad”, “Rainy Day Bergen Women”) and “Exit Wounds” with a quotation from Elizabeth I. Praise for the songwriting, mockery of “art poser” David Thomas; the album only fully opens up with the booklet. Overall tone: positive.

2001-07-06-the-guardian-creatures-of-lig.kurz: Four stars: Sweeting praises the control with which Leven, on his seventh Cooking Vinyl album, shapes difficult, dark songs into a whole; behind the artful surfaces, fierce emotions rage.
inhalt: Four stars: Sweeting praises the control with which Leven, on his seventh Cooking Vinyl album, shapes difficult, dark songs into a whole; behind the artful surfaces, fierce emotions rage. Singled out are the contributions of Andy Diagram (trumpet) and David Thomas and the song title “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ”. Overall tone: “frequently awesome, and frequently terrifying”.

2001-07-11-tromso-jackie-leven-pa-tomgan.kurz: Disappointed review by a self-declared admirer: after a longer appreciation of Leven's presence and music (large parts taken verbatim from Matland's concert review of 04.03.2000), it says *Creatures of Light and Darkness* is more heavily arranged than before; the overweight instrumentation…
inhalt: Disappointed review by a self-declared admirer: after a longer appreciation of Leven's presence and music (large parts taken verbatim from Matland's concert review of 04.03.2000), it says *Creatures of Light and Darkness* is more heavily arranged than before; the overweight instrumentation slows dynamics, drive and commitment. Even the flirtation with Norwegians in “Rainy Day Bergen Women” and the idiosyncratic “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” do not save the album; if the music does not carry, the words do not catch either.

2001-07-13-tonsbergs-blad-norgesvennen-j.kurz: Short, very favourable review: Leven has lived life – as leader of the “legendary punk group” Doll by Doll, then heroin as a painkiller after a brutal mugging – but got back on his feet, fortunately for everyone who appreciates tradition-rooted British rock with good lyrics.
inhalt: Short, very favourable review: Leven has lived life – as leader of the “legendary punk group” Doll by Doll, then heroin as a painkiller after a brutal mugging – but got back on his feet, fortunately for everyone who appreciates tradition-rooted British rock with good lyrics. Over ten years he has earned the status of a “friend of Norway”, deserved through personality, integrity and credibility.

2001-07-18-hamar-dagblad-det-fins-ingen-.kurz: Leven, frontman of Doll by Doll from 1977 to 1983, has come back stronger than ever after violence and drug problems, an original artist with something on his mind.
inhalt: Leven, frontman of Doll by Doll from 1977 to 1983, has come back stronger than ever after violence and drug problems, an original artist with something on his mind. His lyrics have poetic ambitions, and he also sets other people's poetry to music (Robert Frost). The music is marked by dark sounds and demands concentration; in the complex, detailed sound picture, however, the lyrics are at times somewhat clouded.

2001-07-19-gaesteliste-das-leben-ist-ein.kurz: Interview on “Creatures of Light and Darkness” (2001). To begin with: Leven has his own whisky brand, “Leven's Lament”; he says a company called MacDuff produces it, and the label shows a Scottish and an English soldier from the last war as an image of a changing Scotland.
inhalt: Interview on “Creatures of Light and Darkness” (2001). To begin with: Leven has his own whisky brand, “Leven's Lament”; he says a company called MacDuff produces it, and the label shows a Scottish and an English soldier from the last war as an image of a changing Scotland. Maurer mentions that Leven worked in the Haig distillery in his youth. Leven describes himself as a “counterpart to the clown”: happy in private, committed to dark undertones in his work. The album's central theme is the relationship with his recently deceased father, from “My Spanish Dad” to “Bergen Girls” (with David Thomas); his father was unmusical but in old age found a way into music and into Leven's work through his enthusiasm for Spain (he learned Spanish) (his own account). Leven interprets “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” as a question of where Jesus had to take his human feelings, linked with Scottish shipyard workers. On the writing process: some songs arrive finished, others he works on for months; he only recognises an album's guiding motif afterwards, and his greatest worry is losing the ability to write. Outlook: an autumn tour, possibly with the trumpeter David Diagram.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his relationship to the clown figure.

2001-07-25-harstad-tidende-stemningsfull.kurz: Positive review: the “boss of the legendary Doll by Doll” has again delivered a solid album; in phrasing and approach he recalls Van Morrison, but loves dramatic effects (slamming doors, trickling rain, cheering).
inhalt: Positive review: the “boss of the legendary Doll by Doll” has again delivered a solid album; in phrasing and approach he recalls Van Morrison, but loves dramatic effects (slamming doors, trickling rain, cheering). He values big words and visions; “Rainy Day Bergen Women” is more familiar to Norwegians than the Jesus title. Its strength is atmosphere and closeness to the music, which demands active listening – music for life, to which one returns in the autumn dark.

2001-07-26-the-guardian-i-am-an-abject-f.kurz: Conversation over a pint at Marylebone station. Aizlewood begins with Leven's annual ritual: every spring he travels with a sleeping bag, a few books and little money to a randomly chosen country station and sets off walking to walk off his aggression.
inhalt: Conversation over a pint at Marylebone station. Aizlewood begins with Leven's annual ritual: every spring he travels with a sleeping bag, a few books and little money to a randomly chosen country station and sets off walking to walk off his aggression. Stages of the biography follow, some told this way only here: son of a carpet fitter from Fife, work in a rocket factory, married at 16, driven out of the neighbourhood by a gang at 17, farm work from Cornwall to Glasgow, in Franco's Madrid in the early 70s, where *Control* was allegedly the only thing easily obtainable. Doll by Doll (“Dull By Dull” to their detractors), the 1983 attack in Market Street in Islington with a cut across the throat, loss of his falsetto, heroin, withdrawal, the CORE Trust (discreetly supported by Princess Diana); his partner and CORE co-founder ran off with the Dalai Lama's bodyguard. Leven has since withdrawn from running the trust and lives in Hampshire with Debbie, who is teaching him “80/20” organisation. *Creatures of Light & Darkness* processes the death of his father the previous year. Leven half-amusedly calls himself “an abject failure”, rejects a crossover in the manner of David Gray, describes the rigours of long German tours and his reserve of unrecorded songs. Overall tone: sympathetic, with regret at the little recognition he has received.

2001-07-jam-creatures-of-light-and-darkn.kurz: Italian review (mark 8) with a biographical introduction (Fife, his mother's blues, *Control* as John St. Field, Doll by Doll, Charisma singles 1983, mugging, separation, heroin, return in the late 80s).
inhalt: Italian review (mark 8) with a biographical introduction (Fife, his mother's blues, *Control* as John St. Field, Doll by Doll, Charisma singles 1983, mugging, separation, heroin, return in the late 80s). Guaitamacchi goes through the album track by track, names “Exit Wound” as the only weaker song and “The Sexual Loneliness Of Jesus Christ” as the best; he mentions that the Italian label S4 translated the lyrics of this song into Italian, and praises the Frost setting and “Billy Ate My Pocket”. Conclusion: ten masterly songs in a simple, elegant sound setting.

2001-08-11-drammens-tidende-jackie-leven.kurz: Conversation before the 2001 Norway tour (last updated online in 2010). Leven says his youth was marked by trouble in a rough environment, which is why he left Scotland; Bergen was the first city outside Britain in which he lived, and a photo from his young Bergen days hangs at his mother's.
inhalt: Conversation before the 2001 Norway tour (last updated online in 2010). Leven says his youth was marked by trouble in a rough environment, which is why he left Scotland; Bergen was the first city outside Britain in which he lived, and a photo from his young Bergen days hangs at his mother's. “Rainy Day Bergen Women” came about after a night of heavy drinking, on the morning walk to the fish market. On his whisky “Leven's Lament” he says that after a serious whisky illness in Paris he no longer drinks it – a dangerous drink.

Andreassen describes the music as “white Scottish soul”; *The Mystery of Love* brought him Norwegian fans and tours as far as Australia. Leven would like to record Tim Hardin songs but shies away from the time it would take from his own pieces. He talks about working with David Thomas (Pere Ubu) on the new album and the duo Ubudoll, who last played in Oslo; he considers another Ubudoll album unlikely. He is now becoming a little well known even in Scotland.

2001-08-21-glamdalen-opphengt-i-det-bla.kurz: Mixed review: after his comeback Leven discharged ten years of pent-up writing in albums, singles and EPs, somewhere between Van Morrison and a “Celtic Henry Rollins”.
inhalt: Mixed review: after his comeback Leven discharged ten years of pent-up writing in albums, singles and EPs, somewhere between Van Morrison and a “Celtic Henry Rollins”. On *Creatures* his old Doll by Doll comrade Jo Shaw plays guitar and David Thomas takes part. The “Caledonian Soul” sounds familiar, but the musical engine begins to grind a little; Leven at times loses himself in big thoughts and forgets melodies that carry – “Rainy Day Bergen Women” should never have left the drawing board. By contrast, “My Spanish Dad”, “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ”, “Wrapped Up in Blue” and the jazzy “Friendship Between Men and Women” belong on any best-of. For the time being the album stands in the shadow of *Forbidden Songs* and *Fairy Tales for Hard Men*.

2001-09-04-dagbladet-na-blir-det-leven.kurz: Short interview piece at the start of the Norway tour in September 2001. The hook is not the new album but Leven's own whisky: Grønneberg presents him as probably the first artist in the world with his own whisky label.
inhalt: Short interview piece at the start of the Norway tour in September 2001. The hook is not the new album but Leven's own whisky: Grønneberg presents him as probably the first artist in the world with his own whisky label. Leven says that in winter 2001 a fan approached him in a pub, revealed himself as the director of the Islay Mist distillery and asked him to “compose” a whisky of his own. Leven stresses that he does not care what is in the bottle; what matters to him is the label: it shows the motif “The Order of Release” (a woman freeing a Scot captured after Culloden). Leven interprets the picture as a depiction of female strength that humiliated Scottish men and contributed to violence against women; Scotland is far ahead in Europe for domestic violence, and the label is meant to make people think – a typical Leven interpretation, hard to verify.

On the album *Creatures of Light and Darkness* (summer 2001, according to the article his 21st studio album, praised by critics) Leven says it is exactly the record he always wanted to make; he compares his role with a fixed line-up of musicians to that of a football manager. He likes Norway because of the weather, which reminds him of Scotland, especially the rain in Bergen – hence the song title “Rainy Day Bergen Women”. The article lists the tour dates.

2001-09-05-bergensavisen-hyller-jenter-f.kurz: Preview of the concert on 06.09.2001 at Den Stundesløse, where Leven's own whisky can also be bought at the bar.
inhalt: Preview of the concert on 06.09.2001 at Den Stundesløse, where Leven's own whisky can also be bought at the bar. Leven says he loves picturesque Bergen and its women; “Rainy Day Bergen Women” was hard to write, he wanted it to take off at the end, and the lyrical song gradually became a humorous one. Being compared with Van Morrison flatters him, even if Morrison no longer achieves anything at the level of *Astral Weeks* and *Moondance*, but has one of the best voices.

Personal matters, as his own account: he is better than ever, he has come to terms with the death of his father, with whom he reconciled towards the end of his life; he lives with a woman who teaches him to live in the now, and her son. In the 80s he was addicted to heroin and completely on the floor. Writing is often therapy for him; his songs are more descriptive than sentimental. He sees his soul as influenced by black masters such as Lightnin' Hopkins, Blind Lemon Jefferson and R. L. Burnside – the latter making his best records at over 70. For the concert the venue is launching “Leven's Lament”; the album received the top rating of 6 in BA.

2001-09-06-lofotposten-rolig-leven-traff.kurz: Review of the concert on Tuesday, 04.09.2001, at Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg in front of 110 spectators.
inhalt: Review of the concert on Tuesday, 04.09.2001, at Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg in front of 110 spectators. In T-shirt, shorts and white tennis socks Leven looked like AC/DC singer Brian Johnson but played quiet material; ballads were at the centre. The audience was spellbound by the voice and the idiosyncratic guitar playing with slaps on the body and stomping; humorous stories about things experienced and dreams went down well. Some were waiting for faster pieces; a blues towards the end woke the room. Criticism only of disruptive people at the back of the room.

2001-09-08-bergensavisen-altfor-mye-leve.kurz: Reserved to negative review of the solo concert at Den Stundesløse (night of 07.09.2001, about two hours): Leven insisted on telling very long stories from his life; many tuned out, only the closest fans stayed attentive.
inhalt: Reserved to negative review of the solo concert at Den Stundesløse (night of 07.09.2001, about two hours): Leven insisted on telling very long stories from his life; many tuned out, only the closest fans stayed attentive. As a stand-up comedian he is as unconvincing as Jonas Fjeld as Thomas Giertsen; a pity, since he is a brilliant songwriter and an assured singer. Highlights: “Rainy Day Bergen Women”, “Single Father”, “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ”. A photo caption mocks the short trousers.

2001-09-10-rogalands-avis-leven-uten-dod.kurz: Enthusiastic review of the tour finale on Saturday, 08.09.2001, at Sting Nere: two hours, 16 songs, not a minute of slack; the Scot looked like a tramp and entertained like a king.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review of the tour finale on Saturday, 08.09.2001, at Sting Nere: two hours, 16 songs, not a minute of slack; the Scot looked like a tramp and entertained like a king. The reviewer hardly knew Leven beforehand and asks why some become superstars and others remain an insider tip. Leven walked on stage in shorts, a tattered shirt and with a patched-up guitar; he gets away with swearing, sex talk and puns thanks to a disarming manner, scattered in anecdotes from Norway and Scotland, small digs at Mette-Marit and at Americans. Only four songs came from the new album. Leven promised to come back next year – only about 50 spectators were there.

2001-09-12-sarpsborg-arbeiderblad-en-man.kurz: Positive short review: Leven always has the critics on his side because he is a tradition-bearer; *Creatures* is atmospheric, tradition-inspired music that demands listening and then gives a lot back.
inhalt: Positive short review: Leven always has the critics on his side because he is a tradition-bearer; *Creatures* is atmospheric, tradition-inspired music that demands listening and then gives a lot back. He is a good storyteller, everything written with heart, performed simply and with feeling. Melodically he has been stronger; the album grows but hardly reaches *Fairy Tales for Hard Men*.

2001-09-18-grenzwellen-creatures-of-ligh.kurz: Album review in the online magazine for the radio programme “Grenzwellen” (archive paths point to radio ffn) (entry of 18.09.2001).
inhalt: Album review in the online magazine for the radio programme “Grenzwellen” (archive paths point to radio ffn) (entry of 18.09.2001). The reviewer “Ecki” summarises Leven's path (Doll by Doll, heroin, rebirth with “Mystery of Love” and seven further “invariably moving” albums), ranks him above Nick Cave as a songwriter because he manages without lachrymosity, and calls him “one of the last great storytellers of our time”. He says Leven wrote in his autograph book in 1994 that it never rains in Scotland, which is why the songs are so cheerful. The new album does not quite reach “Fairytales for Hardmen” and “Night Lilies”, but is more convincing than “Defending Ancient Springs”; its centrepiece is the almost ten-minute “Rainy Day Bergen Women” with David Thomas about the death of his father. Below the text: a photo of Leven by Uli Kniep, a link “Jackie Leven Interview” and the dates 30.10. Hamburg Schlachthof and 31.10. Kiel Räucherei.

2001-10-05-uncut-jackie-leven-borders-ox.titel: [Concert review] Jackie Leven at Borders Bookshop, Oxford Street, London

2001-10-triste-the-triste-interview-jack.kurz: Longest interview in the website archive, conducted before a concert at Jim's Cafe in Colne (Lancashire) on the tour for *Creatures of Light and Darkness*.
inhalt: Longest interview in the website archive, conducted before a concert at Jim's Cafe in Colne (Lancashire) on the tour for *Creatures of Light and Darkness*. Leven describes the Bryn Derwen studio near Bethesda on the edge of Snowdonia (sound engineer David Wrench), which feels to him like the Scottish west coast, and his way of working: intensive pre-production with demos sent several times to the musicians, so that studio time runs “like a military operation”; he always gives a safe brief but hopes for better ideas from the musicians. He calls sound collages “landscaping” and cites the producer John Sinclair (Doll by Doll days). He tells how the shipyard workers' voices in “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” came about (a tip from Michael Cosgrave over a beer in Bethesda), of “Billy Ate My Pocket” (a horse eats a note from his pocket) and of the Blackwood song after an encounter on a bridge in Regensburg. Album titles are “stalking horses”; *Defending Ancient Springs* was meant to be provocatively called “The Total Poetry of Industrial Language”. He distinguishes male “concept” from female “imagination”, sneers at Kevin Rowland, speaks openly about the death of his father (in “My Spanish Dad” and “Rainy Day Bergen Women”), praises Michael Weston King (whose next album he wants to produce at Bryn Derwen in January 2002), explains invented bars in his booklet thank-you lists (Royston Vasey) and admits to having deliberately smuggled the “Small Faeces” joke into the Cooking Vinyl newsletter. To close: merchandising is vital in Germany (up to £1000 per night), and he changed agents three times in three years in order to play away from the usual club circuit.
zitate_kontext: Leven on sound collages on his albums.

2001-11-21-irish-examiner-jackie-leven-f.kurz: Preview of Leven's Ireland tour in autumn 2001, written by Liam Carson (then at Lilliput Press, later founder of the Irish Language Literature Festival IMRAM) for the *Irish Examiner* and the *Irish News*.
inhalt: Preview of Leven's Ireland tour in autumn 2001, written by Liam Carson (then at Lilliput Press, later founder of the Irish Language Literature Festival IMRAM) for the *Irish Examiner* and the *Irish News*. The text opens with Leven's quotation from a Yeats poem about the feeling of being blessed and able to bless, and makes blessing, friendship, community and poetic tradition its leitmotif. Leven talks about Fife's coal mines, wool and paper mills in the 50s and 60s and about women washing at stone communal troughs in the snow. He describes Doll by Doll as the opposite of punk's “cartoon violence”; formerly a vision drove him, today he is interested in the dream world. He criticises a culture that wants to analyse everything – images should work on their own. He explains at length how “Call Mother A Lonely Field” came about (a winter morning on a frozen field by the Thames at Maidenhead, a sudden longing for his mother). *Defending Ancient Springs* refers to Kathleen Raine's study, *Creatures of Light and Darkness* contains “My Spanish Dad” about his late father and a setting of Robert Frost. With Bly he sees “unexpressed grief” as the root of collective evils. To close: Leven as a bard with rogue's tales, who has spent a lot of time in Cork and Kerry. Overall tone: hymnic.
zitate_kontext: Leven on the change since Doll by Doll.

2001-12-03-mescalina-creatures-of-light-.kurz: Very positive review: Leven as an “omone scozzese” with a heavy past (Doll by Doll, mugging in London, heroin, founding of the CORE Trust) who, together with David Thomas, has found a refined passion.
inhalt: Very positive review: Leven as an “omone scozzese” with a heavy past (Doll by Doll, mugging in London, heroin, founding of the CORE Trust) who, together with David Thomas, has found a refined passion. Ten ballads, archaic in effect, modern in production (choirs, mandolins, brass, violins, bells, some electronics); singled out are “Hidden World Of She”, “Rainy Day Bergen Women”, “Stopped By Woods On A Snowy Evening” (Robert Frost), “Sexual Loneliness Of Jesus Christ” and “Wrapped Up In Blue”. Comparisons with the young Van Morrison and a more rural Costello.

2001-12-17-pennyblackmusic-great-songs-f.kurz: Carter recommends the low-priced four-CD box as the best introduction to Leven's “Celtic Soul” of folk, rock and poetry.
inhalt: Carter recommends the low-priced four-CD box as the best introduction to Leven's “Celtic Soul” of folk, rock and poetry. *The Wanderer* is available regularly for the first time, supplemented by three bonus tracks (live recordings from Australia, Norway, Poland and Wales, among others); *Control* (recorded in 1971) shows a still unfinished voice – Leven himself attributes it to a phase of intensive LSD use. Singled out are the liner notes and “Working Alone / A Blessing” with the recitation of the James Wright poem.

2001-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-leven-sa.titel: [Collected finds Nasjonalbiblioteket 2001: news items, announcements, lists]

2002-01-wondrous-stories-experiencing-ja.medium: Wondrous Stories (magazine of the Classic Rock Society), no. 120; web version on rockreviews.co.uk
2002-01-wondrous-stories-experiencing-ja.kurz: Doug Anderson, an English fan, accompanied Leven through Germany for two weeks in October 2001 as merchandiser – he got the job through a call in an email group.
inhalt: Doug Anderson, an English fan, accompanied Leven through Germany for two weeks in October 2001 as merchandiser – he got the job through a call in an email group. His report for the Classic Rock Society's magazine (January 2002, “slightly altered” as a web version) first describes the daily routine of the tour: short drives anticlockwise around the country, late soundchecks, often poorly prepared equipment, up to seven hours of work per evening. At the merchandise stand the Haunted Valley CD *Deep in the Heart of Nowhere* sold best, because the audience mostly already owned the new studio album.

The second part describes the concert: Leven and Michael Cosgrave opened with “Call Mother a Lonely Field”, after which the programme varied according to mood; fixtures were “Billy Ate My Pocket”, “Jim O'Windygates” (introduced with memories of Leven's work in the Haig whisky factory) and a train story of up to ten minutes. There were no encores (“Jackie doesn't believe in them”). Shows lasted almost two hours. Anderson compares Leven to a mixture of Billy Connolly and a bass-baritone Bob Dylan. Also included are a complete setlist and the December 2001 dates. Enthusiastic fan tone.

2002-08-23-rolling-stone-forum-jackie-le.kurz: Oldest Leven thread in the forum of the German Rolling Stone, 29 posts from August 2002 to March 2024 (two pages).
inhalt: Oldest Leven thread in the forum of the German Rolling Stone, 29 posts from August 2002 to March 2024 (two pages). It begins with fans compiling their own best-ofs and assessments of the production; people discuss whether Leven would be better off staying unknown. In 2003 people are waiting for the tour with Midnight Choir and Richard Thompson presented by the magazine and for the promised Doll by Doll reissue. One user remembers a poorly attended Doll by Doll reunion concert in the mid-nineties at which Alan Bangs was said to be in the audience. The user “hasenschnitte” announces in February 2003 a new German Yahoo group on Leven and posts the March 2003 dates (Tuttlingen, Tübingen, Frankfurt, Essen, Bremen, Kiel, Singwitz, Hannover, Bielefeld). In August 2003 a concert recording on Radio Eins is discussed, in September 2005 a studio guest appearance on Radio Eins about “Elegy for Johnny Cash”, and a user recalls Leven's appearance at the Nuremberg Bardentreffen in 2001. After his death “stefane” announces the NDR Info obituary “Elegie für den Celtic Soulman” by Uli Kniep (14.01.2012) with the announcement text; “thomas-zimmer” posts his own concert review of the appearance at the Jubez in Karlsruhe in 2008 (Olivier story, “Museum of Childhood”, Roberto Duran song). Last post: a pointer to the Radio Bremen Zwei programme of 01.04.2024 with the recording from the Sendesaal Bremen of 29.03.2004.

2002-globalguest-inoffizielles-gaestebuc.medium: globalguest.com/gb/TOUT – guestbook of the fan site jackieleven.com
2002-globalguest-inoffizielles-gaestebuc.kurz: Around 60 entries. Fans thank him for the Christmas concert in Milford (December 2001, with praise for organiser Mick Nolan and the “Girls”) and for the live albums *Greetings From Milford* (“finally Main Travelled Roads on CD”) and *Barefoot Days*; people ask about Doll by Doll reissues a…
inhalt: Around 60 entries. Fans thank him for the Christmas concert in Milford (December 2001, with praise for organiser Mick Nolan and the “Girls”) and for the live albums *Greetings From Milford* (“finally Main Travelled Roads on CD”) and *Barefoot Days*; people ask about Doll by Doll reissues on CD and about Doll by Doll concerts hinted at in the Haunted Valley newsletter. The writer Liam Carson is looking for a copy of the Concrete Bulletproof Invisible record and in August asks for news. Concert reports come from Otley, Leeds, Watford, Vienna (Aera, 16.05.), Hebden Bridge, Ruthin (North Wales; some women in the audience took offence at coarse stories), Tregaron and Leicester (The Musician); a promoter from Portsmouth (City Bar) reports a poorly attended but great evening. A Norwegian mentions concerts with David Thomas in Oslo, a Japanese writes that he sent Doll by Doll poems by airmail over twenty years ago, which were printed in a magazine. The fans' complaints about a Haunted Valley membership that never got a reply begin here. In December a German fan announces a new German Yahoo group.

2002-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-leven-sa.titel: [Collected finds Nasjonalbiblioteket 2002: news items, announcements, lists]

2003-01-20-bergensavisen-cd-jackie-leven.kurz: Hymnic short review: nobody sings as poetically about trains leaving dirty industrial towns in the rain, or about the romance of backyards in Stockholm, Bergen and Amsterdam (“My Philosophy”).
inhalt: Hymnic short review: nobody sings as poetically about trains leaving dirty industrial towns in the rain, or about the romance of backyards in Stockholm, Bergen and Amsterdam (“My Philosophy”). Leven is Scotland's best-kept secret and deserves an audience on the scale of Leonard Cohen's; a future classic is “A Little Voice in Space”, and “Heroin Dealer Blues” has a lived background. Leven is doing well today, clearer than ever. Rating according to a later BA article (01.03.2003): 5 out of 6.

2003-02-03-rockol-jackie-leven-nelle-can.kurz: The Milan interview accompanies “Shining Brother Shining Sister”. Leven explains why he includes poems and reciting guests in his recordings.
inhalt: The Milan interview accompanies “Shining Brother Shining Sister”. Leven explains why he includes poems and reciting guests in his recordings. In doing so he distinguishes his song lyrics from actual poetry: in his estimation, poetry is found only in places in his songs. He combines his enthusiasm for literary language with a criticism of the rock of the time.

Leven names Fontella Bass and Feodor Chaliapin as early inspirations. He explains “Heroin Dealer Blues” as an attempt to approach Randy Newman's art. He traces the sound backdrop of “Classic Northern Diversions” to train journeys; he also links “Irresistible Romance” with observations made on the road. These are the songwriter's statements about his work, not independently verified records of how the songs came about.

Further topics are his interest in the music that taxi drivers listen to and the pub as a public place of encounter. He explicitly explains the Neruda reference of the album title against the background of the looming Iraq war and the humanity of the people living there. At the end the editors list five planned Italian concerts in March 2003. No author is named in the visible version.

2003-02-03-the-guardian-jackie-leven-kor.kurz: Enthusiastic live review from the pub stage in Otley. Simpson summarises Leven's life story as he tells it (Doll by Doll, knife attack, heroin, founding of a support centre for addicts) and describes a “big, beautifully damaged” troubadour who alternates between vodka and lager.
inhalt: Enthusiastic live review from the pub stage in Otley. Simpson summarises Leven's life story as he tells it (Doll by Doll, knife attack, heroin, founding of a support centre for addicts) and describes a “big, beautifully damaged” troubadour who alternates between vodka and lager. Only about a third of the evening consists of songs (including “Heroin Dealer Blues”, “Three O'Clock Men”, “Dust Elegy” from the new album), the rest of funny and abysmal stories. Comparison: a cocktail of Van Morrison, Nick Drake and Irvine Welsh.

2003-02-06-gaesteliste-der-tod-der-traeu.kurz: Long interview on “Shining Brother Shining Sister” (2003). Leven explains the choice of guests who recite poems: David Thomas reads Rilke, Ron Sexsmith a poem by E. E. Cummings at the end of “My Philosophy”; you have to be careful about who you give which text to.
inhalt: Long interview on “Shining Brother Shining Sister” (2003). Leven explains the choice of guests who recite poems: David Thomas reads Rilke, Ron Sexsmith a poem by E. E. Cummings at the end of “My Philosophy”; you have to be careful about who you give which text to. Former Doll by Doll colleagues also appear on the album. He speaks at length about “Savannah Waltz”, which is based on a series of powerful, “cinematic” dreams of an old, dignified woman waiting for a male angel; the dream world is, for the West, a lost world (his own account). Of the dealer Dusty in “Heroin Dealer Blues” he says he does not choose the characters, they find him; society passes responsibility down the line. Good creativity has a healing quality (example Chet Baker), but nobody buys CDs for that. “My Philosophy” is about the time when his life was falling apart: he holed up with newspapers in the Marylebone underground station until two friendly policemen asked if everything was all right; he replied that he was working on his philosophy – the sign to carry on (his own account). Also: praise of clichés and Euro-pop (“the music in the lifts”), production of Michael Weston King's album, announcement of the tour with Richard Thompson and Midnight Choir, accompanied by “Michael Cosgrove” [sic].
zitate_kontext: Leven on the dream behind “Savannah Waltz”.

2003-02-11-dagsavisen-gamle-helter.kurz: Joint review of the new Cooking Vinyl albums by Richard Thompson (*The Old Kit Bag*) and Leven: both have made so many brilliant records that more of the same becomes a bit much, even if each is more than good in itself.
inhalt: Joint review of the new Cooking Vinyl albums by Richard Thompson (*The Old Kit Bag*) and Leven: both have made so many brilliant records that more of the same becomes a bit much, even if each is more than good in itself. Leven writes ambitious poetry about the big questions of life by a tried-and-tested formula, often grandly arranged for a man who mostly performs alone with a guitar. Criticised is the courting of his international audience with city-name lines (Hamburg, Oslo, Bergen, Milan), which does not reach his usual lyrical level. The album is exemplary in execution, but Leven, like Thompson, is beginning to repeat himself.

2003-02-12-sarpsborg-arbeiderblad-en-bed.kurz: Positive review: Leven is one of those musicians without a commercial spotlight, however solidly they work; Van Morrison fans must be satisfied, except that Leven draws on Scottish rather than Irish tradition.
inhalt: Positive review: Leven is one of those musicians without a commercial spotlight, however solidly they work; Van Morrison fans must be satisfied, except that Leven draws on Scottish rather than Irish tradition. On the new album he is brighter and lighter in mood and varies his expression more than before, when he was inclined to reticence and single-mindedness; the backgrounds range from the synthetic through rock to jazz. Recommendation to discover Leven now at the latest.

2003-02-19-stavanger-aftenblad-poesi-for.kurz: Review of *Shining Brother, Shining Sister* (Cooking Vinyl/VME, 66:50 min.) with guests such as David Thomas, Ron Sexsmith and Robert Bly.
inhalt: Review of *Shining Brother, Shining Sister* (Cooking Vinyl/VME, 66:50 min.) with guests such as David Thomas, Ron Sexsmith and Robert Bly. Flatøe praises the expressiveness and ballad character but criticises the length of many pieces and wishes for more discipline in cutting; he mentions a song about a drinker in Cardiff and one in which Oslo and Bergen, but not Stavanger, appear. Conclusion: benevolent, music for melancholy evenings; no rating in the text.
zitate_kontext: on the excessive length of the songs.

2003-02-23-gaesteliste-koeln-gloria-mit-.kurz: Report from the Cologne evening of the short tour with Midnight Choir and Richard Thompson, on which the three acts alternated the running order; Leven closed the evening with Michael Cosgrave on keyboards.
inhalt: Report from the Cologne evening of the short tour with Midnight Choir and Richard Thompson, on which the three acts alternated the running order; Leven closed the evening with Michael Cosgrave on keyboards. Among other things he told the stories from the Haig whisky distillery and of the London policemen behind “My Philosophy”, and stretched the songs with Cosgrave to over ten minutes in places. Overall tone: very positive, the three acts complemented each other “almost magically”.

2003-02-26-tromso-jackie-leven-leverer-i.kurz: Enthusiastic review: Leven has never made a bad album; with his 18th record for Cooking Vinyl he is in top form, perhaps better than he has been for a long time.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review: Leven has never made a bad album; with his 18th record for Cooking Vinyl he is in top form, perhaps better than he has been for a long time. The lyrics and melodies have a rare power, carried by one of the best soul voices in the business – whether the subject is drug dealing, immortal love or back yards in Stockholm and Bergen. Guests: Ron Sexsmith, David Thomas, Robert Bly. Recorded in Wales, rehearsed and prepared in California – hence both sunny and heavy with rain. Notice of the concert at Blå Rock on Sunday, 2 March.

2003-02-28-tromso-jackie-leven-pa-blaroc.kurz: Preview of the concert on Sunday, 02.03.2003, at the Blå Rock Café; the opening (acknowledgements of Tromsø bars on record sleeves) is taken over from Matland's text of 2000.
inhalt: Preview of the concert on Sunday, 02.03.2003, at the Blå Rock Café; the opening (acknowledgements of Tromsø bars on record sleeves) is taken over from Matland's text of 2000. The promoter Egon Holstad describes the difference between records and stage: the albums are in part pompous and overloaded with arrangements and guests, whereas live Leven is intimate and gripping – just him, a guitar and a miked-up floorboard; plus the wildest stories, which prompt laughter and reflection. Caption: photo from the concert of 02.03.2000.

2003-02-cooking-vinyl-pressemitteilung-s.titel: [Press release] Jackie Leven – Shining Brother Shining Sister (COOKCD250)

2003-03-01-bergensavisen-leven-gar-i-fen.kurz: Preview of two Bergen appearances: on 07.03.2003 at the small venue Madam Felle and on 08.03. (International Women's Day) at Bergen Landsfengsel.
inhalt: Preview of two Bergen appearances: on 07.03.2003 at the small venue Madam Felle and on 08.03. (International Women's Day) at Bergen Landsfengsel. Leven says he was addicted to heroin and knows what it means to be an outlaw; he is looking forward to the prison concert. The prison's leisure activities manager, Frode Trefall, calls it a big thing to have a “world name” as a guest and expects lively interest from the prisoners.

Bergen has a special place in his heart, he says; the atmosphere reminds him of Scotland, and he mentions Bergen in at least one song on every new album. On the guests on *Shining Brother Shining Sister* (David Thomas, Ron Sexsmith, Robert Bly): none of them is ordinary, all are difficult, and that is exactly what makes them exciting; Sexsmith was at first afraid of him because of his past. He says he himself worked in a London women's prison, looking after women whose children were growing up without fathers and needed male values. He understands people who prefer alcohol or drugs to television (he himself is at times addicted to television), but has no time for state intervention – one has to want to stop oneself. Today he drinks alcohol in moderation and has his own whisky, Leven's Lament. The album had received 5 out of 6 in BA.

2003-03-01-nordlys-kiltkledd-helt-tilbak.kurz: Preview of the fifth Tromsø concert on Sunday, 02.03.2003. Egon Holstad (Blå Rock) calls his friend Leven “an incredible guy”, one of the best guitarists in the world, immensely authoritative on stage, self-deprecating and ruthlessly open; Leven is coming a day early in order to walk around in the snow in his kilt…
inhalt: Preview of the fifth Tromsø concert on Sunday, 02.03.2003. Egon Holstad (Blå Rock) calls his friend Leven “an incredible guy”, one of the best guitarists in the world, immensely authoritative on stage, self-deprecating and ruthlessly open; Leven is coming a day early in order to walk around in the snow in his kilt. Leven is coming straight from a German tour with Richard Thompson and Midnight Choir and will also play Kabelvåg, Bergen and Oslo in Norway.

2003-03-06-lofotposten-ettertenksom-leve.kurz: Review of the concert on Tuesday, 04.03.2003, at the Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg before 50 people: a quiet, attentive audience; anyone who had expected the drive of the new album got a quiet, at times powerful version of soul, blues and rock “of the very best brand”.
inhalt: Review of the concert on Tuesday, 04.03.2003, at the Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg before 50 people: a quiet, attentive audience; anyone who had expected the drive of the new album got a quiet, at times powerful version of soul, blues and rock “of the very best brand”. The story of the heroin dealer's dream was both moving and funny. A freshly converted visitor has his say. Fact box: born 1950 in Fife, Doll by Doll with four albums 1978–1982, act of violence 1983.

2003-03-07-tonsbergs-blad-cd-jackie-leve.kurz: Very positive review: after years of drug problems Leven seems to be staying on the “narrow path” and is more alert than ever; his slightly alternative “pop noir” works almost perfectly.
inhalt: Very positive review: after years of drug problems Leven seems to be staying on the “narrow path” and is more alert than ever; his slightly alternative “pop noir” works almost perfectly. He recalls Lou Reed a little, but offers more intensity and magic; the creative production is full of surprises, and the lyrics range from tender love to black everyday realism to bizarre humour.

2003-03-09-bergensavisen-leven-bak-muren.kurz: Report on Leven's hour-long concert on 08.03.2003 in the sports hall of Bergen prison, guarded by around ten officers; the night before he had played at Madam Felle.
inhalt: Report on Leven's hour-long concert on 08.03.2003 in the sports hall of Bergen prison, guarded by around ten officers; the night before he had played at Madam Felle. Leven jokes that he could just as well have been sitting in a bar. Between songs he talked about his time as a heroin addict; inmates recognised themselves, and one praises the message that one can get free of intoxication and prison. According to the paper, Leven served several spells in British prisons as a young man in the 1960s. In the second half of the concert the tempo picked up.

2003-05-08-pennyblackmusic-shining-broth.kurz: Carter considers the album Leven's strongest since *Night Lilies* (1998), perhaps his best ever: *Defending Ancient Springs* and *Creatures of Light and Darkness* had contained only scattered classics.
inhalt: Carter considers the album Leven's strongest since *Night Lilies* (1998), perhaps his best ever: *Defending Ancient Springs* and *Creatures of Light and Darkness* had contained only scattered classics. He singles out “My Philosophy”, “Another Man in the Old Arcade” (one of the best Leven songs), and the almost ten-minute “A Little Voice in Space” with a Mandelstam poem and David Thomas's reading of Rilke; the trumpet elegy before “Savannah Waltz” is played by the film composer Geoffrey Burgon. Praise too for Leven's liner notes and Deborah Greenwood's backing vocals.

2003-11-05-kanaliena-gr-jackie-leven-int.medium: Kanaliena.gr / programme “Rockzone” (recording on YouTube, channel Dimitris Antonopoulos)
2003-11-05-kanaliena-gr-jackie-leven-int.kurz: A good five-minute edit of a conversation which, according to the on-screen caption, the Greek presenter Dimitris Antonopoulos conducted on 5 November 2003 for Kanaliena.gr or his programme “Rockzone”; the questions have been cut out, leaving only Leven's answers.
inhalt: A good five-minute edit of a conversation which, according to the on-screen caption, the Greek presenter Dimitris Antonopoulos conducted on 5 November 2003 for Kanaliena.gr or his programme “Rockzone”; the questions have been cut out, leaving only Leven's answers. The caption lists as topics Peter Hammill, Van Morrison, “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” and concerts. Leven says that anyone who wants to become a singer takes on responsibility: one's own voice speaks for others, for love, hatred and anger – Hammill understands this particularly well. He admires Van Morrison for his early work but finds the last ten years monotonous; he himself wants to carry on the tradition that Van embodied at his peak, and thinks that Michael Cosgrave does the same. He wrote “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” on the Greek island of Astypalaia, alone on a hot day, thinking of a Jesus with human fears. He will stop when there are no good songs left in him; the tour through Germany, Spain, Britain and now Greece is tiring but lovely. Advice to young musicians: do not look to fame, but be artistically satisfied with yourself. Overall tone: a short, reflective promotional conversation during the trip to Greece with Cosgrave and Michael Weston King.

2003-canongate-strong-great-indie-discog.titel: The Great Indie Discography (2nd ed.; 1st ed. 1999 as The Great Alternative & Indie Discography) – entry “Doll By Doll” with Jackie Leven

2003-globalguest-inoffizielles-gaestebuc.medium: globalguest.com/gb/TOUT – guestbook of the fan site jackieleven.com
2003-globalguest-inoffizielles-gaestebuc.kurz: With well over 90 entries, 2003 is the strongest year of this guestbook. It accompanies *Shining Brother Shining Sister* (February 2003), which fans from Cornwall, France (a record dealer who wants to sell 200 copies), Kiel, Asker and Hamm (Radio Runde Hamm: “CD of the month”) celebrate; the radio DJ…
inhalt: With well over 90 entries, 2003 is the strongest year of this guestbook. It accompanies *Shining Brother Shining Sister* (February 2003), which fans from Cornwall, France (a record dealer who wants to sell 200 copies), Kiel, Asker and Hamm (Radio Runde Hamm: “CD of the month”) celebrate; the radio DJ Ecki Stieg writes that the album almost saved his life. The February/March tour with Richard Thompson and Midnight Choir can be followed place by place: Haarlem (19.02., with Michael Cosgrave), Hamburg St. Pauli-Theater (20.02.), Berlin (21.02.), Vienna (25.02.), Oslo John Dee (06.03.), then a German tour whose dates a fan posts (Tuttlingen, Tübingen, Frankfurt, Essen, Bremen, Kiel, Singwitz, Hannover, Bielefeld), with an argument over whether Kiel took place at the Halle 400 or the Räucherei. A host in Tübingen recalls conversations about Rilke and Blake. Further traces: Bein Inn (Fife, January), Penzance, Flowerpot Derby, Førde (Norway, June), Edinburgh Fringe (August), New Roscoe Leeds, Midlands Arts Centre as support for Cara Dillon (July), a US thank-you for Leven's contribution to the Frankie Miller tribute.

Many entries revolve around Doll by Doll: one fan saw them in 1979/80 “blowing Devo off the stage”, a musician from Leeds played support in the Clifton Villas era and saw Jo Shaw smash his Stratocaster, a pedal steel player lived with Vincent Crane in Warwick Avenue in the 1970s, and people keep asking about CD editions of the Doll by Doll albums, until someone mentions CD-R bootlegs. Fans praise the monthly columns and wish for them as a book. At the end of the year a buyer complains that his cheque has been cashed but the CD has not arrived – a foretaste of the problems of 2008.

2004-01-05-kindamuzik-for-peace-comes-dr.kurz: Enthusiastic review of the regular reissue of the live album from London's Twelve Bar Club, which in 1996 had appeared only in a small edition for fan club members.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review of the regular reissue of the live album from London's Twelve Bar Club, which in 1996 had appeared only in a small edition for fan club members. Praised are the setlist, the cover versions (“Slim Slow Slider”, “Pale Blue Eyes” – in the booklet “Pale Blues Eyes”) and the three narrative pieces between the songs (“Acid Roast Beef”, “Whisky Story”, “Jackie Losing It”). Reference to Leven's Crossing Border appearance shortly beforehand. Overall tone: very positive, “superieure live-plaat”.

2004-01-24-rolling-stone-forum-jackie-le.kurz: Short thread (7 posts, Jan./Feb. 2004) with the dates of the spring 2004 tour (24.03. Bonn Harmonie to 03.04. Vienna Chelsea, including Hamburg Knust, Kiel Räucherei, Northeim, Hannover, Frankfurt Sinkkasten, Munich Muffatcafé, Berlin Quasimodo, Dresden Starclub) and mixed memories of concerts:…
inhalt: Short thread (7 posts, Jan./Feb. 2004) with the dates of the spring 2004 tour (24.03. Bonn Harmonie to 03.04. Vienna Chelsea, including Hamburg Knust, Kiel Räucherei, Northeim, Hannover, Frankfurt Sinkkasten, Munich Muffatcafé, Berlin Quasimodo, Dresden Starclub) and mixed memories of concerts: one user found a concert disappointing, others entertaining; one recalls a Doll by Doll reunion concert at the Hamburg Fabrik in front of about 15 paying customers. Notice of Michael Weston King & The Decent Men feat. Jackie Leven on 29.05.2004 at the Berlin Knaack.

2004-01-26-gaesteliste-for-peace-comes-d.kurz: Review of the Cooking Vinyl reissue of the earlier Haunted Valley live album. Maurer recommends it as “the calling card of Leven the performer”: relaxed, different versions of his own songs, a few cover versions (blues, Lou Reed, Van Morrison) and above all the funny stories between the songs.
inhalt: Review of the Cooking Vinyl reissue of the earlier Haunted Valley live album. Maurer recommends it as “the calling card of Leven the performer”: relaxed, different versions of his own songs, a few cover versions (blues, Lou Reed, Van Morrison) and above all the funny stories between the songs. Overall tone: positive, especially for fans who missed the concert CD.

2004-01-27-celtic-connections-pressemitt.titel: [Press release] Ian Rankin and Jackie Leven present 'Jackie Leven Said'

2004-01-30-bbc-folk-awards-2004-folk-clu.titel: Jackie Leven 2004 Live or Die [recording; presentation of “Folk Club of the Year” for the BBC Folk Awards]

2004-02-17-drammens-tidende-herlig-uform.kurz: Enthusiastic review of the Cooking Vinyl edition of the solo live album *For Peace Comes Dropping Slow*: a gloriously relaxed concert recording, just Leven, acoustic guitar and foot rhythm on the guitar case.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review of the Cooking Vinyl edition of the solo live album *For Peace Comes Dropping Slow*: a gloriously relaxed concert recording, just Leven, acoustic guitar and foot rhythm on the guitar case. Originally released in 1996, but never regularly, presumably sold only through the fan club. It contains many of his best songs since the comeback, such as “Call Mother a Lonely Field”, and monologues – one about “Arctic sex” after a Norway tour in Tromsø. Leven had recently toured Germany with Midnight Choir; for the reviewer he is one of the greatest living artists.

2004-03-02-mescalina-shining-brother-shi.kurz: A belated review which explicitly does not consider the album a masterpiece, but an open, many-voiced mosaic: guest names and text sources from Robert Bly, Rilke, Ron Sexsmith, Cummings, David Thomas, Sitwell, Neruda, Mandelstam and Ciaran Carson.
inhalt: A belated review which explicitly does not consider the album a masterpiece, but an open, many-voiced mosaic: guest names and text sources from Robert Bly, Rilke, Ron Sexsmith, Cummings, David Thomas, Sitwell, Neruda, Mandelstam and Ciaran Carson. Discussed are “Classic Northern Diversions”, “Irresistible Romance”, “My Philosophy”, “Dust Elegy”/“Savannah Waltz”, “A Little Voice In Space”, “Heroin Dealer Blues” and “1798”. Overall tone: positive, “disco necessario”.

2004-03-15-rolling-stone-forum-jackie-le.kurz: Long rating thread (83 posts, 2004–2020, six pages) in which forum users rate Leven albums with stars.
inhalt: Long rating thread (83 posts, 2004–2020, six pages) in which forum users rate Leven albums with stars. Consensus: “The Mystery of Love” and “Forbidden Songs of the Dying West” are regarded as masterpieces (up to five stars, places in personal top-500 lists); “Fairy Tales for Hard Men” falls slightly short for many, while later albums such as “Defending Ancient Springs” and “Shining Brother Shining Sister” are defended by individuals. One user reports that in 1995, on holiday in Oban, he narrowly missed a Leven concert. In November 2011 there are condolences; one user had wanted to go to the (cancelled) Münster concert, another points to a DLF feature, “Ein großer Unbekannter”, on 19.11.2011.

2004-03-26-wdr-rockpalast-crossroads-jac.kurz: Television recording by WDR at the Rockpalast festival “Crossroads” at the Bonn Harmonie (23–26 March 2004); Leven played on the last evening, 26 March 2004, with Kevin Foster (bass) and Michael Cosgrave (keyboards, vocals).
inhalt: Television recording by WDR at the Rockpalast festival “Crossroads” at the Bonn Harmonie (23–26 March 2004); Leven played on the last evening, 26 March 2004, with Kevin Foster (bass) and Michael Cosgrave (keyboards, vocals). The WDR page lists the setlist A Little Voice in Space, Classic Northern Diversions, Live or Die, Poortoun, My Philosophy, Call Mother a Lonely Field, Empty in Soho Square, Exit Wound and introduces Leven with a press text (“perhaps the greatest Scottish singer/songwriter”, a Stereoplay quotation). In 2018 the Rockpalast channel published a 44-minute version with four songs and three short interview segments (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pcJw_Zjf94); in 2024 MIG Music put the whole concert (around 75 minutes, with narrative passages such as “Jackie Talks About Kiel And His Mother” and “… Norwegian Prisoners”) online (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R4VYTXQUQFI). The material was released as the DVD “Live at Rockpalast” (2011) and as the CD+DVD “Live at Rockpalast 2004” (2024).

inhalt: Three days after the Bonn Rockpalast appearance, Leven played with Michael Cosgrave in the Sendesaal of Radio Bremen; the recording was released in 2024 as CD 3–4 of “Live Or Die – Live In Bremen 1999 & 2004” (including Single Father, My Philosophy, Fly, Empty in Soho Square, A Little Voice in Space, Classic Northern Diversions, Little Brown Box, Poortoun, narrative passages such as “Butterfly”). Leven's column mentions the “radio recording in Bremen” of the tour “Forty Years Of Missed Hotel Breakfasts”.

2004-04-the-word-ian-rankin-and-jackie-l.kurz: Report and conversation on the evening “Twa Twisted Fifers” at the Celtic Connections festival in Glasgow (January 2004), at which Ian Rankin read his new short story “Jackie Leven Said” and Leven sang songs at suitable points, accompanied by Michael Cosgrave on keyboards.
inhalt: Report and conversation on the evening “Twa Twisted Fifers” at the Celtic Connections festival in Glasgow (January 2004), at which Ian Rankin read his new short story “Jackie Leven Said” and Leven sang songs at suitable points, accompanied by Michael Cosgrave on keyboards. Du Noyer describes the story (two brothers from Fife, one of whom becomes a pop producer in London) and sketches Leven's life story: John St Field (Leven: trouble with the law), Doll by Doll, the attack and addiction, the solo albums. Leven mentions 130 concerts a year (previously 200). Rankin explains that Rebus would like Leven's music because they are stories about disappointed hard men; Leven announces “The Haunting Of John Rebus”. The two talk about emotional reticence in Fife, about pubs as an outlet, about a “Celtic” view of the world (Leven: reality lies in the in-between, for instance between tree and bark) and about the differences between Glasgow and Edinburgh. Rankin thinks Leven's life would make a great book. Songs sung include “Man Bleeds In Glasgow” and “Gylen Gylen”.

2004-05-28-gaesteliste-orange-blossom-sp.kurz: Festival report from the Glitterhouse festival Orange Blossom Special. On Saturday (29.05.2004) Leven and Michael Cosgrave opened with quiet, elegiac ballads and stories, including “Single Father”; afterwards Leven played lead guitar in Michael Weston King's new band The Decent Men, with Cosgra…
inhalt: Festival report from the Glitterhouse festival Orange Blossom Special. On Saturday (29.05.2004) Leven and Michael Cosgrave opened with quiet, elegiac ballads and stories, including “Single Father”; afterwards Leven played lead guitar in Michael Weston King's new band The Decent Men, with Cosgrave also on trumpet there. A fan is quoted on how astonishingly gently the “huge man” played; backstage the whisky level had dropped rapidly. Overall tone: very positive, MWK's set with Leven “the first highlight of the festival”.

2004-11-15-gaesteliste-the-meeting-of-re.kurz: Review of the DVD from the Crossing Border Festival in The Hague (2003) with Leven, Michael Cosgrave, David Thomas, Ian Rankin and Ciaran Carson plus four interviews.
inhalt: Review of the DVD from the Crossing Border Festival in The Hague (2003) with Leven, Michael Cosgrave, David Thomas, Ian Rankin and Ciaran Carson plus four interviews. Maurer warns that this is not a “proper” Leven DVD but a peculiar mixed performance in amateurish picture quality, more for specialists; a complete concert would have made more sense. Overall tone: reserved, with mockery of Leven's shirt with a hole on the shoulder.

2004-11-23-kindamuzik-jackie-leven-blijf.kurz: Backstage conversation at the Crossing Border festival in The Hague, held on a Friday afternoon (from the context, 12.11.2004, Leven's second Crossing Border appearance), published on 23.11.2004. Dielemans describes a subdued mood: Leven drinks canned beer, stares at the just-released …
inhalt: Backstage conversation at the Crossing Border festival in The Hague, held on a Friday afternoon (from the context, 12.11.2004, Leven's second Crossing Border appearance), published on 23.11.2004. Dielemans describes a subdued mood: Leven drinks canned beer, stares at the just-released DVD “The Meeting Of Remarkable Men” and lost his mother a few days earlier. The author summarises the biography (Control 1971, Doll by Doll from 1976, attack in a London alley, heroin addiction, comeback in 1994 with the albums up to “Creatures of Light and Darkness”).

Leven says that for “Control” he took a lot of LSD, like everyone at the time; because of trouble with the police the record came out under another name and only in Spain, and he forgot about it for a long time. He describes the 2003 Crossing Border evening at the Koninklijke Schouwburg with Ian Rankin, Ciaran Carson and David Thomas in detail: an invitation from the organiser Louise Behre, no rehearsal, Rankin and Thomas had been on a bender the night before, he himself was very nervous; a scene captured on the DVD in which Thomas urges him to hurry and then apologises. As follow-up projects he mentions an appearance with Rankin and James Yorkston at Celtic Connections, an evening in Fife with an English author, a new album to be recorded in Beirut with a large “gypsy orchestra” and released in summer 2005, and the double CD “Jackie Leven Said” for January. In closing: in the Netherlands he hardly sells any records, but he feels at home in The Hague (narrow streets, dark pubs, rain like in Glasgow) and wants to keep trying. Overall tone: a warm, slightly melancholy portrait.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his attitude to touring.
on the unprepared Crossing Border show in 2003.

2004-globalguest-inoffizielles-gaestebuc.kurz: Around 50 entries up to early 2005. One fan was at the evening with Ian Rankin in January 2004 and once saw Doll by Doll as the support act for John Otway and Hawkwind.
inhalt: Around 50 entries up to early 2005. One fan was at the evening with Ian Rankin in January 2004 and once saw Doll by Doll as the support act for John Otway and Hawkwind. The AllMusic critic Thom Jurek asks in January for review copies, as Leven's records are hardly available in the USA. In March 2004, in response to an appeal from Leven, around ten fans apply to be merchandise sellers for the German tour. Concert greetings come from Brighton (The Greys, with David Thomas), Botley, Kiel (together with Tony Joe White, 24.03.), Munich, Cologne, Berlin, Frankfurt, Dresden, Essen (with Michael Weston King), Moers (festival with David Thomas), Leicester (with Dan Britton) and Glastonbury (with Michael Weston King's band). On 04.04.2004 Robin Spreafico, a former Doll by Doll member, gets in touch from Indonesia and asks how he can reach Leven. One fan points out the reissue of *For Peace Comes Dropping Slow*, another complains that the news page has not been updated for a year. There are birthday wishes on 18.06. (a “midsummer party” is mentioned). The last recorded entry (13.01.2005) asks about the dates of the tour with The Earlies and a concert at the Morden Tower, Newcastle.

inhalt: 122-minute concert film by the Dutch director Paul Hegeman, recorded at the Crossing Border Festival in The Hague in November 2003 (on 14.11.2003, according to Leven's column). On stage Leven meets, largely in improvisation, David Thomas (Pere Ubu), Ian Rankin and the poet Ciaran Carson, accompanied by Michael Cosgrave. IMDb lists Cooking Vinyl and Paul Hegeman Productions as production companies and 31 January 2005 as the British release date (IMDb year 2004).

2005-04-26-drammens-tidende-jackie-leven.kurz: Preview with a telephone interview (“vel hjemme i England”) ahead of Leven's appearance closing the 2005 Working Class Hero festival in Drammen on Sunday, 1 May – according to the paper his first concert there in two years.
inhalt: Preview with a telephone interview (“vel hjemme i England”) ahead of Leven's appearance closing the 2005 Working Class Hero festival in Drammen on Sunday, 1 May – according to the paper his first concert there in two years. Andreassen introduces Leven as the former frontman of Doll by Doll, whose voice Q had counted among the greatest British voices; the solo albums since 1994 are first-rate without having made him widely known. Åge Aleksandersen is named as a prominent fan.

Leven says (self-report) that he has just come back from Beirut, where he recorded new songs with Lebanese and Greek musicians – it still sounds like a Western Jackie Leven record, but it is the most exciting thing he has done. He does not measure success in sales: he knows many successful musicians, but none of them gets to travel to Tromsø. At length he repeats the Diana anecdote: after the attack (in the paper “1982”, “mugged and stabbed”) he worked for years with addicts and met Princess Diana in the course of it; her “Why don't you sing something” was perhaps the most important moment of his life, and he did not dare to sing again for over ten years.

On the festival's name, Leven says he is himself a “working class man”; in England a festival would not call itself that, because under Tony Blair people want to forget their industrial roots. Andreassen closes by noting that Leven's concerts are never boring – he has seen “quite a few”.
zitate_kontext: Leven on more successful fellow musicians.

2005-04-30-dagsavisen-leven-i-litteratur.kurz: Major interview on the double album *Jackie Leven Said* with Ian Rankin, shortly before Leven's next visit to Norway.
inhalt: Major interview on the double album *Jackie Leven Said* with Ian Rankin, shortly before Leven's next visit to Norway. Rakvaag stresses that the collaboration began, in a way, in Norway: according to the booklet, Leven discovered on a flight from Bergen to Tromsø that he appears in Rankin's novel *Resurrection Man* (in the paper “Ressurection Man”, Norw. “Botsgang”) as Inspector John Rebus's favourite singer. Leven confirms this (self-report): he was reading it over a few drinks before a difficult landing. Norway is for him the “extreme version of Scotland”; he has played here since 1966, then as guitarist of the blues singer Doris Henderson – his first trip abroad as a professional musician.

Rankin and Leven then exchanged emails and worked out a joint stage show for festivals in Glasgow and Edinburgh in 2004. Rankin's story is about a musician who travels from London to Fife for his mother's funeral. Leven describes the shared theme: men whose lives are becoming blurred and whose inner lives are a mystery to them. He sings old songs that inspired Rankin, and three new ones, including “The Haunting of John Rebus”; the rest of the double album is a retrospective chosen jointly. The title alludes to Van Morrison's “Jackie Wilson Said”; a character quotes “My Spanish Dad”.

On drinking, Leven says he has not been addicted to heroin for 20 years and does not want to go on appearing as an ex-junkie for ever; he believes in good company when drinking, but also spends a lot of time at home sober. He loves the melancholy of travelling alone; as a young man he won a national writing competition with a travel story. Outlook: solo at the Working Class Hero festival in Drammen on 1 May, a week later with David Thomas (Pere Ubu) as UbuDoll at Bergenfest. Fact boxes on Leven (including: the Doll by Doll albums soon to appear on CD for the first time, next album recorded in Beirut with Greek and Lebanese musicians) and on Rankin.

2005-05-02-gaesteliste-jackie-leven-said.kurz: Review of the double CD on which Ian Rankin reads his short story “Jackie Leven Said” and Leven, with Michael Cosgrave, illustrates it musically, supplemented by jointly chosen songs (including Bacharach's “Say A Little Prayer”).
inhalt: Review of the double CD on which Ian Rankin reads his short story “Jackie Leven Said” and Leven, with Michael Cosgrave, illustrates it musically, supplemented by jointly chosen songs (including Bacharach's “Say A Little Prayer”). Verdict: only for “hardcore fans”. Maurer reports that James Yorkston told him Leven had already phoned him as a fellow Fifer.

2005-05-04-bergensavisen-bombedrama-beir.kurz: BA meets the “Bergensvenn” Leven at the start of a six-day stay in Bergen. Leven says (self-report) that a few months ago he was sitting in a street café in Beirut when, two blocks away, the car bomb exploded that killed the former prime minister Rafik al-Hariri; he w…
inhalt: BA meets the “Bergensvenn” Leven at the start of a six-day stay in Bergen. Leven says (self-report) that a few months ago he was sitting in a street café in Beirut when, two blocks away, the car bomb exploded that killed the former prime minister Rafik al-Hariri; he had been there to record his forthcoming record with local and Greek musicians. He was terrified for his life and refuses to go back for cover photos.

The reason for the long stay is Bergenfest: on Friday he plays with David Thomas (Pere Ubu). Bergen is his “spiritual centre”, the festival head Frank Nes invited him for six days; he wants to relax and write. On *Jackie Leven Said* he repeats the flight anecdote (Bergen–Tromsø, Rankin's novel, Rebus as a fan); Rankin's publisher first turned the project down and then postponed its marketing by eight months. A tour is open: his mother died last year, after his father's death he buried himself in work, and now he wants to be at home with his wife and write songs.

On Doll by Doll: Warner did not care about the four albums, and now someone has finally woken up – partly thanks to the Rankin record. He rules out a live reunion, but says they have talked about a new joint studio album. Ending with “Rainy Day Bergen Woman” and a wish for rain.

2005-06-22-sarpsborg-arbeiderblad-et-sja.kurz: Friendly review of *Jackie Leven Said* (section “Opplesing/folk”). Brøndmo retells how it came about (Leven read Rankin on a plane and found himself John Rebus's favourite musician), considers the story “not Rankin at his best, but not bad either”; it is read live from Edinburgh with a few…
inhalt: Friendly review of *Jackie Leven Said* (section “Opplesing/folk”). Brøndmo retells how it came about (Leven read Rankin on a plane and found himself John Rebus's favourite musician), considers the story “not Rankin at his best, but not bad either”; it is read live from Edinburgh with a few musical interjections from Leven and Michael Cosgrave. CD 2 has three new songs, otherwise familiar material – more something for fans. Everything feels a little untidy, but charming through its humour and Scottish dialect.

2005-07-03-rolling-stone-de-short-cuts-j.kurz: Short review in Doebeling's column: a record of a “delightful tryst of two Scottish art eccentrics” in Edinburgh – Rankin's reading of the short story about a record producer, interludes by Leven and Cosgrave, a “preposterous” discussion about the Kingdom of Fife, new songs.
inhalt: Short review in Doebeling's column: a record of a “delightful tryst of two Scottish art eccentrics” in Edinburgh – Rankin's reading of the short story about a record producer, interludes by Leven and Cosgrave, a “preposterous” discussion about the Kingdom of Fife, new songs. Rating: 3.0 (out of 5).

inhalt: Positive review: like many people, Leven came to Cash only through the “American Recordings”; two songs are dedicated directly to Cash (the title track as an imagined last vocal recording by Cash, “The Law of Tide” sung by Robert Fisher). Praised are “Blue Soul Dark Road”, “No Honour In This Love”, “Vibration White Finger” and “King of the Barley” about the lonely drinkers at the bar.

2005-09-06-dagsavisen-i-johnny-cashs-fot.kurz: Very positive review: the album breathes love for Cash and for the country-rock/Americana tradition, paired with “honest and austere Scottish lyricism”.
inhalt: Very positive review: the album breathes love for Cash and for the country-rock/Americana tradition, paired with “honest and austere Scottish lyricism”. Recorded in Beirut but with a Memphis feel; the title song is a gesture of thanks to Cash's producer Rick Rubin. As a poet Leven is more refined than Cash; the album shows a warm, still more melancholy side and sounds like a geographical round trip (Lebanon, Greece, USA, Northern Ireland, Wales, England) – neither a covers album nor a “world” record. Rating according to Dagsavisen of 23.09.2005: five (out of six).
zitate_kontext: on the album for Cash and Leven fans.

2005-09-09-the-independent-album-jackie-.kurz: Gill appreciates Leven's portraits of men. The love songs convince him less.
inhalt: Gill appreciates Leven's portraits of men. The love songs convince him less.

2005-09-13-drammens-tidende-gjennombrudd.kurz: Enthusiastic review, noting the Union Scene concert with the Small World Orchestra and Eivind Kløverød: *Elegy for Johnny Cash* is meant to be Leven's definitive breakthrough in Norway, comparable with Cohen and Van Morrison as “friends of Norway”.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review, noting the Union Scene concert with the Small World Orchestra and Eivind Kløverød: *Elegy for Johnny Cash* is meant to be Leven's definitive breakthrough in Norway, comparable with Cohen and Van Morrison as “friends of Norway”. Praised are the mixture of Scottish white soul, Celtic folk tradition and pop, and the sombre “The Law of Tide”, on which Robert Fisher (Willard Grant Conspiracy) sings and conjures up Cash's spirit; opener “Blue Soul Dark Road”. Objections: programmed drums, a few anonymous songs – nevertheless, for the critic, one of the greatest albums of the year. In the DT year-end list (27.12.2005) it came 9th.

2005-09-15-halden-arbeiderblad-leven-pa-.kurz: Preview of the concert at the pub Siste Reis in Halden on Sunday, 25.09.2005. The promoter is Tom Skjeklesæther of Halden, who ran the rock club Ratz in Oslo in the early 1980s: Doll by Doll was the first band to play there.
inhalt: Preview of the concert at the pub Siste Reis in Halden on Sunday, 25.09.2005. The promoter is Tom Skjeklesæther of Halden, who ran the rock club Ratz in Oslo in the early 1980s: Doll by Doll was the first band to play there. Biographical outline (Roma family, Irish father, northern English mother, youth in Scotland, London/Berlin/Madrid, attack, addiction, since 1985 CORE, support from Princess Diana and Eric Clapton, “fifteen solo albums”). Skjeklesæther places Leven between Van Morrison and Mike Scott (Waterboys) and stresses that he prefers to play in small, intimate venues.

2005-09-19-mescalina-jackie-leven-said.kurz: Review of the double CD with Ian Rankin (recording from the Queen's Hall, Edinburgh, August 2004, plus three new songs and older material).
inhalt: Review of the double CD with Ian Rankin (recording from the Queen's Hall, Edinburgh, August 2004, plus three new songs and older material). Verzeletti explains how it came about (Leven found his name in a Rankin text, both come from Fife), finds the reading on CD hard going for non-native speakers and the live songs too long; the three new songs, written from Rebus's point of view, above all “Linseed Oil” about the smell of linseed oil in Kirkcaldy, are the best part. Overall tone: more for fans.

2005-09-26-drammens-tidende-naervaer-av-.kurz: Review of the opening concert of the Union Scene (Sat 24.09.2005, 10 pm, about 250 listeners) with Leven and his now four-piece band.
inhalt: Review of the opening concert of the Union Scene (Sat 24.09.2005, 10 pm, about 250 listeners) with Leven and his now four-piece band. Gundersen is disappointed by the band sound: synthetic synthesizer sounds and a booming bass did not suit Leven's music; the best sound came from the Drammen percussionist Eivind Kløverød (in the paper “Kløverud”), whose playing ideally complemented Leven's rhythmic guitar, including a percussion duel. Leven himself is a “big man” with a big voice, presence and coarse, humorous announcements, a poet and master guitarist with great stylistic range. Further back in the hall the audience's chatter was disruptive; Leven needs intense closeness, a listening audience and sparse instrumentation.
