2005-09-27-rogalands-avis-enigmatisk.kurz: Short, positive review looking forward to Leven's concert at Checkpoint (Stavanger) “in just under a month”: even odd production decisions cannot spoil Leven's classic songwriting.
inhalt: Short, positive review looking forward to Leven's concert at Checkpoint (Stavanger) “in just under a month”: even odd production decisions cannot spoil Leven's classic songwriting. On the title song and “The Law of Tide” Leven leans closely on Cash's singing; the record, made in Lebanon, contains sounds from Near Eastern and British folk music. A great record that takes some getting used to. According to Rogalands Avis of 18.10.2005, 5 on the dice scale; running time 49:53.

2005-09-28-nordlys-skotsk-tromso-patriot.kurz: Short interview on the day of the concert at Blå Rock, Tromsø (Wednesday, 28.09.2005). Leven says (self-report) that Tromsø has a positive “end-of-the-world-feeling”; his love of Tromsø arose during four earlier visits, and he wrote some of his best songs in Tromsø hotel rooms.
inhalt: Short interview on the day of the concert at Blå Rock, Tromsø (Wednesday, 28.09.2005). Leven says (self-report) that Tromsø has a positive “end-of-the-world-feeling”; his love of Tromsø arose during four earlier visits, and he wrote some of his best songs in Tromsø hotel rooms. He is on a big Norway tour and has already played Oslo and Trondheim. On *Elegy for Johnny Cash*: Cash meant nothing to him at first, until the video for “Hurt” moved him; after that he came to appreciate the last albums in particular.

2005-09-plattentests-de-elegy-for-johnny.kurz: Review for the album's release (released 12.09.2005, Cooking Vinyl/Indigo) under the title “Black Suit”.
inhalt: Review for the album's release (released 12.09.2005, Cooking Vinyl/Indigo) under the title “Black Suit”. Ding describes Leven's voice, marked by life, and the stranglehold attack of the mid-eighties, then the album as a walk through Cash's last stations with vagabonds and the forgotten; recorded in Beirut during a Roma festival with musicians such as the percussionist Reza Almieri, the viola player Mixialis Kataxanis and Robert Fisher. The smooth polish occasionally gets in the way. Rating: 6/10 (reader average 7/10).

2005-10-01-lofotposten-bla-leven.kurz: Disappointed review of the concert at the full Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg on Thursday, 29.09.2005; the support act was Hot Club de Norvège.
inhalt: Disappointed review of the concert at the full Præstengbrygga in Kabelvåg on Thursday, 29.09.2005; the support act was Hot Club de Norvège. Everything was as on every Kabelvåg visit – vodka glass and beer on the floor, guitar on the belly, dry quips – and the singing impeccable (comparison with Cornelis Vreeswijk). But after barely an hour and long soundchecks many left the hall or gathered outside in the smokers' corner; perhaps the jazz fans left after the support act, perhaps Leven lacked energy after a long tour of northern Norway. Among other songs he sang “Universal Blue”.

2005-10-16-bergensavisen-bergensblod.kurz: This week Leven was “official Scottish ambassador” in Bergen: on Wednesday (12.10.2005) he appeared as musical guest of the British Week at Galleri Nygaten, for the 60th anniversary of the Norway–Shetland ferry link; in the second set the audience was very drunk, he…
inhalt: This week Leven was “official Scottish ambassador” in Bergen: on Wednesday (12.10.2005) he appeared as musical guest of the British Week at Galleri Nygaten, for the 60th anniversary of the Norway–Shetland ferry link; in the second set the audience was very drunk, and he had to sing the more cheerful songs. On Friday (21.10.) he plays solo at Kamelon, his second Bergen concert of the year. Leven says (self-report) that he never liked Johnny Cash – Cash stood for him for Scottish “rednecks” – until a few years ago he saw the video for “Hurt” in a hotel room in Svolvær; the Rubin albums are fabulous. The title song became the “locomotive” during the recordings in Lebanon as the most positive piece; the release date of 12 September, the second anniversary of Cash's death, is a coincidence. Plans: a Bergen concert with Ian Rankin the following year, a house swap for a week with Frank Nes (Leven and his wife Deborah in Bergen), perhaps a record in Bergen. *Elegy* got a 5 on the dice scale in BA.

2005-10-17-stavanger-aftenblad-leven-lov.kurz: Preview with an interview on Leven's concert at Stavanger's Checkpoint Charlie (the Thursday after publication, so probably 20.10.2005).
inhalt: Preview with an interview on Leven's concert at Stavanger's Checkpoint Charlie (the Thursday after publication, so probably 20.10.2005). The 55-year-old has been very active for ten or eleven years after a long break. Stavanger reminds him of small Scottish towns, and he plans to use the day off after the concert to explore.

At the centre is *Elegy for Johnny Cash* (2005). Leven says the album came about in Beirut: at a music event he met old friends again and got to know Lebanese musicians; rather than bringing them to Scotland, he travelled to Lebanon with the producer. The title came only during the recording. He did not like Cash as a young man; he discovered him only about two years earlier, when he heard “Hurt” on the radio in a hotel in Kabelvåg and fell in love. At the concert he intends to play old, new and unreleased pieces; he thinks his music appeals to all age groups, likes to talk to the audience after concerts and treats pushy fans politely but firmly. The article closes with an overview of the concert week in Stavanger (Zoom finale, Brian McFadden, Dungen and others).

2005-11-11-nrk-no-nordaforr-med-jackie-l.autor: anonymous (NRK; journey and photos: Arne Berg, NRK P2)
2005-11-11-nrk-no-nordaforr-med-jackie-l.kurz: NRK text portrait for the radio series “Ukas P2-artist” (14–18.11.2005, weekdays 9.30–10.00 am on NRK P2).
inhalt: NRK text portrait for the radio series “Ukas P2-artist” (14–18.11.2005, weekdays 9.30–10.00 am on NRK P2). Short biography: after four Doll by Doll albums a severe crisis, heroin as self-medication against anxiety, finally overcoming the addiction; the later records are self-critical, honest and at the same time quirkily humorous, and revolve around the question of what it means to be a human being and above all a man. The P2 man Arne Berg, a long-time Leven listener, accompanied him to concerts in Tromsø and Kabelvåg and along the coast on the Hurtigruten; the landscape awoke in Leven memories of his Scottish outsider childhood.
zitate_kontext: the basic question of his songs according to NRK.

2005-11-16-gaesteliste-der-furchtlose-so.kurz: Interview on “Elegy for Johnny Cash” (2005). Leven says that both his parents died the previous year, his father after a long illness at about the time of Cash's death; only through his father's death did he come to Cash's music, and the title song “wrote itself” (self-report).
inhalt: Interview on “Elegy for Johnny Cash” (2005). Leven says that both his parents died the previous year, his father after a long illness at about the time of Cash's death; only through his father's death did he come to Cash's music, and the title song “wrote itself” (self-report). He avoided country for a long time because in his youth in Scotland mainly insufferable “rednecks” listened to it; Michael Weston King showed him the way in. The songs are more about other people, for instance “King of the Barley” (the brooding Scottish pub-goer) and “Vibration White Finger” (occupational disease as a parable). Musically he worked with the sound engineer David Wrench and Lebanese musicians he had met at a festival: the drummer “Reesa” advised using drum machines so that the guitars would have more room, the bassist Mohammed played; “All The Rage” contains a rap section he wrote himself. Robert Fisher (Willard Grant Conspiracy) recites a poem by Gary Snyder and sings “The Law of Tide”; “In Memory of My Mother” is a poem by Patrick Kavanagh, for his mother, who died in October 2004. For the tour with Cosgrave he is considering a Greek viola player and a Norwegian percussionist. Leven's conclusion: he is less afraid today and writes more powerfully, now that both parents are dead.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his development as a songwriter.

2005-11-16-ostlendingen-leven-uten-brak.kurz: Short review: Leven, a mixture of poet and musician, almost always delivers something solid. The title leads one to expect a tribute album, but it is that only in part – a few pieces in Cash's style, otherwise his own songs, often dark, at times light and pretty; spoken word and a bit of “hip-hop light” without a central role.
inhalt: Short review: Leven, a mixture of poet and musician, almost always delivers something solid. The title leads one to expect a tribute album, but it is that only in part – a few pieces in Cash's style, otherwise his own songs, often dark, at times light and pretty; spoken word and a bit of “hip-hop light” without a central role. The lyrics (poems) are always rewarding.

2005-12-03-kindamuzik-elegy-for-johnny-c.kurz: Dielemans picks up from his 2004 Crossing Border interview in which Leven had announced an album in Beirut.
inhalt: Dielemans picks up from his 2004 Crossing Border interview in which Leven had announced an album in Beirut. He stresses that the title is misleading – only the title track is a tribute to Cash. Singled out: “The Law of Tide”, sung by Robert Fisher (Willard Grant Conspiracy), contributions from Michael Weston King (“Glad Go Blind”) and the rapper Martin Okasili (“All the Rage”). The experiments with electronics are respected, but many pieces are too long and without effect; the voice saves a lot. Overall tone: mixed.

2005-12-12-kindamuzik-jackie-leven-said.kurz: Review of the double CD with Ian Rankin: CD 1 contains Rankin's reading of the story about a family at a funeral, interrupted by Leven's music; CD 2 new songs, “I Say a Little Prayer” and older material.
inhalt: Review of the double CD with Ian Rankin: CD 1 contains Rankin's reading of the story about a family at a funeral, interrupted by Leven's music; CD 2 new songs, “I Say a Little Prayer” and older material. The live half with acoustic guitar and keyboard is praised as pleasant and the Crossing Border-like concept as refreshing, while the studio recordings are panned as smooth, boring and overproduced. Overall tone: mixed to negative.

2006-03-16-mescalina-elegy-for-johnny-ca.kurz: Belated review (the album had come out the previous year, before the Cash film): not a tribute or covers album, but new Leven songs with a homage in the title track and in “The Law Of Tide” (sung by Robert Fisher).
inhalt: Belated review (the album had come out the previous year, before the Cash film): not a tribute or covers album, but new Leven songs with a homage in the title track and in “The Law Of Tide” (sung by Robert Fisher). The musicians come from Greece and Lebanon, where the album was recorded. Singled out: “Museum Of Childhood” (the Leonard–Durán boxing match), “King Of The Barley” (Kirkcaldy), the spoken pieces “In Memory Of My Mother” and “Why Log Truck Drivers…”. Criticism of overloaded arrangements, some of which sound like the Eighties. Overall tone: positive, “un signor disco”.

2006-06-20-gaesteliste-solingen-steinenh.kurz: Report on the concert at the Steinenhaus in Solingen (“Cornish Pub”, promoter Fritz Kappner) on the evening of the World Cup match England–Sweden; Leven greeted the audience with a Swedish flag on his amplifier.
inhalt: Report on the concert at the Steinenhaus in Solingen (“Cornish Pub”, promoter Fritz Kappner) on the evening of the World Cup match England–Sweden; Leven greeted the audience with a Swedish flag on his amplifier. Michael Cosgrave played despite being ill. Leven promoted the Doll by Doll live CD “Revenge of Memory”, a bootleg of the 1983 album withheld by Virgin, and “Songs for Lonely Americans”, and told the story of Bob Dylan in the Moscow metro for “Moscow Train”. Overall tone: pleasant, but quieter and less inspired than usual; the stories more often fizzled out.

2006-06-30-reykjavik-grapevine-dancing-p.kurz: Cover interview during Rankin's visit to Iceland. Asked about his punk band Dancing Pigs, Rankin says his rock-star dream had come true only recently: Leven had found himself mentioned in a Rebus novel, made contact via the publisher; the joint concerts (Rankin reads a long short story, Leven sings matching songs) were so successful that a double CD resulted. Since then he has found himself in record shops such as Virgin or HMV on the shelf next to R.E.M.
inhalt: Cover interview during Rankin's visit to Iceland. Asked about his punk band Dancing Pigs, Rankin says his rock-star dream had come true only recently: Leven had found himself mentioned in a Rebus novel, made contact via the publisher; the joint concerts (Rankin reads a long short story, Leven sings matching songs) were so successful that a double CD resulted. Since then he has found himself in record shops such as Virgin or HMV on the shelf next to R.E.M.

2006-09-08-gaesteliste-sir-vincent-lone-.kurz: Maurer explains the alter ego as Leven presents it at concerts: he had written more songs than the market could cope with.
inhalt: Maurer explains the alter ego as Leven presents it at concerts: he had written more songs than the market could cope with. The music is a kind of “Jackie Light” with Cosgrave, less opulent, the lyrics more concrete and in part political rather than poetic. The Bob Dylan anecdote for “Moscow Train” is retold. Overall tone: friendly, slightly amused that Leven is pictured on the cover.

2006-09-08-the-independent-album-sir-vin.kurz: Gill prefers the restrained songs. The electronic experiments convince him less.
inhalt: Gill prefers the restrained songs. The electronic experiments convince him less.

2006-09-11-musicomh-sir-vincent-lone-son.kurz: Three out of five stars for the British Cooking Vinyl release of the first Lone album.
inhalt: Three out of five stars for the British Cooking Vinyl release of the first Lone album. The pseudonym allows the ex-Doll by Doll singer to experiment with American folk of the 1960s and to sidestep his own reputation. Praised are the pared-down, word-focused approach, the dry humour (*Straight Outta Caledonia*), the cold electronic *Moscow Train*, *The Lights Below*, *The War Crimes of Ariel Sharon* and especially *In Search Of Stone*. Criticism: lack of form, constant changes of mood, flagging momentum – the freedom of the project becomes its weakness; a “ragbag of fascinating scraps”.

2006-10-10-drammens-tidende-mer-politisk.kurz: Short review of the Cooking Vinyl edition (in Norway via Bonnier Amigo) of *Songs for Lonely Americans*, which Leven releases under the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone.
inhalt: Short review of the Cooking Vinyl edition (in Norway via Bonnier Amigo) of *Songs for Lonely Americans*, which Leven releases under the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone. Andreassen hears the familiar vocal splendour, but a more political tongue than usual (“The War Crimes of Ariel Sharon” and “(I've Never Known) Peace on Earth” are named); the album is indispensable for fans, but at the same time more ordinary and less special than much else by Leven. “Revenge of Memory” and “Balamory Death Chant” are singled out. Closing: for the many people in Drammen who have discovered Leven, a record that completes the picture of the “great Scottish artist”. Overall tone: benevolent, but not euphoric.

2006-12-12-plattentests-forum-jackie-lev.kurz: Thread from December 2006 to 2014 (around 20 posts). Praise for “The Mystery of Love” and for his live presence (“live the man is a bomb”), a memory of a concert at the Cologne Gloria with Richard Thompson and Midnight Choir, mockery of Leven's girth and Bermuda shirts.
inhalt: Thread from December 2006 to 2014 (around 20 posts). Praise for “The Mystery of Love” and for his live presence (“live the man is a bomb”), a memory of a concert at the Cologne Gloria with Richard Thompson and Midnight Choir, mockery of Leven's girth and Bermuda shirts. In 2007 a user sees Leven shopping in central Cologne; the Plattentests reviewer Oliver Ding and a user find the new album weak (“I've Been Everywhere” praised as a “Germany impression”). From 15.11.2011 there are posts of mourning, including on “Working Alone” and “Gylen” as formative songs, and the remark that having seen his concerts was a privilege.

inhalt: The short introduction names eleven folk-rock pieces and Johnny Dowd and Leon Hunt as guests. Despite being placed in the reviews section, the visible text contains no actual verdict, only a brief introduction and the track list.

2007-02-16-gaesteliste-oh-what-a-blow-th.kurz: Short review: not a revolutionarily new but a typically classic Leven album with Johnny Dowd as a partner, a homage to Kevin Coyne, more blues in the guitar playing, poems by Kenneth Patchen and “I've Been Everywhere” as a comic list of his usual tour stops.
inhalt: Short review: not a revolutionarily new but a typically classic Leven album with Johnny Dowd as a partner, a homage to Kevin Coyne, more blues in the guitar playing, poems by Kenneth Patchen and “I've Been Everywhere” as a comic list of his usual tour stops. Theme: drinking. Overall tone: benevolent.

2007-02-16-the-independent-album-jackie-.kurz: Gill praises the combination of despair and black humour. He particularly recommends “Vox Humana”.
inhalt: Gill praises the combination of despair and black humour. He particularly recommends “Vox Humana”.

2007-02-19-musicomh-oh-what-a-blow-that-.kurz: Three out of five stars. Smith begins with the confession that he long took Leven for a woman, compares the album's handling of ageing with Dylan's *Modern Times* and praises Johnny Dowd's contributions, which bring a “gothic”, American mood.
inhalt: Three out of five stars. Smith begins with the confession that he long took Leven for a woman, compares the album's handling of ageing with Dylan's *Modern Times* and praises Johnny Dowd's contributions, which bring a “gothic”, American mood. He calls “Vox Humana” and “One Man One Guitar” masterpieces.

2007-02-26-kindamuzik-oh-what-a-blow-tha.kurz: Review taking up the album's ghost motif (warning notice in the inlay, collection of quotations in the booklet).
inhalt: Review taking up the album's ghost motif (warning notice in the inlay, collection of quotations in the booklet). Discussed are “Vox Humana”, “Another Man's Rain”, “I've Been Everywhere” as a tour of Germany with Johnny Dowd, Dowd's reading of Kenneth Patchen's “The Skaters”, the ode to Judee Sill and the Kevin Coyne homage “Here Come The Urban Ravens”; Leon Hunt (banjo) and Michael Cosgrave shape the sound. Verdict: well-disposed but undecided – some of it grips, some of it leaves one cold.

2007-03-02-rolling-stone-de-oh-what-a-bl.kurz: Mixed review: the “estimated 23rd album” is an all too cosy sequel to the last records, “preaching to the converted”.
inhalt: Mixed review: the “estimated 23rd album” is an all too cosy sequel to the last records, “preaching to the converted”. Variety is provided by Johnny Dowd (allegedly won over a bottle of absinthe) with “One Man One Guitar” and the Patchen poem “The Skaters”; the Judee Sill homage “The Silver In Her Crucifix” is a success, the Kevin Coyne song “well meant”. “I've Been Everywhere” lists German tour cities, with “Baden-Baden” in the chorus. Verdict: the “iron man” has developed a little rust.

2007-04-05-musicomh-jackie-leven-troubad.kurz: Four out of five stars. Jerome describes a cramped, smoky club with waitresses walking past in front of the stage, and a nervous yet self-assured Leven whose voice makes one forget all adversity.
inhalt: Four out of five stars. Jerome describes a cramped, smoky club with waitresses walking past in front of the stage, and a nervous yet self-assured Leven whose voice makes one forget all adversity. Played were, among others, “Elegy for Johnny Cash”, “Museum of Childhood”, “Here Come the Urban Ravens” (announced as a tribute to Kevin Coyne), “Moscow Train” and “Vox Humana”, accompanied by Michael Cosgrave (keyboards) and a guitarist “Kevin O'Foster”. Plenty of coarse stage humour, including about Gordon Brown and Amy Winehouse.

2007-04-12-the-telegraph-british-rocks-l.kurz: Neil McCormick uses the reissue of all four Doll by Doll albums on Rhino as an occasion to declare “Gypsy Blood” (1979) the lost masterpiece of British rock: sweeping, tipping from the tender to the terrifying, with Leven's voice gliding between baritone and falsetto; he comp…
inhalt: Neil McCormick uses the reissue of all four Doll by Doll albums on Rhino as an occasion to declare “Gypsy Blood” (1979) the lost masterpiece of British rock: sweeping, tipping from the tender to the terrifying, with Leven's voice gliding between baritone and falsetto; he compares the effect with “Dark Side of the Moon”, “Forever Changes” and “The Bends”. The album came out on the small label Automatic to good reviews and dismal sales; the band harmed itself with its belligerent attitude, made many enemies and changed label after the flop. The master tapes were said to be lost, and some reissues were mastered from vinyl. Leven speaks (self-report) about the band as an alliance of traumatised people (Jung quotation on “matching psychic disturbance”), about the aspiration to be the definitive band of its time, and about the self-chosen images that had closed doors. There follow the attack after the band's end (18 months without a voice), heroin, the cure through acupuncture and “psychic healing”, the founding of the Core Trust in 1985 and anecdotes about Princess Diana, who had urged him to sing. Finally: Jo Shaw now builds hi-tech studios (for Mark Knopfler and Paul Allen, among others), David McIntosh is a potter and furniture maker. Verdict: hymnic.

2007-04-22-rocktimes-oh-what-a-blow-that.kurz: Detailed, positive review: less melodramatic and more relaxed than its predecessors, with folk, rockabilly, chanson and blues, produced by Leven with David Wrench; part of the vocal tracks were reportedly recorded in a Ukrainian church.
inhalt: Detailed, positive review: less melodramatic and more relaxed than its predecessors, with folk, rockabilly, chanson and blues, produced by Leven with David Wrench; part of the vocal tracks were reportedly recorded in a Ukrainian church. The reviewer mentions that the four Doll by Doll albums have been announced for reissue. Verdict: not his most emotionally dense work, but a good one; “the dark man” is mellowing with age.

2007-04-25-die-welt-unglaublich-schoener.kurz: Krulle describes a thrilling evening at the Knust in Hamburg with Michael Cosgrave. He praises Leven's singing, his playing melody and bass at the same time, and the combination of songs with comic stories.
inhalt: Krulle describes a thrilling evening at the Knust in Hamburg with Michael Cosgrave. He praises Leven's singing, his playing melody and bass at the same time, and the combination of songs with comic stories.

2007-04-bluesnews-jackie-leven-apner-blu.kurz: Two-page conversation in the Norwegian blues magazine on the occasion of *Oh What a Blow That Phantom Dealt Me!*, conducted while Leven was on a “flying visit” in Oslo to play a sold-out concert at John Dee (March 2007).
inhalt: Two-page conversation in the Norwegian blues magazine on the occasion of *Oh What a Blow That Phantom Dealt Me!*, conducted while Leven was on a “flying visit” in Oslo to play a sold-out concert at John Dee (March 2007). The introduction sums up the legend: Doll by Doll in 1979 as the hottest live band in London's clubs, four acclaimed albums, then the knife attack with his throat slit open, heroin against the pain, the founding of the Core Trust, in which Leven is said to have cured himself, as one of the first patients, with acupuncture and healing treatment. The royal family became patron, and Princess Diana persuaded him on a visit to sing again. In Norway Leven has a very loyal audience; the author calls his music “hvit keltisk soul”.

Leven says (self-report) that his mother constantly listened to black American blues; while other children listened to Elvis, he grew up with Lightnin' Hopkins, favourite piece “Blues in the Bottle”. With the new album he deliberately opened this box and wanted an “unveiled” blues mood; he had always written from a blues heart. “Childish Blues” was meant to sound like Tom Waits and now sounds like Leon Redbone. A lot of modern blues is lazy and meaningless; one has to work the blues into the contexts of today's world. Andreassen praises the guitar playing and the role of Johnny Dowd, who gives the album “Tom Waits darkness”; Leven hints that English critics demanded more collaboration with Dowd. At the same time the Doll by Doll albums appear on CD for the first time. Verdict: very favourable, the author compares the album with Chris Rea's blues box set of the previous year.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his mother's blues records.

2007-05-09-mescalina-oh-what-a-blow-that.kurz: Leven lives from music and releases at least one album a year, each with a reason to exist.
inhalt: Leven lives from music and releases at least one album a year, each with a reason to exist. This one, however, is not one of his best: eleven songs about forgotten ghosts (Judee Sill, Kevin Coyne, Kenneth Patchen, acquaintances from touring), with Johnny Dowd, David Wrench (production), Michael Cosgrave and Leon Hunt; “Mellow My Madness” is dedicated to an initiative for the mentally ill (with DJ Unfit For Work). Really strong pieces are missing. Verdict: lukewarm.

2007-06-14-kevin-coyne-home-page-whisper.titel: Whispers From The Offing – A Tribute to Kevin Coyne (Comments and Reviews)
2007-06-14-kevin-coyne-home-page-whisper.autor: Pascal Regis (compilation); press and fan voices
2007-06-14-kevin-coyne-home-page-whisper.kurz: Collection page for the charity tribute CD for Kevin Coyne (Life and Living Records, March 2007, in aid of projects at London's Maudsley Hospital).
inhalt: Collection page for the charity tribute CD for Kevin Coyne (Life and Living Records, March 2007, in aid of projects at London's Maudsley Hospital). Leven connection: the translated review from the Nuremberg city magazine *Plärrer* (5 stars, CD of the Month, issue 5/2007) mentions the “well-known Scottish songwriter” Leven, who dedicated a song to Coyne on his new CD, which is also included here; a transcribed article from the *Derby Evening Telegraph* (Sarah Whelan, 14.06.2007) mentions *Here Come the Urban Ravens* as a new song inspired by Leven's friendship with Coyne. Several fan reviews single out Leven's contribution as the only non-cover track.

2007-07-23-halden-arbeiderblad-den-store.kurz: Fact profile from a series that festival organiser Tom Skjeklesæther wrote for Halden Arbeiderblad about the artists of Down on the Farm 2007 (Gribsrød gård, Enningdalen near Halden).
inhalt: Fact profile from a series that festival organiser Tom Skjeklesæther wrote for Halden Arbeiderblad about the artists of Down on the Farm 2007 (Gribsrød gård, Enningdalen near Halden). Header with fact box (Fife, born 1950), listening recommendations (*The Mystery of Love*, *Oh What a Blow That Phantom Dealt Me!*, and by Doll by Doll *Gypsy Blood* and *Doll by Doll*, both on CD for the first time in 2007) and jackieleven.com.

The familiar biography is retold: Leven as a troubadour of “classic Celtic soul” alongside Van Morrison; ten years' pause after the dissolution of Doll by Doll (given here as 1984), because at the start of the recordings for his solo debut in London he was said to have been attacked and almost strangled and unable to speak for almost two years; heroin addiction; in 1988 a single with the new band CBI with two Doll by Doll members and Glen Matlock. At the end of the 1980s he is said to have freed himself from heroin with a method he developed himself, which became the basis of the CORE organisation; Leven sits on its board today and received England's highest civil award for CORE. Indirectly Princess Diana brought him back to music: during a CORE visit he struck up an old Scottish song when she asked him.

Important for Norway: Doll by Doll had a strong Norwegian fan base and in 1982 opened the rock club Ratz in Oslo with a sold-out concert, one of the band's last. Since 1994 twelve official solo albums plus fan-club records; collaborations with Robert Bly, Ian Rankin, David Thomas and Johnny Dowd, the last at Down on the Farm in 1998. Leven is said to be known for improvised collaborations on stage and, together with Robyn Hitchcock and John Paul Jones, is to host the new Campfire Stage.

2007-09-24-drammens-tidende-jackie-pa-bu.kurz: Preview of the “exclusive” concert on Thursday, 4 October 2007, at Buddy (Amtmand Blomsgate, Drammen) – according to the paper Leven's fourth visit to Drammen, where he has a large, loyal audience and many friends.
inhalt: Preview of the “exclusive” concert on Thursday, 4 October 2007, at Buddy (Amtmand Blomsgate, Drammen) – according to the paper Leven's fourth visit to Drammen, where he has a large, loyal audience and many friends. Leven is said to be on a larger tour with a total of 45 concerts before Christmas in England, Belgium, Germany, Scotland, Sweden and Norway. Dagbladet called him “Scotland's answer to Van Morrison”; he himself acknowledges roots in Johnny Cash and Van Morrison. The DT review by Øyvind R. Gundersen of his appearance at the Working Class Hero festival “two years ago” (2005) is quoted. On 3 and 4 October DT announces the concert again as a “Lyttekonsert” at 9 pm.

2007-10-03-vaganavisa-en-annen-manns-reg.kurz: Double-page report with interview, conducted on the day of the concert (Wednesday, 26.09.2007) in Svolvær; published a week later.
inhalt: Double-page report with interview, conducted on the day of the concert (Wednesday, 26.09.2007) in Svolvær; published a week later. Photos show Leven with organiser Jan Åge Johansen (“to gode venner”). Opening: Leven sits in the car, rain on the windscreen; the author recaps the attack of 1983, the loss of his voice and record contract and the way out of heroin via holistic therapy.

Leven says (self-reports): on first entering the Præstengbrygga he had thought the room, with a staircase in the middle of the hall, hopeless – and had been wrong. He told his Norwegian agent he wanted to see not just Oslo and Bergen but the whole country. The relationship between audience and artist is like being in love. Once, on a Saturday night in northern Norway, he played to a noisy audience, so bad that Johansen went home; otherwise the Brygga is a place where people listen, and the friendship with Johansen matters. He writes constantly in a notebook; as occasions for songs he names a woman in a bar who asked him to sell a car and died the same evening, a homeless man by the railway tracks in Trondheim and a man on the Hurtigruten who wanted to go home in the Trollfjord. Norway's nature is frightening to him, Lofoten a brutal version of the Scottish north-west coast; he used to hike alone in the Hebrides, now here. He lives on the English south coast with a view of the Isle of Wight. In Europe he plays with a band, in Scandinavia alone – a band in northern Norway would be too expensive, and he likes the solitude. He has an “almost erotic relationship with rain” and wrote “Another Man's Rain” about it. The evening's concert is being recorded and is due to appear on CD next year; in 2008 a new album is coming and he will return to Kabelvåg.

2007-11-14-gaesteliste-koeln-kulturbunke.kurz: Report on the Cologne concert with Michael Weston King as support (plus Markus Segschneider).
inhalt: Report on the Cologne concert with Michael Weston King as support (plus Markus Segschneider). Maurer relays Leven's steakhouse anecdote with the Willard Grant Conspiracy in Glasgow and stresses that Leven is a classic storyteller who refuses encore rituals. The show was especially personal: stories about women trouble, the attack and recovery, and a “Royal Lunch” with Lady Diana, for whom he had to sing “Main Travelled Roads” (self-report); Cosgrave has lately also played flute. Verdict: positive, without great revelations.

2008-01-03-rolling-stone-de-jackie-balfo.kurz: Double review of the pseudonym albums: Sir Vincent Lone's second album “When the Bridegroom Comes (Songs for Women)” with quiet folk songs and cover versions (Jackson C. Frank, Judee Sill, Donovan, David Childers, Dan Britton) – a “cosy record for the congregation”; and the audiobook “Chip Pan Fire”, in…
inhalt: Double review of the pseudonym albums: Sir Vincent Lone's second album “When the Bridegroom Comes (Songs for Women)” with quiet folk songs and cover versions (Jackson C. Frank, Judee Sill, Donovan, David Childers, Dan Britton) – a “cosy record for the congregation”; and the audiobook “Chip Pan Fire”, in which Leven as Jackie Balfour, junior reporter of the “Glenrodent Gazette”, describes Scottish small-town life, supplemented by three stage stories. Verdict: all the names add up to a whole after all – Leven the storyteller.

2008-01-netrhythms-jackie-balfour-chip-p.kurz: Kidman reviews the spoken-word album by Leven's fictional twin Jackie Balfour, one of two simultaneous Leven releases.
inhalt: Kidman reviews the spoken-word album by Leven's fictional twin Jackie Balfour, one of two simultaneous Leven releases. Part 1: episodes from Balfour's first job as a local reporter at the notorious “Glenrodent Gazette” in Fife in the mid-1960s, interrupted by piano interludes by Michael Cosgrave based on Scottish dance forms. Part 2: three well-known Leven stories – *Sting's Dead* (live before a German audience), *Stupid Local Boasts* (from the Rankin show at the Edinburgh Festival 2004, Rankin as “straight man”) and *Sex Tourist* (club in Sydney, 2001). Verdict: affectionate and amusing, but suited only to a small audience.

2008-07-23-whiskyfun-music-and-whisky-in.kurz: The conversation combines the announcement of “Lovers at the Gun Club” with Leven's musical preferences and his ideas about drinking whisky.
inhalt: The conversation combines the announcement of “Lovers at the Gun Club” with Leven's musical preferences and his ideas about drinking whisky. Leven lists his musical partners to date and singles out Johnny Dowd. For the new album he gives 18 August 2008 as the release date. Afterwards he wants to travel through Europe for several months; the overseas tours mentioned for the following year are intentions at the time of the interview.

As his favourite singer he names Chet Baker, as a particularly admired songwriter Judee Sill; for cleaning he listens to Roland Kirk. His later appreciation of Patsy Cline serves him as an example of how age and circumstances change listening. For him, music and whisky can equally trigger a brief moment of inner harmony.

Leven says his father wrote a whisky book and took him to distilleries as a teenager. Linkwood and Mortlach are particularly important to him, but he now often prefers simple blends in ordinary bars. His answers are directed against status consumption and over-refined connoisseur language. He links places, drinks and music into small scenes; the provocative judgements and comic stories belong to the tone of the interview and are not factual quality assessments.

2008-08-18-musicomh-lovers-at-the-gun-cl.kurz: Four out of five stars. Cole introduces Leven as “the nearest thing to Johnny Cash that Britain will ever have”; the album offers no surprises, Leven has found his formula of dark, rough-hewn folk.
inhalt: Four out of five stars. Cole introduces Leven as “the nearest thing to Johnny Cash that Britain will ever have”; the album offers no surprises, Leven has found his formula of dark, rough-hewn folk. Highlighted are “Dent in the Fender and the Wheel of Fate”, “My Old Home” and “Woman in a Car”; the American influences enrich the album.

2008-08-22-gaesteliste-nicht-ganz-richti.kurz: Interview on “Lovers at the Gun Club” (2008). Maurer reports that Leven chose the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone after being annoyed that Will Oldham, and not he, had come up with “Bonnie Prince”; the new album was recorded without the record company's knowledge, which Leven plays down.
inhalt: Interview on “Lovers at the Gun Club” (2008). Maurer reports that Leven chose the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone after being annoyed that Will Oldham, and not he, had come up with “Bonnie Prince”; the new album was recorded without the record company's knowledge, which Leven plays down. Difference between Leven and Lone: Jackie is more dogged because he has to live from it, Sir Vince has more fun (self-report). Johnny Dowd sings the title song; the two met when both happened to be performing in Kufstein. The title story: a drive through the Shenandoah Valley with the “transsexual killer” Shannon Doyle, children giving the Hitler salute, followed by shooting practice at the shooting club (self-report, evidently invented or exaggerated). Leven wants songs to sound “not quite right”, as with David Lynch or Tarantino; he considers “Innocent Railway” one of his best songs. He chooses poetry out of love, not to convert people. Closing anecdote: “Olivier's Blues” came about with Sir Laurence Olivier, whose son Rich Olivier is a close friend (Leven is godfather to his son); Olivier called him a “jolly green giant” (self-report). Outlook: autumn tour with Cosgrave.

2008-08-26-ostlendingen-jackie-leven-lov.kurz: Positive short review from the record page: Hovensjø introduces Leven (58) as a poet and musician who began as John St. Field, was singer of Doll by Doll, has a spell as a junkie behind him and has since delivered one great album after another.
inhalt: Positive short review from the record page: Hovensjø introduces Leven (58) as a poet and musician who began as John St. Field, was singer of Doll by Doll, has a spell as a junkie behind him and has since delivered one great album after another. The new one is “meget interessant”: Leven mixes styles and borrows other people's music – the guitar solo from Them's “Gloria” in the title track, Willie Dixon's “My Babe” in “Olivier Blues”, a verse from David Childers’ “Heart in My Soul” in “The Dent in the Fender and the Wheel of Fate”; Childers’ original recording closes the album. Partly rocky, partly jazzy, partly folky, partly poem reading; the lyrics have an unsettling false bottom, which Leven's dark, vibrating voice emphasises. Recommendation for a concentrated hour of listening.

2008-08-29-bergensavisen-jackie-leven-ti.kurz: Short preview: on Sunday, 9 November (2008) Leven, currently promoting *Lovers at the Gun Club*, will play again at Madam Felle on Bryggen in Bergen, where he has already given “magical” concerts; beautiful songs and absurd stories are promised.
inhalt: Short preview: on Sunday, 9 November (2008) Leven, currently promoting *Lovers at the Gun Club*, will play again at Madam Felle on Bryggen in Bergen, where he has already given “magical” concerts; beautiful songs and absurd stories are promised. The *Independent*'s four-out-of-five-star review of the new record is quoted. Biographical key data: first album 1971, Doll by Doll 1978–1982, solo restart in the early 1990s.

2008-08-netrhythms-lovers-at-the-gun-clu.kurz: Davies agrees with Leven's own assessment that this is one of his best albums. He describes the title song with Johnny Dowd as lead voice (inspired by stories of a person called Shannon Doyle), “Olivier Blues”, the Kenneth Patchen setting “To Whom It May Concern”, “Fareham Confidential” an…
inhalt: Davies agrees with Leven's own assessment that this is one of his best albums. He describes the title song with Johnny Dowd as lead voice (inspired by stories of a person called Shannon Doyle), “Olivier Blues”, the Kenneth Patchen setting “To Whom It May Concern”, “Fareham Confidential” and the closing piece “Heart in My Soul”, taken over from David Childers. Very positive: “idiosyncratic, intoxicating, fascinating and generous”.

2008-08-vanguard-online-jackie-leven-int.kurz: Short, apparently written interview by the webzine Vanguard Online on the release of Lovers At The Gun Club (2008).
inhalt: Short, apparently written interview by the webzine Vanguard Online on the release of Lovers At The Gun Club (2008). Leven explains that he puts albums together as a “family” of songs, always with one old and one new song; “Fareham Confidential” was written in ten minutes in a bar in Fareham. He defends guest tracks by other artists (here David Childers) as a means of creating community among musicians, and collaborations (Johnny Dowd, David Thomas) for their voice and persona. He owns a large poetry library; after a Patchen poem on the predecessor (Oh What A Blow That Phantom Dealt Me), Gun Club also contains one. He is in constant contact with Robert Bly. A second and third Argyll Cycle album are conceivable; another album is in progress for 2010. Playful questions: with Lightnin' Hopkins he would found the zombie band “Leven and Hopkins (deceased)”; on male melancholy and the nickname “the miserable git”.

2008-09-01-westzeit-lovers-at-the-gun-cl.kurz: Enthusiastic short review: never have Leven's interpretations been “so snotty, skewed, rough”; in the title track, sung by Johnny Dowd, Leven quotes Van Morrison's “Gloria”.
inhalt: Enthusiastic short review: never have Leven's interpretations been “so snotty, skewed, rough”; in the title track, sung by Johnny Dowd, Leven quotes Van Morrison's “Gloria”. Hübner praises a light-footed assurance like that of Tom Waits, the Go-Betweens or Lambchop. Rating: 4 (Westzeit scale, presumably out of 5).

2008-09-03-the-independent-jackie-leven-.kurz: Gill praises Leven's empathy and stage humour. The accompaniment supports his storytelling.
inhalt: Gill praises Leven's empathy and stage humour. The accompaniment supports his storytelling.

2008-09-04-rolling-stone-forum-jackie-le.titel: [Thread: Jackie Leven] (Topic 5, tour dates 2008–2011, tour cancellation 2011)
2008-09-04-rolling-stone-forum-jackie-le.kurz: Thread with 15 posts from September 2008 to September 2011, in which fans post and comment on the German tour dates.
inhalt: Thread with 15 posts from September 2008 to September 2011, in which fans post and comment on the German tour dates. September 2008: 11.09. Verden (Kornbrennerei Flander), 12.09. Völklingen-Lauterbach, then Ansbach, Karlsruhe Jubez, Essen, Berlin, Hannover, Kiel, Hamburg, Bonn, Eppstein; plus the Benelux, UK and Norway dates up to November 2008. February 2009 (Herbrechtingen to Bremen), May 2010 (06.05. Kiel to 20.05. Marburg, including Verden, Einbeck, Hannover, Frankfurt Nachtleben, Saarbrücken, Berlin Quasimodo, Singwitz, Munich Garage, Vienna Chelsea, Dortmund Piano, plus 11.05. Solingen Phönixx), September 2010 (Amsterdam, Hamburg Knust, Münster, Bremen, Essen, Stuttgart, Dresden) and September 2011 (16–27.09., Marburg to Hamburg). On 08.09.2011 “stylo” reports that the 2011 tour is cancelled because of Leven's illness; he is receiving inpatient treatment, and the tour is to be made up in spring 2012. On 24.09.2011 a note on the new “official bootleg” “One Long Cold Morning”.

2008-10-29-nordlys-jackie-leven-tromso-c.titel: [Interview: Jackie Leven before the Circa concert and the Madrugada support slot in Tromsø]
2008-10-29-nordlys-jackie-leven-tromso-c.kurz: Double-page preview with quotes from a conversation. Leven is coming to Tromsø at the weekend: first a solo concert at Circa on Saturday afternoon (5 pm), then as support act for Madrugada at their farewell concerts at the Kulturhuset on Sunday and Monday.
inhalt: Double-page preview with quotes from a conversation. Leven is coming to Tromsø at the weekend: first a solo concert at Circa on Saturday afternoon (5 pm), then as support act for Madrugada at their farewell concerts at the Kulturhuset on Sunday and Monday. The unusual afternoon start is explained by Leven's second passion, Liverpool FC: he has to watch the Tottenham–Liverpool match at half past six, he says, laughing.

The article summarises the biography (Doll by Doll, dissolved 1982; solo career; nocturnal attack after a studio session, almost strangled, loss of speech, of friends and of his partner, psychological problems, heroin, isolation; after a year the founding of a foundation for addiction rehabilitation) and calls him an honest, hard-working and unusually well-reviewed musician whom the Tromsø audience has often seen (a caption mentions one of Leven's “many Blårock concerts” and a dog named Basil who stays at home).

Leven says (self-report) that he has liked Tromsø since seeing a report in an English newspaper many years ago and telling his manager that was where he wanted to go. He always stays at the Grand Hotell, where he has written very many songs: wake up, breakfast, walk through the streets, write in the room. Impressions from the street and from pubs are “stored” and come out when he writes in peace. He knows Norwegian music well, used to support Midnight Choir, rates Bertine Zetlitz (a joint appearance in Stavanger, afterwards the same flight to Oslo) and thinks Norwegian music is currently “hip” in Britain. He calls the invitation from Madrugada a great honour; he remembers the day he got their first record.

2008-11-08-varden-en-lun-kveld-pa-puben.autor: unknown (not reliably attributable in the OCR)

2008-11-12-drammens-tidende-jackie-leven.titel: [Interview/Preview: Jackie Leven back in Drammen – “Comeback overtalt av Lady Diana”]
2008-11-12-drammens-tidende-jackie-leven.kurz: Culture page (p. 12 of the issue) with interview before the second “Lyttekonsert” at Buddy on Thursday, 13.11.2008, 8 pm.
inhalt: Culture page (p. 12 of the issue) with interview before the second “Lyttekonsert” at Buddy on Thursday, 13.11.2008, 8 pm. Andreassen recalls the sold-out concert there the previous year, calls Leven “Scotland's answer to Van Morrison”, refers to Doll by Doll and to the attack in a London side street with a serious neck injury; a subheading claims that Lady Diana persuaded him to make a comeback. The reports from the ongoing Norway tour showed a Leven in rare form, with a new album and new songs; his voice is comparable to Roy Orbison and Aaron Neville, his stock of stories full of irony equally remarkable.

Leven explains (self-report) that it will not be a blueprint of last year's concert: it is about true stories from his life, about accepting and understanding oneself; one cannot die with feelings of guilt. He touches on the US election (a black president is surely not a bad thing). A longer anecdote is set in the 1970s (in the OCR “…castle”, presumably Newcastle): after a falling-out with his business partner, a man named Keith was shot in broad daylight – a “Shannon” had been hired for it – and that same evening a woman in the hotel bar confided her knowledge to him; a strange friendship grew out of it. In Drammen he always feels “magic”; the town reminds him of the working men's clubs of his youth, where people smoked and drank beer – perhaps remnants of the working class; and he likes the women there.

2008-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-2008.kurz: The first roughly 45 entries (16.07.–20.12.2008) welcome the new official website and the album *Oh What A Blow That Phantom Dealt Me* or
inhalt: The first roughly 45 entries (16.07.–20.12.2008) welcome the new official website and the album *Oh What A Blow That Phantom Dealt Me* or Sir Vincent Lone's *Lovers at the Gun Club*. The dominant theme is the direct sale of the live album *Live From A Cornish Pub In Germany*: German fans ask how they are to pay without a British cheque, Britons are still waiting for their CD in September. Alongside this, concert greetings from Vienna (Chelsea, 15.09.), Hamburg, Berlin (Quasimodo), Bonn, Eppstein, Leiden, Dublin, Oslo, Bury, Hebden Bridge, London (Borderline, Putney) and Retford; a fan offers home-made Leven badges, a schoolboy from Johnstone thanks Leven for a school visit in December 2008. A Bonn fan raves about the stage story of “Black Bob”, another asks what in the tales is fact and what is fiction. A user who reveals himself as part of the organiser's circle reports the move of the concert on 07.12.2008 from Coffee Bliss (Lenzie) to Bar Bliss (Kirkintilloch) and then its cancellation. A fan from Liverpool thanks Leven, saying his music accompanied him through the end of an addiction.

2008-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-leven-sa.titel: [Collected finds Nasjonalbiblioteket 2008: short notices, announcements, lists]

2009-02-13-gaesteliste-the-haunted-years.kurz: Review of the double CD with two Haunted Valley live albums: the prison concert in Bergen (2000 according to the text), rather cool, and the recording from Munich's Muffathalle with Cosgrave and Deborah Greenwood, on which Leven shines as an entertainer.
inhalt: Review of the double CD with two Haunted Valley live albums: the prison concert in Bergen (2000 according to the text), rather cool, and the recording from Munich's Muffathalle with Cosgrave and Deborah Greenwood, on which Leven shines as an entertainer. Live recordings are ambivalent because Leven's gestures are missing. Verdict: more for fans who were not members of the Haunted Valley.

2009-02-17-ostlendingen-fra-bergen-fengs.kurz: Short review of the double CD *The Haunted Year – Winter*: Leven (Doll by Doll, then “på kjøret”, trapped again, since then a series of beautiful albums with impressive lyrics) feels at home in Bergen; one CD shows him alone with guitar at the concert in Bergen prison in 2003, where he occasionally tells…
inhalt: Short review of the double CD *The Haunted Year – Winter*: Leven (Doll by Doll, then “på kjøret”, trapped again, since then a series of beautiful albums with impressive lyrics) feels at home in Bergen; one CD shows him alone with guitar at the concert in Bergen prison in 2003, where between songs he tells of his “crooked” life and – with bare accompaniment – one can hear even better than usual how well he sings. The second CD comes from a Munich café in 2000 with fellow musicians, the keyboard player bringing more studio sound. Verdict: Bergen is better.

2009-02-netrhythms-haunted-year-winter.kurz: Introduction to the *Haunted Year* series, with which Leven makes the eight limited fan-club albums regularly available after the end of the Haunted Valley magazine.
inhalt: Introduction to the *Haunted Year* series, with which Leven makes the eight limited fan-club albums regularly available after the end of the Haunted Valley magazine. *Munich Blues* (Café Muffathalle, Munich, with Michael Cosgrave and Deborah Greenwood) comes across as playful, *Men in Prison* (men's prison in Bergen) as more intense, opening with Leven's account of his own past with violence and drugs. Benevolent and informative, no rating.

2009-03-01-record-collector-haunted-year.kurz: Kris Needs (who had followed Doll by Doll for *ZigZag* as early as 1978) calls Leven “the UK's mightiest troubadour” and welcomes the reissue of the Haunted Valley live albums.
inhalt: Kris Needs (who had followed Doll by Doll for *ZigZag* as early as 1978) calls Leven “the UK's mightiest troubadour” and welcomes the reissue of the Haunted Valley live albums. He praises the recording from the men's prison in Bergen (“The Garden”) and *Munich Blues* with Michael Cosgrave and Debbie Greenwood; the booklet with Leven's “Deep Pool” texts is worthy of a book. Very positive; rating not shown on the website.

2009-03-17-laagendalsposten-knut-buen-og.titel: [Kongsberg Jazz Festival 2009: Knut Buen meets Jackie Leven]

2009-04-27-musicomh-man-bleeds-in-glasgo.kurz: Four out of five stars. Oliver considers *Man Bleeds in Glasgow* (1998, with the Celtic Soulmen) the stronger part, because the live versions do without the at times “pale” studio production.
inhalt: Four out of five stars. Oliver considers *Man Bleeds in Glasgow* (1998, with the Celtic Soulmen) the stronger part, because the live versions do without the at times “pale” studio production. *Greetings From Milford* shows Leven as an interpreter of other people's songs (Velvet Underground, Van Morrison's “Madame George”) and ends with Doll by Doll's “Main Travelled Roads”. Leven is a neglected “national treasure”.

2009-05-05-soundi-the-haunted-year-men-i.kurz: Finnish review of the double CD from the reissue series (concert in the Norwegian prison in Bergen and a solo concert in a Munich café), rated 4 out of 5 stars.
inhalt: Finnish review of the double CD from the reissue series (concert in the Norwegian prison in Bergen and a solo concert in a Munich café), rated 4 out of 5 stars. Kanerva compares Leven with Van Morrison – the same Celtic-bluesy roots, but without his breakthrough; Leven's discography fluctuates greatly, only *Night Lilies* is a flawless masterpiece. Praised are powerful, nuanced acoustic guitar playing, stories from life and the baritone; only a great artist is so at one with audience and songs.
zitate_kontext: On life as a travelling musician.

2009-05-netrhythms-haunted-year-spring.kurz: Review of the second double CD of the series: *Man Bleeds in Glasgow* (Water Rats, London, with the Celtic Soulmen Michael Cosgrave and Stephen Hannigan) and *Greetings From Milford* (Haunted Valley Christmas party with the Stornoway Girls at the British Legion Club, Milford).
inhalt: Review of the second double CD of the series: *Man Bleeds in Glasgow* (Water Rats, London, with the Celtic Soulmen Michael Cosgrave and Stephen Hannigan) and *Greetings From Milford* (Haunted Valley Christmas party with the Stornoway Girls at the British Legion Club, Milford). Davies stresses Leven's underrated humour and the cover versions (Dylan, Van Morrison “Madame George”, Bill Withers, Velvet Underground). Positive tenor (“a very good year for Leven fans”).

2009-06-04-record-collector-jackie-leven.kurz: Short live review: Leven opens with “Standing in Another Man's Rain” and closes with “The White Bars of Heaven”; in between the Johnny Cash elegy, a song about ravens and a psychedelic blues transition to Beatles, Van Morrison and Donovan.
inhalt: Short live review: Leven opens with “Standing in Another Man's Rain” and closes with “The White Bars of Heaven”; in between the Johnny Cash elegy, a song about ravens and a psychedelic blues transition to Beatles, Van Morrison and Donovan. Neech highlights the anecdotes (such as how Ralph McTell frightened Leven at their first meeting), the powerful guitar playing and the range of the voice. Verdict in one word: “Unique.”

2009-06-10-diskant-jackie-leven-the-haun.kurz: Danish review of the reissue double CD *The Haunted Year – Spring* (*Man Bleeds in Glasgow* with the Celtic Soulmen, *Greetings From Milford* with the Stornoway Girls).
inhalt: Danish review of the reissue double CD *The Haunted Year – Spring* (*Man Bleeds in Glasgow* with the Celtic Soulmen, *Greetings From Milford* with the Stornoway Girls). Wamsler acknowledges Leven, the “King of Celtic Soul”, as a very good songwriter and strong singer, but finds him less gripping as a live entertainer; the first CD is too static, the second livelier. Verdict: too few highlights for a double album, mixed; no rating.

2009-06-il-popolo-del-blues-spring-man-b.kurz: Review of the spring instalment of the “Haunted Year” series: “Man Bleeds In Glasgow” (Water Rats, London, 1998, with the Celtic Soulmen Michael Cosgrave and Steafan Hannigan) and “Greetings From Milford” (Haunted Valley Christmas party 1999 at the British Legion Club, Milford).
inhalt: Review of the spring instalment of the “Haunted Year” series: “Man Bleeds In Glasgow” (Water Rats, London, 1998, with the Celtic Soulmen Michael Cosgrave and Steafan Hannigan) and “Greetings From Milford” (Haunted Valley Christmas party 1999 at the British Legion Club, Milford). Praised are “Night Lilies”, “Call Mother A Lonely Field”, covers of Dylan, Lou Reed and Van Morrison, and a “Main Travelled Roads” version that surpasses the original. Verdict: very positive, Leven as a rousing performer. With complete track list.

2009-07-03-dalane-tidende-jackie-leven-d.kurz: Profile in the festival programme of the Visefestivalen in Egersund (section “Dalane Brygghus”). Aalbu strings together the Leven legends, expressly as hearsay (“etter sigende”): the first pupil in Scotland to be expelled from school for drug possession; Doll by Doll shortly before the breakthrough; in 1984 on the…
inhalt: Profile in the festival programme of the Visefestivalen in Egersund (section “Dalane Brygghus”). Aalbu strings together the Leven legends, expressly as hearsay (“etter sigende”): the first pupil in Scotland to be expelled from school for drug possession; Doll by Doll shortly before the breakthrough; attacked in 1984 on the way home from the studio and kicked in the larynx; a doctor is said to have prescribed him anabolic steroids, which led him to heroin and into deep depression; exit with a method he developed himself, including Chinese acupuncture, founding of a detox clinic and of The Core Trust; his girlfriend ran off with the Dalai Lama's bodyguard. In 1994 the comeback with *The Mystery of Love…* (with Mike Scott and Robert Bly), plus his own whisky “Leven’s Lament”, which Salman Rushdie is said to have recommended in the booklet. As highlights of the discography he apparently names *Fairy Tales for Hard Men*, *Creatures of Light and Darkness* and *Shining Brother Shining Sister* (titles garbled in the OCR). Live spartan with acoustic guitar, on record opulent and Celtic-masculine.

2009-07-06-dalane-tidende-fantastisk-his.kurz: Positive short review of the concert at Dalane Brygghus during the Visefestivalen Egersund (early July 2009): Leven is a big man in more than one sense, whom life has knocked about; through his stories the audience took part in his life and cheered.
inhalt: Positive short review of the concert at Dalane Brygghus during the Visefestivalen Egersund (early July 2009): Leven is a big man in more than one sense, whom life has knocked about; through his stories the audience took part in his life and cheered. He tells tall tales – for instance that he was thrown out of Alicia Keys's limousine, and that he finally wrote a hymn to Johnny Cash, whom he had hated for years – and talks about sex, booze and a long life in the music business. The songs are rough, about ravens and the theft of urban souls.

2009-07-07-varden-buen-og-leven-gi-ut-pl.kurz: Report on the premiere of the “Bestillingsverket” by Knut Buen and Leven at the Kongsberg Jazz Festival (Thursday, 02.07.2009, Christians Kjeller) with an outlook: there is to be a joint record and at least one further concert, this time in Tuddal.
inhalt: Report on the premiere of the “Bestillingsverket” by Knut Buen and Leven at the Kongsberg Jazz Festival (Thursday, 02.07.2009, Christians Kjeller) with an outlook: there is to be a joint record and at least one further concert, this time in Tuddal. The idea came from blues/folk enthusiast Jon Gjerde. The two wanted to be announced as “two old codgers from Scotland and Telemark”; Leven told anecdotes between songs, Buen opened with a poem reading in his birth town. Buen says he had to develop a Hardingfele base layer specially for Leven's songs; the two worked for a few days at the hotel in Tuddal on rhythm and tone. He praises Leven as a “skinnende poet” and would like to continue the collaboration. Programme: springar, gangar, folk tunes and songs, joined by the “red thread of love”. Photo: Fredrik Pedersen.

2009-07-24-gaesteliste-the-haunted-year-.kurz: Short review of the reissue of two Haunted Valley CDs with live recordings from Brighton and Yorkshire, guests such as David Thomas, many unfamiliar stories and some studio rarities.
inhalt: Short review of the reissue of two Haunted Valley CDs with live recordings from Brighton and Yorkshire, guests such as David Thomas, many unfamiliar stories and some studio rarities. Maurer notes that the Haunted Valley no longer exists. Verdict: solid, above all for collectors.

2009-07-25-record-collector-troubadour-h.kurz: Kris Needs exposes the supposed “recently deceased eccentric drinker” Sir Vincent Lone, whose three albums were said to have been available only in a London coffee house, as Leven “in fanciful mood”.
inhalt: Kris Needs exposes the supposed “recently deceased eccentric drinker” Sir Vincent Lone, whose three albums were said to have been available only in a London coffee house, as Leven “in fanciful mood”. For Doll by Doll fans he singles out the new acoustic version of *An Honest Woman* (originally a 12" B-side, live highlight), also *Florin/Tweed*, *His Arms Are Full Of Broken Things* and the Bert Jansch cover *Strolling Down The Highway*. The album ends with a guest piece by Leven's friend Chris Conway. Verdict: very positive, Leven as a “greatly-underrated talent”.

2009-07-30-the-skinny-sir-vincent-lone-t.kurz: Short review of the third Lone album: Leven “kills” his pseudonym and thereby presents a “posthumous” album that is better than the usual estate retrospectives.
inhalt: Short review of the third Lone album: Leven “kills” his pseudonym and thereby presents a “posthumous” album that is better than the usual estate retrospectives. The reduced production suits the legend of Lone as a regular at London's Troubadour Coffee House (example: Bert Jansch's *Strolling Down The Highway*). The highlight is *Rove On Wraith Of Raith*, in which Ian Rankin is mentioned by name. Very positive verdict: “A fine epitaph.”

2009-07-netrhythms-haunted-year-summer.kurz: Davies describes the two live recordings (Black Horse, Otley; The Greys, Brighton) as dominated by Leven's between-song announcements – on *Barefoot Days* there is room for only six songs, but there are anecdotes, for example about an encounter with Joni Mitchell.
inhalt: Davies describes the two live recordings (Black Horse, Otley; The Greys, Brighton) as dominated by Leven's between-song announcements – on *Barefoot Days* there is room for only six songs, but there are anecdotes, for example about an encounter with Joni Mitchell. On the second CD he singles out “Down by the River” with guest singer David Thomas (Pere Ubu) and regrets that the duet “You've Lost That Loving Feeling” announced in the press release is missing. Friendly tenor, stories “fascinating”, no rating.

2009-08-03-musicomh-barefoot-days-deep-i.kurz: Three out of five stars. Oliver praises the new studio title song “Barefoot Days” and calls Leven a criminally overlooked songwriter; *Deep in the Heart of Nowhere* reproduces a typical Leven concert more completely, but flows less convincingly.
inhalt: Three out of five stars. Oliver praises the new studio title song “Barefoot Days” and calls Leven a criminally overlooked songwriter; *Deep in the Heart of Nowhere* reproduces a typical Leven concert more completely, but flows less convincingly. Conclusion: Leven is a live attraction because nothing seems rehearsed.

2009-09-11-gaesteliste-sir-vincent-lone-.kurz: Maurer declares Sir Vincent Lone “dead”: the alter ego has served its purpose, since Cooking Vinyl goes along with three or four Leven albums a year anyway; musically Lone does not differ from Leven.
inhalt: Maurer declares Sir Vincent Lone “dead”: the alter ego has served its purpose, since Cooking Vinyl goes along with three or four Leven albums a year anyway; musically Lone does not differ from Leven. The third Lone album, previously available only at concerts, is a good interim album with humorous “instant Leven classics”, acoustic material and live recordings. Verdict: benevolent.

2009-11-30-diskoryxeion-jackie-leven-gre.kurz: Short blog entry: reproduces Leven's English booklet note on “Greek Notebook” (1999) and adds two Greek sentences – fans of the rare acid-folk album “Control” (here: Movieplay 1975) would find Leven's Greek connection in “Greek Notebook”; a significant artist to be discovered.
inhalt: Short blog entry: reproduces Leven's English booklet note on “Greek Notebook” (1999) and adds two Greek sentences – fans of the rare acid-folk album “Control” (here: Movieplay 1975) would find Leven's Greek connection in “Greek Notebook”; a significant artist to be discovered.

2009-11-netrhythms-haunted-year-autumn.kurz: Review of the final instalment of the *Haunted Year* series. Davies describes *Greek Notebook* as 33 sketches (“Island”) from Walkman recordings made over seven years on Astypalea – interesting as an insight into the working process, more for completists.
inhalt: Review of the final instalment of the *Haunted Year* series. Davies describes *Greek Notebook* as 33 sketches (“Island”) from Walkman recordings made over seven years on Astypalea – interesting as an insight into the working process, more for completists. *Only the Ocean Can Forgive* mixes studio and German live recordings (including from the “Acoustic Stories” tour of 2003, “Sting's Dead” as a ten-minute narrative) and ends with “Barefoot Days” from the Haunted Valley Christmas party of 2002 with Joe Shaw and Kevin Hewick. Matter-of-fact and benevolent, no rating.

2009-12-06-record-collector-haunted-year.kurz: Needs describes *Greek Notebook* as Walkman sketches from a remote Greek island – perhaps the most unconventional item in Leven's catalogue, but a fascinating glimpse into the creative process.
inhalt: Needs describes *Greek Notebook* as Walkman sketches from a remote Greek island – perhaps the most unconventional item in Leven's catalogue, but a fascinating glimpse into the creative process. *Only the Ocean Can Forgive* combines live recordings from 2004 and comic monologues (“Sting's Dead”) with three studio pieces; the series ends “on a major high”.

2009-george-yefchak-njaca-corrections-qu.kurz: Troyanovich introduces Leven to an audience from the American correctional system. The piece appears in the newsletter of the New Jersey chapter of the American Correctional Association, Volume 3, Number 1, Spring/Summer 2009, on printed pages 18–19. It opens with the joint project with Ian…
inhalt: Troyanovich introduces Leven to an audience from the American correctional system. The piece appears in the newsletter of the New Jersey chapter of the American Correctional Association, Volume 3, Number 1, Spring/Summer 2009, on printed pages 18–19. It opens with the joint project with Ian Rankin and stresses that Leven is hardly known outside Europe.

The text combines a brief career outline with the CORE Trust and focuses particular attention on “Men in Prison”. Troyanovich describes the recording as a solo concert in Bergen prison and points to Leven's introductory words there about addiction and his own experiences. He also explains the reissue of the fan-club material in the series “The Haunted Year” and announces “Troubadour Heart”.

A further focus is the poetry worked into Leven's recordings. The author names numerous poets and recommends several albums as a starting point. For the collection the article is above all evidence of reception outside the usual music press: Leven is presented here through prison concerts, addiction support and poetry. It is not a scholarly study or an effectiveness evaluation of CORE; its biographical claims therefore gain no additional evidential weight.

2009-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-2009.kurz: Around 40 genuine entries. The trouble over *Live From A Cornish Pub In Germany* grows: several buyers report that their cheque was cashed in 2008 but the CD never arrived; in June one writes that it has been over a year, a Scottish fan has been waiting since Glenfarg for a paid-for, signed album and letter …
inhalt: Around 40 genuine entries. The trouble over *Live From A Cornish Pub In Germany* grows: several buyers report that their cheque was cashed in 2008 but the CD never arrived; in June one writes that it has been over a year, a Scottish fan has been waiting since Glenfarg for a paid-for, signed album and letter and comments on this with a Fife proverb. Alongside this, thanks for concerts in Essen and Bremen (February, with a question about the track list of an “official bootleg” from Hull 2009), Karlsruhe, Wallingford (Rugfest, June), Sidmouth (August), Milton Keynes (Stables, November, with four new songs) and Glenfarg; a 15-year-old Norwegian girl says she knows Leven through her father. A fan from Langholm recalls Leven's time in Carlisle, a woman from Wales her first concert in 1983 at London's Embassy Club and promotional badges from the manager of the time, a sound engineer from San Francisco writes that he mixed Doll by Doll live in the 1970s. A Kassel fan misses new columns, an Italian woman asks about the missing *Haunted Year* instalments “Summer” and “Autumn”, and in August people welcome Leven back after a “dark time”.

2009-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-leven-sa.titel: [Collected finds Nasjonalbiblioteket 2009: short notices, announcements, lists]

2009-vanguard-online-jackie-leven-interv.kurz: Long conversation, conducted in December 2008 before a concert at the pub The Roscoe in Leeds and published eight months later.
inhalt: Long conversation, conducted in December 2008 before a concert at the pub The Roscoe in Leeds and published eight months later. Leven says he is not getting anywhere in Britain, while in Germany things are going well. He lives from music, with outliers such as a royalty cheque for £10,000 because the Doll by Doll song “Soon New Life” became the radio song for births in South America (self-report). The publisher prevents him from re-recording old Doll by Doll songs. He describes Cooking Vinyl as a former “scavenging label” that has become a real label. Sir Vincent Lone sells better in Britain than Jackie Leven; Vince albums are cheaply produced “diffusion Jackie albums”, whereas Scandinavia and Germany expect high production values. Further topics: his sound engineer David Lynch, weaker songs on records, Lovers At The Gun Club as the end point of a sound, politics (Leven calls himself a socialist, brought up in the “communist” mining districts of Fife, Young Communists), songs about broken men as healing, 100 to 120 concerts a year, Scottish identity, Wetherspoon pubs as gathering places for lonely exiled Scots, poetry, the philosopher Charlie Martin, listening habits (Roland Kirk, Stephen Isserlis, Vaughan Williams) and a planned song “I Love Chet Baker When He Sings”.

2010-01-20-sentireascoltare-only-the-oce.kurz: Review of the double CD from the “Haunted Year” series (release date according to the page 01.12.2009): three studio tracks (including “Autumn Song”) and six live tracks from Cologne and Frankfurt 2003, including “Barefoot Days” with Kevin Hewick and Joe Shaw; the second CD gathers Walkman sketches from the Greek islands.
inhalt: Review of the double CD from the “Haunted Year” series (release date according to the page 01.12.2009): three studio tracks (including “Autumn Song”) and six live tracks from Cologne and Frankfurt 2003, including “Barefoot Days” with Kevin Hewick and Joe Shaw; the second CD gathers Walkman sketches from the Greek islands. Turra places Leven between British folk and early Leonard Cohen and calls his cult status “undeserved”. Rating 7/10.

2010-02-24-telegraph-blogs-the-rock-star.kurz: Blog entry by Telegraph rock critic Neil McCormick after Leven's concert at London's Slaughtered Lamb to launch Gothic Road (February 2010).
inhalt: Blog entry by Telegraph rock critic Neil McCormick after Leven's concert at London's Slaughtered Lamb to launch Gothic Road (February 2010). McCormick calls Leven “Britain's lost rock star” and the most talented singer-songwriter who never became a household name, and lists the stations of his life (expulsion over drugs, Doll by Doll, attack, heroin, CORE Trust with Diana). The core is an anecdote Leven told on stage (McCormick stresses that Leven is not always a reliable narrator): in October 2009 Leven accompanied Ralph McTell to his honouring by the All Party Folk Music Group in the House of Commons; there Prime Minister Gordon Brown, Leven's schoolmate from Kirkcaldy, persistently asked McTell whether “Streets of London” should not be called “Streets of Paris” for economic reasons, and praised the situation of the homeless under New Labour. Leven calls Brown a “political hero”. Note on the duet with McTell (“Cornelius Whalen”) on Gothic Road (release 4 April 2010) and listening recommendations from Gypsy Blood to Troubadour Heart.

2010-04-02-gaesteliste-gothic-road.kurz: Positive review: a “very solid Jackie classic” about the path of life (and of death), with specific pieces such as “Cornelius Whalen”, “Tilda Swinton” and “Mini Bar”, a guest appearance by Leven's old idol Ralph McTell and Cosgrave also on flute.
inhalt: Positive review: a “very solid Jackie classic” about the path of life (and of death), with specific pieces such as “Cornelius Whalen”, “Tilda Swinton” and “Mini Bar”, a guest appearance by Leven's old idol Ralph McTell and Cosgrave also on flute. Big Euro-pop melodic arcs compensate for the “aimless, bluesy noodling” of the last records; Leven returns to his Celtic-melancholic roots.

2010-04-08-word-magazine-blog-jackie-lev.kurz: “Fangie” has admired Leven since a Doll by Doll gig in a Manchester pub in 1982 and calls him his “Great Lost Superstar” of British music; he recommends *Fairy Tales for Hard Men*, *The Mystery of Love*, *Shining Brother Shining Sister* and *Control*.
inhalt: “Fangie” has admired Leven since a Doll by Doll gig in a Manchester pub in 1982 and calls him his “Great Lost Superstar” of British music; he recommends *Fairy Tales for Hard Men*, *The Mystery of Love*, *Shining Brother Shining Sister* and *Control*. Six replies name *The Haunted Year – Winter*, the Rankin audiobook from the Queen's Hall, *Defending Ancient Springs* and the new *Gothic Road*; one reader describes how Leven turned up before a gig with a thick wad of notes “about things I could talk about” and did not use them, and relates a stage story about a jealous boyfriend in front of the television.

2010-04-09-haugesunds-avis-jackie-leven-.titel: [Interview and concert report: Jackie Leven at Dikselen, Haugesund] (picture caption “Opp fra rennesteinen”)
2010-04-09-haugesunds-avis-jackie-leven-.kurz: Conversation and short report on the previous evening's performance (08.04.2010) at the Haugesund venue Dikselen, the opening of the 2010 Norway tour. Leven played material from the just-released *Gothic Road* as well as older songs such as “Big Tears” to a “conscious and marginal” audience.
inhalt: Conversation and short report on the previous evening's performance (08.04.2010) at the Haugesund venue Dikselen, the opening of the 2010 Norway tour. Leven played material from the just-released *Gothic Road* as well as older songs such as “Big Tears” to a “conscious and marginal” audience. The author recalls that The Pogues had played at the same venue in 1984, with Elvis Costello as sound engineer.

Leven says he travels through Norway to see the country; friends in London hardly dared leave the city. People envied him his “interesting life” – a misunderstanding, he says; his life has something “cinematically bad” about it. He describes his audience as people who think for themselves and do not let a lifestyle be sold to them; in England many young people come. The article summarises his biography (Doll by Doll 1978–1982 without mainstream success; friendship and collaboration with Ian Rankin, Glen Matlock and Frank Black) and describes the mugging on his way home from the studio during work on his first solo album: two years without a voice, mental problems, isolation and heroin. Leven partly takes the blame on himself, in his own account – he had been drunk and had walked alone despite the engineers' warning; he grew up because of it. About his label he says that indie companies are no better than others and dropped him without hesitation, so he must have done something right. *Gothic Road* is presented as his 16th solo album; Dagbladet's critic Fredrik Wandrup gave it five pips.
zitate_kontext: Leven on the myth of his life.

2010-04-10-itromso-jackie-leven-pa-basta.kurz: Announcement of the concert on Wednesday, 14.04.2010, at Bastard Bar, Tromsø. Head of bookings Egon Holstad praises the voice, guitar playing and storytelling of the “Scottish friend”, which he says make even stand-up comedians look pale; on his last visit to Tromsø Leven had enchanted the audience alone on a large stage as the support act for Madrugada on their farewell tour, while the intimate Bastard will be something quite different.
inhalt: Announcement of the concert on Wednesday, 14.04.2010, at Bastard Bar, Tromsø. Head of bookings Egon Holstad praises the voice, guitar playing and storytelling of the “Scottish friend”, which he says make even stand-up comedians look pale; on his last visit to Tromsø Leven had enchanted the audience alone on a large stage as the support act for Madrugada on their farewell tour, while the intimate Bastard will be something quite different.

2010-04-11-rocktimes-gothic-road.kurz: Song-by-song review: an opening with a German satnav announcement, “Cornelius Whalen” (about the last surviving participant of the 1936 Jarrow March) with Ralph McTell, “Song for Bass Guitar and Death” with Deborah Greenwood, and a German captain's announcement before “Hotel Mini Bar”.
inhalt: Song-by-song review: an opening with a German satnav announcement, “Cornelius Whalen” (about the last surviving participant of the 1936 Jarrow March) with Ralph McTell, “Song for Bass Guitar and Death” with Deborah Greenwood, and a German captain's announcement before “Hotel Mini Bar”. Verdict: typically quirky, more relaxed, and an acquired taste even for fans; the reviewer declines to give a rating, saying the album needs time to work.

2010-04-13-haugesunds-avis-gothic-road.titel: Jackie Leven: «Gothic Road» (review in the column “Et hode foran”)
2010-04-13-haugesunds-avis-gothic-road.kurz: Very positive review (“Sterkt”): Leven has become an elegant gentleman “with several ghosts in the closet”, an eternal outsider like his contemporaries John Cooper Clarke and Billy Childish.
inhalt: Very positive review (“Sterkt”): Leven has become an elegant gentleman “with several ghosts in the closet”, an eternal outsider like his contemporaries John Cooper Clarke and Billy Childish. *Gothic Road* is described as a “blue record with black humour”, personal but not self-pitying; the review praises big guitar parts, plain bluesy-jazzy rhythms and the bright, present voice. Highlights: “Song for Bass Guitar and Death”, “My Lost Blonde”, “Hotel Mini Bar”; allusions to Ian Curtis, Joan Crawford and Dolly Parton.

2010-04-13-laagendalsposten-leven-og-bue.titel: [Preview:] Nå samles Jackie Leven og Knut Buen igjen (subheadings “Ny duo”, “Felesjef”)
2010-04-13-laagendalsposten-leven-og-bue.kurz: The Kongsberg local newspaper reports that the Leven/Knut Buen duo, which premiered with a sold-out concert at the Kongsberg Jazz Festival 2009 (photo: performance in the backyard of “Christians …”), will perform together again at Bergenfest 2010: the concert on the Småscenen of Den Nationale Scene is divided into three parts – Leven solo, Leven and Buen together, Buen solo.
