2010-04-15-karmsund-skotsk-morkemann.kurz: Portrait with quotations from conversation after Leven's concert at Dikselen, Haugesund, the previous week (08.04.2010).
inhalt: Portrait with quotations from conversation after Leven's concert at Dikselen, Haugesund, the previous week (08.04.2010). Sørhus introduces him as “Scotland's answer to Van Morrison”, who turns sixty in 2010. Leven says (in his own account) that Bergen was the first city in which he performed as a professional musician: at 16, in 1966, he toured with the American gospel/blues singer Doris Henderson, and Bergen was the first stop; he recalls arriving through the fjord and the stench of a fish-processing plant, but says he fell in love with Norway at once – the people had the same “madness” as the Scots. One of his favourite poets was Olav H. Hauge, so it was exciting to be close to his home region.

On the origin of “Rainy Day Bergen Women” he says he was woken in Bergen by coughing in the next room, looked out on the rainy street full of hurrying women and wrote the song in half an hour; his father had just died, and it was his first song about his death. In Haugesund some had taken him for an “old punk” and expected punk songs. He loves the studio because he is “incredibly good” in it, but the record company only allows an album every 18 months – hence the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone.

2010-04-20-romerikes-blad-leven-leverer-.kurz: Positive short review: “Scotland's best-known Gypsy” has been delivering high-quality records since Doll by Doll in the late 1970s; after nearly dying in a street fight in the mid-1980s he fought his way back.
inhalt: Positive short review: “Scotland's best-known Gypsy” has been delivering high-quality records since Doll by Doll in the late 1970s; after nearly dying in a street fight in the mid-1980s he fought his way back. On *Gothic Road* (12 tracks, 52:25) Ralph McTell, Michael Cosgrave, Kevin Foster and David Wrench take part; Leven remains rooted in folk and song traditions and delivers impressive lyrics. Highlights: “Absolutely Joan Crawford”, “Song for Bass Guitar and Death”, “John Paul Getty's Silver Cadillac”.

2010-04-21-dalane-tidende-jackie-leven-t.titel: [Preview: Jackie Leven back in Egersund – concert at Grand Kjelleren for Verdens bokdag]
2010-04-21-dalane-tidende-jackie-leven-t.kurz: Large preview of the concert on Friday, 23.04.2010, at Grand Kjelleren in Egersund, organised by the Egersund Visefestival in cooperation with World Book Day (Leven performs after a Bokkafé).
inhalt: Large preview of the concert on Friday, 23.04.2010, at Grand Kjelleren in Egersund, organised by the Egersund Visefestival in cooperation with World Book Day (Leven performs after a Bokkafé). Festival director Henning Feyling says Leven felt so comfortable at the festival in summer 2009 – he gave two concerts at Dalane Brygghus, with people standing all the way down the stairs – that he was determined to come back; after the Trondheim concert on Tuesday he will travel down and spend two free days in Egersund. It is the first time the festival has put on a concert outside its July dates, as a test of the mood; the summer programme (including Hanne Boel, Steve Wynn) was to be handed out at the concert. Feyling points to Dagbladet's review, which proclaimed Leven “Scotland's dark master singer” and gave *Gothic Road* five pips.

Aalbu, who by his own account has been to nine or ten Leven concerts (including Stavanger, Bryne), adds a personally coloured portrait: Leven tells so many tall stories that fact and fiction blur; this is followed by the familiar biographical stations (Romani descent, expelled from school for drugs, Doll by Doll, the 1984 mugging with a kick to the larynx, steroids, heroin, depression, self-treatment including Chinese acupuncture, a rehab clinic and the Core Trust, comeback in 1994 with Mike Scott and Robert Bly), the whisky “Leven's Lament” with a Salman Rushdie recommendation in the booklet, and Leven's quirky song titles. Leven is at least as interesting between the songs as when singing, comparable to Van Morrison, Scott Walker and John Martyn. A side column is devoted to his old shorts, always the same ones.
zitate_kontext: on the blurriness of his biography (start of sentence).

2010-04-21-nordlys-stodig-fra-leven.kurz: “Bunnsolid”: Leven is among the most remarkable living lyricists, literary and full of pop-culture references, never showing off.
inhalt: “Bunnsolid”: Leven is among the most remarkable living lyricists, literary and full of pop-culture references, never showing off. He masters existentialist darkness (“Gothic Road”, “Last of the Badmen”) just as well as quirky everyday observations from touring life (“Hotel Mini Bar”) and humour – “Absolutely Joan Crawford (With a Bit of Tilda Swinton on the Side)” is priceless. Objection: it too rarely really sparks; craftsmanship, production and the voice, which sounds of old whisky and lived life, nevertheless make the album a good buy.

2010-04-22-chicago-reader-a-cult-artists.kurz: One of the few North American articles about Leven, published for the US release of Gothic Road (Vol.
inhalt: One of the few North American articles about Leven, published for the US release of Gothic Road (Vol. 39 No. 31 of the Chicago Reader). The critic Cliff Doerksen, who comes from Winnipeg, recounts how Doll by Doll found a small following in his home town in 1979 and defends the first three albums (Remember, Gypsy Blood, Doll by Doll) as the greatest lost rock albums; Grand Passion falls short. From the liner notes of the 2007 Rhino reissues he quotes that John Peel and Paul Morley loathed the band. Discovering the UbuDoll project with David Thomas (2000) led him to Leven's solo work; he considers Leven possibly the most underrated living songwriter. Gothic Road is the 13th solo studio album since 1994; mentioned are Chip Pan Fire, collaborations with Johnny Dowd, Ron Sexsmith and Ian Rankin, and a quotation from David Thomas from the DVD The Meeting of Remarkable Men (2004). Leven talks about touring (formerly 200 days a year, now fewer), about the genre label, and about the fact that lack of attention sometimes makes him angry but that he made his choice.

2010-04-22-karmsund-gothic-road.kurz: Positive review: the “friend of Norway”, with a new release every eighteen months plus collaborations and bootlegs, is one of Britain's most industrious artists.
inhalt: Positive review: the “friend of Norway”, with a new release every eighteen months plus collaborations and bootlegs, is one of Britain's most industrious artists. Above all he is an outstanding storyteller whose lyrics balance on the very edge of poetry, delivered in a deep voice with sharp humour. Mentioned are the Russian choir (brothers of Kursk victims), Ralph McTell and “Hotel Mini Bar” about the loneliness of touring life; “John Paul Getty's Silver Cadillac” is a classic Leven narrative that grips even after many plays.

2010-04-29-drammens-tidende-skotsk-pa-bu.kurz: Preview of Leven's appearance at the “lyttekonserter” at Buddy Scene in Drammen, conducted by Johnny Andreassen (who had already done the Fremtiden interview in 1995).
inhalt: Preview of Leven's appearance at the “lyttekonserter” at Buddy Scene in Drammen, conducted by Johnny Andreassen (who had already done the Fremtiden interview in 1995). Leven raves (in his own account) that Drammen is “the holiday I always look forward to”, while many concerts around the world are thankless: the “wonderful Margrethe” (promoter Margrethe Berg), walks over the bridge from the hotel, a town with growing self-confidence and Buddy's unique soul. Berg had to close the door at his concerts every time and send latecomers home.

Leven tells how the album title *Gothic Road* came about: after a wild evening he woke up on all fours on his stone kitchen floor, on which he had written “Something Gothic” with a felt-tip pen; his wife was away, the word would not scrub off, and in the process he heard himself say the phrase that became the title. He also declares his support for Gordon Brown, who he says saved England from economic ruin; they went to school together, and he was present at the rugby game in which Brown lost the sight in one eye. A song about the Jarrow protest march is mentioned (“1938” in the paper). In Norway, *Gothic Road* received fives and sixes on the dice.

2010-04-netrhythms-gothic-road.kurz: Davies explains the album concept of the two roads (Royal Road and Road of Poverty and Death) and considers it possibly “poetic smoke and mirrors”.
inhalt: Davies explains the album concept of the two roads (Royal Road and Road of Poverty and Death) and considers it possibly “poetic smoke and mirrors”. He lists the many pop-culture allusions (Ian Curtis, Dylan, the “Jolene” melody in “Last of the Badmen”), the duet number “Cornelius Whalen” with Ralph McTell about the last Jarrow marcher and the closing piece “Island” by co-producer David Wrench. Benevolent, ironically pointed tenor without rating; closing punchline with the comparison to schoolmate Gordon Brown.

2010-06-13-david-belbin-jackie-leven.kurz: “Song of the Week” piece by the writer David Belbin for Leven's 60th birthday. He recounts how he saw Doll by Doll around 1979 at the Ad Lib Club in Nottingham after buying the debut *Remember*: the DJ had played the ballad *Janice* five times before the performance, so the band out of spite did not play it; the concert was harder than any punk band (“Joy Division? Pah.”). Twenty years later he experienced Leven solo in the upstairs room of The Gladstone pub in Nottingham – with his falsetto lost, but a brilliant, earthy and self-mocking storyteller; afterwards Leven confirmed to him that the 1979 concert had been one of Doll by Doll's few good ones.
inhalt: “Song of the Week” piece by the writer David Belbin for Leven's 60th birthday. He recounts how he saw Doll by Doll around 1979 at the Ad Lib Club in Nottingham after buying the debut *Remember*: the DJ had played the ballad *Janice* five times before the performance, so the band out of spite did not play it; the concert was harder than any punk band (“Joy Division? Pah.”). Twenty years later he experienced Leven solo in the upstairs room of The Gladstone pub in Nottingham – with his falsetto lost, but a brilliant, earthy and self-mocking storyteller; afterwards Leven confirmed to him that the 1979 concert had been one of Doll by Doll's few good ones.

Since then he has been a big fan, attends every tour (including Summer Sundae, Derby in June 2010 with stories about Diz Disley, The Flowerpot) and praises the way the albums keep getting better. He repeats Leven's stories about the mugging, heroin, CORE and Princess Diana and remarks that Leven seems to have known an astonishing range of people, from Laurence Olivier to Ralph McTell (a guest on *Gothic Road*). In Derby, Leven spontaneously sang *Strip Show* in the style of Matt Monro. As a listening example he links *Poortoun* in the version from *Men in Prison* (one of the four live double albums of 2009).

2010-06-28-diskoryxeion-jackie-leven-ive.kurz: Blog post by the Greek critic Fontas Troussas: translates Leven's booklet note for “Greek Notebook” (seven years each May and September on Astypalea), recounts how, through the Korean reissue of “Control” (2002, Merry-Go-Round/Beatball, 500 LPs, with liner notes by Leven), he learned that John St. Field is Leven, and reviews “The Haunted Year / Spring” (Celtic Soulmen; The Stornoway Girls with Kevin Hewick, Dan Britton, Lee Allatson) and “Lovers At The Gun Club” (recorded in Wales, one of his most “American” albums, with a Kenneth Patchen setting and a David Childers song). Overall verdict: very positive. Mentions earlier Leven reviews on the blog and in “Jazz & Τζαζ”.

Overall verdict: very positive. Mentions earlier Leven reviews on the blog and in “Jazz & Τζαζ”.

2010-09-22-kindamuzik-jackie-leven-parad.kurz: Review of the concert of 19.09.2010 in the Bovenzaal of the Paradiso, where Leven played before the US roots band Chatham County Line.
inhalt: Review of the concert of 19.09.2010 in the Bovenzaal of the Paradiso, where Leven played before the US roots band Chatham County Line. The reviewer describes “disgust, admiration and sympathy”: sympathy because the hall was not sold out and tickets went at half price on the night; admiration for the voice (compared with Tim Hardin and Aaron Neville) and guitar playing, accompanied by a musician on keyboard and melodica; disgust at the excessive use of “fuck” on stage. The set lasted about an hour, much of it anecdotes (including about Ralph McTell and David Childers); Leven refused encores with a dig at Robbie Williams. Overall verdict: mixed.

2010-12-01-bbc-radio-scotland-stark-talk.kurz: Roughly 26-minute conversational portrait from the BBC Radio Scotland series “Stark Talk” (BBC programme page: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00w68bh).
inhalt: Roughly 26-minute conversational portrait from the BBC Radio Scotland series “Stark Talk” (BBC programme page: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00w68bh). According to the BBC, broadcast on Wednesday, 1 December 2010 (15:30), repeated on 5 December 2010 and – “Another chance to hear … Jackie Leven, who died recently” – on 20 November 2011; no longer available from the BBC. The YouTube description dates the recording to November 2010 (presumably the month of recording; uploaded on 4.11.2014). Stark introduces Leven with Rankin's quip about the “Bob Dylan of Scotland”, Neil McCormick's praise for “Gypsy Blood” and the new album “Gothic Road”, and then works through his life chronologically: why fame failed to materialise (Leven says he avoids psychotherapy out of the superstitious fear of otherwise losing what is good in his writing), childhood in Leslie and Glenrothes as an outsider family, his mother's blues records, skipping school to be out in nature, the school librarian who slipped him Russian and American poetry, the gift of his first guitar and his own tuning. Next come fleeing a Glenrothes gang, years in Spain and Berlin, the Dorset squats, the London squat Bristol Gardens, Doll by Doll as “genuinely violent music”, LSD (Leven names Grof/Halifax's “The Human Encounter with Death” as his favourite book), tours with Hawkwind and Devo, both of whom threw the band off. Leven recounts the mugging after a studio session (almost strangled, around a year without a voice), depression, heroin as a painkiller, getting off it with five-element acupuncture, the founding of the CORE Trust and meeting Princess Diana, who at a charity lunch asked him to sing – for him the beginning of the comeback. The close: meeting Deborah Greenwood through a fan letter about “The Mystery of Love…”, the story about the girlfriend and the Dalai Lama's bodyguard, and the question of stadium fame, which he calmly dismisses. Overall verdict: a warm, humorous portrait; Leven as a self-mocking storyteller whose statements are throughout his own accounts.
zitate_kontext: Leven quotes Anna Kavan as a guiding principle.
his reply to Diana when she said he had once been a singer.

2010-cooking-vinyl-gothic-road-albumtext.titel: Jackie Leven [Artist page with album text “Gothic Road”]

2010-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-2010.kurz: Of roughly 190 entries this year only about 25 are genuine; from September 2010 spam entries flood the guestbook, and in November a fan expressly asks for the rubbish to be deleted.
inhalt: Of roughly 190 entries this year only about 25 are genuine; from September 2010 spam entries flood the guestbook, and in November a fan expressly asks for the rubbish to be deleted. The genuine entries praise *Gothic Road* (Ayr, Bar Libertine, March; Münster, Cologne, Italy), congratulate on the 60th birthday on 18.06. and thank for concerts in Berlin, Munich (16.05., with Michael Cosgrave), Egersund (April), Trowbridge (festival, with Michael Weston King in the tent), Wallingford (Rugfest), Stuttgart and Strathpeffer (22.11.). A fan recalls early 1980s appearances in London (Embassy Club, Hope & Anchor, Dingwalls, as “The Dead Sea Scouts”) and asks about the manager of the time; another refers to a Radio Scotland conversation with Edi Stark (autumn 2010). Still dominant: the never-delivered *Cornish Pub* CD (“nearly two years”), and a Kassel fan complains that columns and replies fail to appear.

2011-04-musikzirkus-magazin-jackie-leven.kurz: Schelle rates the DVD of the Bonn Crossroads performance of 26 March 2004 very positively. Besides Cosgrave he expressly names the bassist Kevin Foster and praises the dense, intimate performance as well as Leven's alternation between songs and stories.
inhalt: Schelle rates the DVD of the Bonn Crossroads performance of 26 March 2004 very positively. Besides Cosgrave he expressly names the bassist Kevin Foster and praises the dense, intimate performance as well as Leven's alternation between songs and stories.

2011-05-25-rocktimes-live-at-rockpalast.kurz: Review of the MIG DVD from the Rockpalast Crossroads series, recorded according to the text on 26.03.2004 at the Harmonie in Bonn with Michael Cosgrave and bassist Kevin Foster.
inhalt: Review of the MIG DVD from the Rockpalast Crossroads series, recorded according to the text on 26.03.2004 at the Harmonie in Bonn with Michael Cosgrave and bassist Kevin Foster. The reviewer, to whom Leven was previously unknown, praises the well-rehearsed, soulful performance and the stories, but criticises the stereo sound and short running time. Conclusion: musically good, a listen recommended.

2011-06-12-musikreviews-de-live-at-the-r.kurz: Enthusiastic review of the first regular live DVD (MIG, 25.04.2011): the Rockpalast performance at the Harmonie in Bonn in 2004 with Cosgrave and Kevin Foster, centred on three long songs from “Shining Brother Shining Sister”, with “Call Mother A Lonely Field” as the highlight.
inhalt: Enthusiastic review of the first regular live DVD (MIG, 25.04.2011): the Rockpalast performance at the Harmonie in Bonn in 2004 with Cosgrave and Kevin Foster, centred on three long songs from “Shining Brother Shining Sister”, with “Call Mother A Lonely Field” as the highlight. König describes the Celtic folk rock with melancholy, sarcasm and bawdy jokes, and jokingly mentions Leven's stage story that Sir Vincent Lone died in 2009 after a discussion about Wittgenstein and Kajagoogoo. The only drawback: a running time of 75 minutes. The comment thread contains memories from the editors Thoralf Koß (an hour's conversation with Leven) and König (two concerts), a reader's condolence of 15.11.2011 (“Jöhrschi”, 18 years of concert-going) and König's sharp criticism of the FAZ obituary of 17.11.2011.

2011-08-13-theartsdesk-edinburgh-fringe-.kurz: Graeme Thomson (later author of the official biography of 2021 and of the Telegraph portrait) describes Leven at a Fringe solo performance three months before his death: physically weakened, but with voice and guitar alone able to captivate a small room.
inhalt: Graeme Thomson (later author of the official biography of 2021 and of the Telegraph portrait) describes Leven at a Fringe solo performance three months before his death: physically weakened, but with voice and guitar alone able to captivate a small room. The stage show comes across as warmer than the albums, which of late were often produced in a cheap, synthetic manner. Between bawdy anecdotes (including about *Toy Story 3*, a Bay City Rollers badge and a Glasgow photo session) he repeatedly hit the mark, for example with “Exit Wound”, “Poortoun” and “Beware Soul Brother” from the forthcoming album, an elegy for a dead brother. Conclusion: a winning mixture of the sacred and the profane. No star rating for Leven.

2011-08-28-pennyblackmusic-jackie-leven-.kurz: Probably one of Leven's last interviews, by telephone shortly before the release of Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man, the joint record with the keyboard player Michael Cosgrave.
inhalt: Probably one of Leven's last interviews, by telephone shortly before the release of Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man, the joint record with the keyboard player Michael Cosgrave. Ben Howarth introduces Leven as a “cult artist's cult artist” (quoting Stewart Lee) and recounts how his father discovered Leven at the Canterbury Fayre festival before Willard Grant Conspiracy. Leven explains that the songs arose in German hotel rooms while waiting for soundchecks and were developed with Cosgrave at soundchecks; he normally records at the Welsh studio Bryn Derwen, this time at Cosgrave's studio on Dartmoor, where he deliberately gave Cosgrave free rein. He talks about Germany as his favourite country to tour, about the backgrounds of songs (“Townes at the Borderline” after an encounter with Townes Van Zandt, “Swine Fever Blues” after a bout of swine flu), about songs that are supposed to take shape only in the studio, about a fixed repertoire of stage stories and how true they are, about the “Official Bootlegs” – prompted by Cooking Vinyl so that he himself would earn from them – and about the “death” of Sir Vincent Lone. Guest tracks by other artists (here John Mayfield) are his principle. At the end: a meeting with Randy Newman after a concert in Bergen and the plan to carry on for at least another ten years.

2011-09-09-gaesteliste-wayside-shrines.kurz: Review of the last studio album: Cosgrave had a free hand this time (keyboards, accordion, tin whistle, percussion, co-composition), while Leven played only acoustic guitar and sang.
inhalt: Review of the last studio album: Cosgrave had a free hand this time (keyboards, accordion, tin whistle, percussion, co-composition), while Leven played only acoustic guitar and sang. It sounds like their joint concerts, hence the absence of bass and drums; songs about and from German hotel rooms, a poem set to music, a humorous Townes Van Zandt reference. Overall verdict: friendly and sober, “typical Leven fodder” – released two months before Leven's death.

2011-09-netrhythms-wayside-shrines-and-t.kurz: Detailed track-by-track review of the last studio album, which Leven recorded alone with Michael Cosgrave in the latter's studio on Dartmoor.
inhalt: Detailed track-by-track review of the last studio album, which Leven recorded alone with Michael Cosgrave in the latter's studio on Dartmoor. Davies considers the leaner album equal to *Lovers at the Gun Club* and *Fairytales for Hardmen*, and singles out “To Live and Die in Levenland”, “Townes at the Borderline” (a memory of Townes Van Zandt) and “Beware Soul Brother”, which he links with the death of Leven's younger brother. According to the accompanying text, the songs were written mostly in German hotel rooms. No star rating, clearly positive overall.

2011-11-08-word-magazine-blog-jackie-lev.kurz: The user “Bogart” (later also active in the Afterword) opens a thread on 08.11.2011: Leven is “very poorly in hospital”, and people are asked to collect stories and thoughts about him; he will hear about them and it may help him.
inhalt: The user “Bogart” (later also active in the Afterword) opens a thread on 08.11.2011: Leven is “very poorly in hospital”, and people are asked to collect stories and thoughts about him; he will hear about them and it may help him. He sketches the path from St Judas and John St. Field via Doll by Doll to solo artist and recalls that the Independent once called him Britain's “great lost popstar”. Over the following days around 17 users write: several discovered Leven through “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” on an Uncut cover CD; a reader from Nova Scotia says Leven cancelled an appointment there and calls him “Van Morrison with his inspiration intact”; a man from Birmingham, whose concert two weeks earlier had been cancelled and moved to early January, tells his “Wrapped Up In Blue” anecdote (the same as in the Afterword 2021/2024). “duco01” came to Leven through his songs for Kevin Coyne; asked whether he had ever sung with Coyne, Leven replied that he had preferred to sit in the audience, and he gave a young guitarist from the writer's family a guest-list place and advice.

On 13.11.2011, the day before the death, the user “Turner” copies a notice from Leven's website into the thread: Leven was gravely ill with cancer and had “only a few days to live”; the same biographical paragraph follows (“In a career stretching over forty years …”, with the error “solo resurgence through the 1980s”) that after the death stood on the obituary home page. From 15.11. words of farewell follow; at the end Bogart quotes a line from “Working Alone / A Blessing”.

2011-11-14-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-.kurz: They begin on the evening of 14.11.2011 (Brussels, Kassel) and peak on 15 and 16.11.; they are written from Scotland and England, Germany (Bochum, Lauterbach, Münster, Düsseldorf, Essen, Frankfurt, Hannover, Kiel, Krefeld, Bremen, Dresden), Norway (Egersund, Oslo, Trondheim, Drammen), Sweden, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Belgium, Northern Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and the USA, some in German. The tone is grief and gratitude for songs, voice, guitar playing and above all the stories; many drink to him (“white bar in Heaven”, “best bar in the sky”). Many only heard of it days or weeks later, and some did not know he had been ill.
inhalt: They begin on the evening of 14.11.2011 (Brussels, Kassel) and peak on 15 and 16.11.; they are written from Scotland and England, Germany (Bochum, Lauterbach, Münster, Düsseldorf, Essen, Frankfurt, Hannover, Kiel, Krefeld, Bremen, Dresden), Norway (Egersund, Oslo, Trondheim, Drammen), Sweden, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Belgium, Northern Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and the USA, some in German. The tone is grief and gratitude for songs, voice, guitar playing and above all the stories; many drink to him (“white bar in Heaven”, “best bar in the sky”). Many only heard of it days or weeks later, and some did not know he had been ill.

Alongside these are memories from people in his circle. Several write about the Doll by Doll period: visits to the band's squat in Maida Vale or “Clifton Villas” in 1979, where the band, with friends and crew, took in young fans; a man from Edinburgh remembers how Doll by Doll, as support for Hawkwind, raided their catering before Hawkwind walked past in capes and silver helmets; others mention concerts at the Blue Note in Derby (around 1980) and at Brollies, Richmond (around 1976?). The brother of a Doll by Doll musician announces that the latter will be at the funeral. Dan Britton, a member of the backing band The Stornoway Girls, thanks Leven for the collaboration and for including a song of his on *When The Bridegroom Comes*. A musician from Wakefield was proud to have stood on stage with Leven; a harmonica player recalls duo performances in Bournemouth and his contribution to “Uptown”; a reviewer says that Deborah Greenwood had already sent him *Control* for review in 1974. An old companion recalls a Norway tour in 1997 and the WOMAD performance on the day of Princess Diana's death, as well as the CORE years. Further traces: a concert in “your Kingdom of Fife” in March 2011 before 53 people, Robyn Hitchcock dedicated a song to Leven at a concert in Shoreditch, BBC Radio 4 featured him on 20.11. in *Last Word*, a Dutchman watches the 2004 Rockpalast recording, an Australian recalls performances in Sydney, at WOMADelaide, in the Barossa Valley and at WOMAD New Zealand.

2011-11-15-bbc-news-tributes-to-scottish.kurz: Short online report from the BBC regional newsroom: Leven died aged 61 after an illness with cancer.
inhalt: Short online report from the BBC regional newsroom: Leven died aged 61 after an illness with cancer. It mainly documents Twitter reactions from Ian Rankin, BBC Radio Scotland presenter Tom Morton (whisky “Leven's Lament”), Eddi Reader and Cooking Vinyl, and quotes at length the tribute that stood on Leven's official website shortly before his death (over 400 songs, “Call Mother” as his greatest song). Doll by Doll is – inaccurately – described as a punk band; the addiction charity is said to have been founded by Leven “with his wife”.

2011-11-15-bergensavisen-jackie-leven-er.kurz: Short death report (15.11.2011, 19.32): the “friend of Bergen” Leven died on Monday evening aged 61 after a long illness with cancer.
inhalt: Short death report (15.11.2011, 19.32): the “friend of Bergen” Leven died on Monday evening aged 61 after a long illness with cancer. It recalls many visits to Bergen, including at Bergenfest, and the 2003 concert for the inmates of Bergen Landsfengsel; the archive photo shows him at Bergenfest 2005. An older Leven quotation about his love for Bergen, its surroundings and its women, and the similarity to the Scottish atmosphere, closes the text.

2011-11-15-caught-by-the-river-caught-by.kurz: Mick Houghton, who in 1978 was responsible for Doll by Doll in the press department of Warner Bros and in 1994 again worked as Leven's press man, remembers on the day after the death.
inhalt: Mick Houghton, who in 1978 was responsible for Doll by Doll in the press department of Warner Bros and in 1994 again worked as Leven's press man, remembers on the day after the death. The first meeting in spring 1978 with Leven and Jo Shaw, both visibly on LSD, the concert at the tiny Rock Garden before a handful of onlookers and interviews with the music press (Hugh Fielder of Sounds; Shaw walked out of an interview in a fish-and-chip shop in Burton upon Trent without a word) paint a picture of a band that intimidated its audience rather than merely threatening it, as punk did. Houghton describes the concept: making the suffering of the soul public, benefit concerts for R. D. Laing's Philadelphia Association instead of Rock Against Racism, flyers and Artaud pictures, plus the aborted NME cover story with Nick Kent. After the debut Remember his involvement ended; in 1994 he worked again with the now gentler Leven on two albums. At the end comes the Dylan story (alleged train journey Berlin–Saint Petersburg in 1988, song after “One Too Many Mornings”), which Houghton never believed. Overall tone: affectionately ironic, Leven as a lovable rogue.

2011-11-15-classic-rock-jackie-leven-die.kurz: The short report tells of Leven's death at the age of 61 and his preceding illness with cancer.
inhalt: The short report tells of Leven's death at the age of 61 and his preceding illness with cancer. It recalls Doll by Doll and characterises his solo career since 1994 through his soul-inflected singing and dramatic storytelling.

2011-11-15-cooking-vinyl-jackie-leven-ju.kurz: The label's official obituary, published the day after the death. It begins with the same sentence as the obituary home page of jackieleven.co.uk (death on Monday, 14 November, “at 8 o'clock in the evening”, cancer) and the same Leven quotation about “spiritual” and “soulful” storytellers.
inhalt: The label's official obituary, published the day after the death. It begins with the same sentence as the obituary home page of jackieleven.co.uk (death on Monday, 14 November, “at 8 o'clock in the evening”, cancer) and the same Leven quotation about “spiritual” and “soulful” storytellers. A detailed account of his life follows: birth in Kirkcaldy, outsider childhood in Glenrothes (father “Irish Cockney”, mother from Newcastle, Romany background), essay prize and expulsion from school for drugs, marriage at 16, rocket factory, driven out by a gang at 17, wandering years (farm work, Berlin, Kerry, Madrid with *Control*), Doll by Doll (four albums, the last with David Gilmour, split in 1983), solo contract with Charisma/Virgin, the mugging in Market Street in Islington (strangled and injured in the throat), loss of the falsetto, several years of heroin, getting clean with five-element acupuncture and “psychic healing”, CORE Trust; from 1994 *Songs From The Argyll Cycle* and *The Mystery Of Love…*, then 24 further albums, *Jackie Leven Said* with Ian Rankin, Ubudoll with David Thomas, Leven's Lament (bottled by Islay Mist), annual walks, five albums in 2009 (Haunted Valley double and Sir Vincent Lone), *Gothic Road* and *Wayside Shrines* with Michael Cosgrave, which Martin Goldschmidt considers the best since *The Mystery Of Love*. Close: Leven's description of *Wayside Shrines* as a “homeopathic record”.

2011-11-15-musikkbloggen-jackie-leven-19.kurz: Short obituary from the Norwegian music blog on the day after Leven's death (14.11.2011, at 20:00 according to the text).
inhalt: Short obituary from the Norwegian music blog on the day after Leven's death (14.11.2011, at 20:00 according to the text). Letrud calls him a tragically overlooked songwriter who was in Norway several times and had a loyal audience there; he himself came to Leven through Ian Rankin's Rebus novels. A brief career outline (*Control* as John St. Field, Doll by Doll, around 40 solo albums including fan-club releases), a reference to the obituary at The Arts Desk and an embedded video (“Empty in Soho Square”). No comments.

2011-11-15-nickchurchill-org-uk-remember.kurz: The Dorset journalist Nick Churchill published a short obituary on the day of the death (blog post of 15.11.2011, updated 2016) and documented beneath it three interviews he had done with Leven for the Bournemouth Echo.
inhalt: The Dorset journalist Nick Churchill published a short obituary on the day of the death (blog post of 15.11.2011, updated 2016) and documented beneath it three interviews he had done with Leven for the Bournemouth Echo. In the obituary he recalls a performance before about 30 people in the skittle alley of his village pub in Dorset (Bere Regis), near the farm where Leven once lived.

- **May 2006** (before a concert at Club Hobo, Bournemouth, 20 May, with Joe Shaw): Leven on former places of residence (Westbourne, Parkstone, Corfe Mullen), a “lifetime lack of achievement award”, the Q Awards, a major German prize with a string-quartet arrangement of “St Judas”, a planned album of songs by Judee Sill and Lightnin' Hopkins, and the Doll by Doll reissues, which hinged on Warner having lost the legal papers.
- **October 2008** (Lovers At The Gun Club, concert at the Opera House): Leven would like to produce Amy Winehouse; explanations of “Fareham Confidential” (drum loop from “Ruby Don't Take Your Love to Town”), of his relationship with Cooking Vinyl and of his Dorset years (farmhouse near Blandford after Control).
- **March 2010** (Gothic Road): Leven on a feared schoolmate, on Gordon Brown, whom he supports, the concept of the “two roads” behind the album title, Ralph McTell and the Jarrow March, the dedication to the musician Tim Mycroft from Blandford.

2011-11-15-rolling-stone-de-jackie-leven.kurz: Short death report: Leven died on Monday evening at eight o'clock in “Southhampton”. Introduced with Leven's well-known quotation about spiritual and soulful storytellers (translated into German, probably based on the obituary home page of jackieleven.co.uk).
inhalt: Short death report: Leven died on Monday evening at eight o'clock in “Southhampton”. Introduced with Leven's well-known quotation about spiritual and soulful storytellers (translated into German, probably based on the obituary home page of jackieleven.co.uk). Refers to the last album with Michael Cosgrave as a collection of dark songs about illness, hallucinations and death. Photo: Cooking Vinyl.

2011-11-15-spiegel-online-songwriter-jac.kurz: Short obituary from the Hamburg editorial office on the day after the death (15.11.2011, 17:27). It names heroin addiction, alcohol, delusion, depression and longing as Leven's main themes, describes him as a “colossus” with a filigree voice and places him in the tradition of Johnny Cash (prison live album in Norway, “Elegy for Johnny Cash” 2005).
inhalt: Short obituary from the Hamburg editorial office on the day after the death (15.11.2011, 17:27). It names heroin addiction, alcohol, delusion, depression and longing as Leven's main themes, describes him as a “colossus” with a filigree voice and places him in the tradition of Johnny Cash (prison live album in Norway, “Elegy for Johnny Cash” 2005). Mentions the last album, released in September, which was partly written “in hotel rooms here”, and that Leven had loyal fans in Germany and toured regularly. Overall tone: respectful, brief.
zitate_kontext: on the importance of the German market.

2011-11-15-the-guardian-jackie-leven-obi.kurz: The most important British newspaper obituary, written by the Guardian folk and world music critic Robin Denselow, who had known Leven since the late 1970s and had interviewed him himself in 1988.
inhalt: The most important British newspaper obituary, written by the Guardian folk and world music critic Robin Denselow, who had known Leven since the late 1970s and had interviewed him himself in 1988. Denselow calls Leven a brilliant outsider with a loyal cult following but without the success he deserved. He sketches the background in Kirkcaldy (Roma descent, in Leven's own account), the early marriage at 16, the wandering years as a labourer and the stage name John St Field. Doll by Doll guitarist Joe Shaw is given extensive space: getting to know each other in a folk club in Bridport (Dorset), a shared squat in Dorset, a meeting in Hamburg, a rehearsal room in the Maida Vale squat. Denselow quotes his own characterisation of Leven at the time as a mixture of Van Morrison and psychopath, and mentions Gypsy Blood and the U2 support slot at the London venue. Next come the 1984 mugging in north London (ribs broken, larynx almost destroyed), the heroin addiction (Leven told Denselow of £150 a day), the cure through acupuncture and reflexology, and the founding of the CORE Trust with Carol Wolf, supported by Pete Townshend and Westminster City Council. At a meeting in 1988, Leven preferred to talk about CORE rather than Concrete Bulletproof Invisible (with Shaw and Glen Matlock). Cooking Vinyl boss Martin Goldschmidt says it took him two years to sign Leven, and that he released 26 albums; he calls the whisky brand “Leven's Lament” and the Dylan song story on the train to Moscow “scams”. Mentioned are Mystery of Love with Robert Bly and Mike Scott, Sir Vincent Lone, Deborah Greenwood, David Thomas and Jackie Leven Said with Ian Rankin. Overall tone: warm, respectful, with the expectation that the music will find a larger audience.
zitate_kontext: Denselow's own description from the Doll by Doll period.

2011-11-15-the-spill-readers-recommend-r.kurz: The opening post pays tribute to Leven as a songwriter who encouraged other musicians to write themselves.
inhalt: The opening post pays tribute to Leven as a songwriter who encouraged other musicians to write themselves. More productive than the short announcement of his death is the comment thread: it shows several ways in which listeners discovered Leven. tincanman2010 expressly names the music references in Ian Rankin's Rebus novels. Others came to him through Doll by Doll or through the music selection of the Readers Recommend community.

notsosourpus reports on his contact via the songwriter Dan Britton and on talks about possible performances in Budapest. These did not come about; no tour date can therefore be inferred from them. An anonymously posted comment recalls Britton's participation in a Haunted Valley Christmas concert and makes the connection to “Greetings from Milford” and other live releases.

The thread also contains a reference to a planned Leven tribute on Johny Brown's “Mining for Gold” on Resonance FM the following Friday. That is a concrete lead for radio archives, but not yet proof of a broadcast. The page shows 22 comments or replies in all. As a source it documents the networking of the fan community; their memories and attributions of records are in each case statements by the users concerned.

2011-11-15-theartsdesk-jackie-leven-1950.kurz: Tribute by Graeme Thomson on the morning after Leven's death. He calls Leven one of the country's most distinctive songwriters with a stubbornly low commercial profile and describes the cast of his songs (Serbian prostitutes, Earls Court taxi drivers, convicts, pub philosophers from Dundee), with whom Leven identified; as his best songs he names “Poortoun” and “Universal Blue”. Leven was an ex-junkie, brawler and enthusiastic drinker, the late records often uneven, the concerts with their digressions (Laurence Olivier, a photo session in a Glasgow alley) always worth seeing. Thomson last saw him in August 2011 in Edinburgh, physically weakened.
inhalt: Tribute by Graeme Thomson on the morning after Leven's death. He calls Leven one of the country's most distinctive songwriters with a stubbornly low commercial profile and describes the cast of his songs (Serbian prostitutes, Earls Court taxi drivers, convicts, pub philosophers from Dundee), with whom Leven identified; as his best songs he names “Poortoun” and “Universal Blue”. Leven was an ex-junkie, brawler and enthusiastic drinker, the late records often uneven, the concerts with their digressions (Laurence Olivier, a photo session in a Glasgow alley) always worth seeing. Thomson last saw him in August 2011 in Edinburgh, physically weakened.

The original version (preserved in the LiveJournal reproduction) was followed by an edited version of an older Herald profile by Thomson, in which the 56-year-old Leven tells at length: being an outsider because of his Roma family in the Fife of the 1950s, nights spent fleeing gangs, LSD years and episodic mental illness during the Doll by Doll period, the 1984 mugging after a bottle of Canadian Club on the way to Maida Vale, two years without a voice and with heroin, healing through acupuncture and “psychic healing”, CORE Trust (Lady Diana, Westminster City Council award), monthly acupuncture to this day, a visit to Oslo and the forthcoming Doll by Doll CD reissues, including musings on a reunion. The current page contains only the obituary part.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his Doll by Doll years (Herald profile).

2011-11-15-theartsdesk-kommentare-jackie.kurz: Beneath Graeme Thomson's obituary (15.11.2011) there were around 30 reader comments up to March 2012; they are no longer visible on the live page today, but are complete in the Wayback capture of 2021.
inhalt: Beneath Graeme Thomson's obituary (15.11.2011) there were around 30 reader comments up to March 2012; they are no longer visible on the live page today, but are complete in the Wayback capture of 2021. A Viennese fan (“Rodja”) learned the news through Michael Cosgrave's Facebook page; Leven's Vienna concert in September had been cancelled. Several commenters name the Southsea Folk and Roots Festival as a regular meeting place, others concerts in Otley, New Brighton, at the Green Man Festival, in Hebden Bridge, Glasgow, Stornoway (1990s) and at the Chimney Boy in Faversham.

Two entries come from Leven's professional circle: the documentary maker Mark Kidel says that Leven had seen his Channel 4 film *Kind of Blue* about melancholy and depression in the 1990s and invited him to show and discuss it at a centre for addicts in Marylebone; Kidel describes Leven's charisma and empathy with those affected. A musician who played on Leven's albums thanks him for introducing him to Yeats's line about the “rag and bone shop of the heart” (February 2012). A Belgian fan describes how in 2008, seriously ill, he set off at short notice for Leven's concert in Eeklo in order to shake his hand.

2011-11-15-word-magazine-blog-jackie-lev.autor: MarkHagen; Amigoman; stevedickychap; Burt Kocain (thread starter)

2011-11-16-bbc-blogs-stuart-bailie-jacki.kurz: Short blog entry by the music journalist and Radio Ulster presenter Stuart Bailie. He recalls a Leven performance at London's Borderline in a kilt with his own whisky, Doll by Doll as a post-punk cult band (Stuart Maconie was said to have been a big fan) and the anecdote with which Leven answered Mike Scott in 1986 when Scott complained about the rock-star life – according to Bailie honoured in the sleevenotes of “Fisherman's Blues”. In 1992 Bailie listened for an afternoon in west London to Leven's stories about addiction and the CORE Trust.

In 1992 Bailie listened for an afternoon in west London to Leven's stories about addiction and the CORE Trust.

2011-11-16-dagsavisen-jackie-leven-er-do.kurz: Short death report in the print edition of 16.11.2011: the Scottish singer and songwriter died on Monday aged 61.
inhalt: Short death report in the print edition of 16.11.2011: the Scottish singer and songwriter died on Monday aged 61. He became known in 1979 as the frontman of Doll by Doll, disappeared for many years with personal problems and returned in 1994; since then he had released 24 albums, most of them of a high standard. Leven's relationship with Norway is highlighted: he was a great “friend of Norway”, played all over the country, often sang about places he visited, translated Rolf Jacobsen into English and recorded a record in the Bergen prison. On a flight to Tromsø he discovered that he was one of the favourite singers of Ian Rankin's fictional character John Rebus; from this the joint album *Jackie Leven Said* arose.

The report is brief (around a hundred words), but bundles the narrative strands about Leven that are common in Norway – prison concert, Rolf Jacobsen, the Rankin encounter – which are also found in later Norwegian tributes (Dagsavisen 2021).

2011-11-16-david-belbin-jackie-leven-rip.kurz: The Nottingham writer David Belbin (young-adult and crime novels) writes a personal obituary two days after Leven's death.
inhalt: The Nottingham writer David Belbin (young-adult and crime novels) writes a personal obituary two days after Leven's death. He says he met Leven several times over the years and could hardly reconcile the affable, very funny man with the fearsome singer he saw in 1979 with Doll by Doll at the Garage in Nottingham – Leven told him twenty years later that it had been one of their few good gigs. Belbin mentions the John St Field album from the early 1970s, the assault, the heroin addiction and Leven's return as a prolific songwriter and storyteller, who he says made him laugh more than any current stand-up comedian.

He had a ticket for a concert in Derby in October 2011 that had been postponed – now he knew the reason. Leven, he says, never played encores (at most granting a single request), but after concerts he would hug and kiss fans and sign autographs. He points to the obituaries in the Guardian and the Herald and to Kevin Hewick's piece at Louder Than War, and posts the song *To Live and Die in Levenland* as an MP3. In the comments one reader recalls a concert at Jim's Café in Colne; in 2021 Belbin adds a reply pointing to the new tribute album.
zitate_kontext: Belbin on Leven as a storyteller.

2011-11-16-gaffa-jackie-leven-er-dod.kurz: Strunk reports Leven's death and refers to the positive GAFFA review of his last album.
inhalt: Strunk reports Leven's death and refers to the positive GAFFA review of his last album. He highlights the long collaboration with Michael Cosgrave and mentions a performance still planned at the Green Hotel in Kinross.

2011-11-16-gonzo-circus-bij-de-dood-van-.kurz: The Dutch music journalist Peter Bruyn explicitly writes not an obituary but a personal recollection.
inhalt: The Dutch music journalist Peter Bruyn explicitly writes not an obituary but a personal recollection. He says he began listening to Leven seriously around the turn of the millennium, after a Doll by Doll LP had sat gathering dust on his shelf for years. He was first moved by the idiosyncratic melodies and the voice (compared with Scott Walker, David Thomas and Robert Fisher of Willard Grant Conspiracy), then by the themes: ordinary people groaning under the weight of life, losing work, wife and ideals, and taking stock in front of a bottle of whisky. Bruyn briefly recounts the biography (the near-strangling in the eighties, damaged vocal cords, heroin, founding a holistic detox clinic, the voice returning in the nineties).

In 2005 Bruyn visited Leven in Münster for an interview, a week before a gig at the Patronaat in Haarlem; he describes him as driven by deep compassion and at the same time very funny, with introductions that lasted longer than the songs. Another Patronaat concert had been planned for the end of September 2011, but the tour was suddenly cancelled because Leven was ill.

The main part is an anecdote: in January 2006 Leven played at a private party that Bruyn held in Haarlem for his own 50th and his partner's 40th birthday, and kept around eighty guests quiet for an hour. Afterwards he only wanted to take his guitar back to the hotel briefly, but got stuck at the bar of the Proeflokaal De Blauwe Druif with an old man, then lay down for a moment at the hotel, fell asleep and woke only shortly before his flight from Schiphol; the next evening he phoned and apologised profusely. The text ends with the sentence that Leven will now never wake up again. Tenor: warm, humorous, sad.

2011-11-16-herald-scotland-jackie-leven-.kurz: Standalone, unsigned Herald obituary (headline “Musician; Born: June 18, 1950; Died: November 14, 2011”), separate from the news report of the same day.
inhalt: Standalone, unsigned Herald obituary (headline “Musician; Born: June 18, 1950; Died: November 14, 2011”), separate from the news report of the same day. It calls Leven one of Scotland's most underrated songwriters and a soulful singer and guitarist. Background according to the text: father Irish-Cockney, mother from north-east England, Roma roots that made him an outsider in the Fife of the 1950s and 60s; Leven tells (as a quotation) of the night in the allotment when he hid from a gang. He was already on the road married at 17, having previously been thrown out of Kirkcaldy High School for drugs, where he was in the same year as Gordon Brown. Then come Berlin, Madrid and Control as John St Field (on a Spanish label), the founding of Doll by Doll in London in 1975, being thrown off tours with Devo and Hawkwind, a solo contract with Virgin in 1984, the mugging on the way home from the studio, two years without a voice, heroin and the cure through acupuncture, CORE Trust with Princess Diana as patron. After that a fresh start with his family, Cooking Vinyl, the 1994 comeback, over 20 albums in 17 years, collaborations with David Thomas, Johnny Dowd and Ian Rankin (Usher Hall 2005). Leven was a crowd-puller in Europe, especially in Germany, and remained a cult figure in Britain. Stage anecdotes (losing his girlfriend to the Dalai Lama's bodyguard, Bay City Rollers badge). The text ends with the 2011 Edinburgh Fringe show, at which Leven was emaciated, and the closing line of “Main Travelled Roads”. Several formulations coincide with Graeme Thomson's Herald profile (c. 2006, reused in the theartsdesk obituary); Thomson as author is plausible but not proven.

2011-11-16-herald-scotland-scots-folk-si.kurz: News item in the Herald: Leven died “on Monday evening” after a long battle with cancer.
inhalt: News item in the Herald: Leven died “on Monday evening” after a long battle with cancer. An unnamed music critic is quoted with the formula of the most talented songwriter who never became a household name, along with tweets from Ian Rankin and Eddi Reader. Short biography: began in the late 1960s as John St Field, 1983 assault and two years without a voice, heroin addiction, over 400 songs, co-founding of the CORE Trust.

2011-11-16-louder-than-war-jackie-leven-.kurz: Tribute by the Leicester singer-songwriter Kevin Hewick, who as a teenager saw over 50 Doll by Doll concerts.
inhalt: Tribute by the Leicester singer-songwriter Kevin Hewick, who as a teenager saw over 50 Doll by Doll concerts. He spans the arc from the folk duo Saint Judas (1969) through Doll by Doll to the solo work and stresses the timeless sharpness of the songs. He recalls at length Remember (1979), a fan community from Derby and Leicester that followed the band everywhere, Leven's Burns guitar decorated with LSD carvings (Leven's own statement to Hewick), Joe Shaw's smashed Stratocaster, the line-up with Dave McIntosh, Robin Spreafico and Tony Waite, and nights on the floor of the squat in Warwick Avenue. The comeback of the 1990s was accompanied by Mick Nolan with the information service and fanzine The Haunted Valley; at the Christmas parties in Milford (Derbyshire) Hewick and other Leicester musicians played with Leven as “The Stornoway Girls”, and in 2002 there was a one-off trio with Leven and Joe Shaw. Overall tone: deeply moved, with mockery of commercially more successful singer-songwriters.

2011-11-16-rock-town-hall-jackie-leven-d.kurz: The operator of the US rock discussion site (“Mr. Moderator”) writes on the day of the death (date given by the site: 16.11.2011) that he knew Leven only through John St. Field's 1975 album *Control*, to which a fellow user had introduced him – a quirky mixture of English hippie folk and pub rock.
inhalt: The operator of the US rock discussion site (“Mr. Moderator”) writes on the day of the death (date given by the site: 16.11.2011) that he knew Leven only through John St. Field's 1975 album *Control*, to which a fellow user had introduced him – a quirky mixture of English hippie folk and pub rock. He says he once asked Leven in vain for an interview for the site and only learned of the duet with David Thomas from the obituary. Four comments: a British user remembers Doll by Doll on John Peel and a concert near him that had been postponed shortly before, another calls *Gypsy Blood* a great lost album, wrongly marketed as New Wave; one points to the Rebus novels.

2011-11-16-telegraph-blogs-jackie-leven-.kurz: Personal obituary by Neil McCormick, Leven's long-standing advocate at the Telegraph.
inhalt: Personal obituary by Neil McCormick, Leven's long-standing advocate at the Telegraph. He calls Leven Britain's great lost rock star and says he used his name as a counter-argument whenever successful musicians claimed that talent always prevails. McCormick saw Doll by Doll in a club in Dublin in the late 1970s and describes them as Celtic heavy-rock Beach Boys with a metaphysical streak, whom he and his musician friends revered; Gypsy Blood, he says, is a masterpiece. He quotes Robin Denselow's early characterisation and sketches Kirkcaldy, Gordon Brown (about whom Leven told many comic stories), the drug expulsion, the assault in the early 1980s with almost two years without a voice, heroin, CORE and Diana, to whom Leven attributed his return to music in the early 1990s. Leven often claimed to be writing a book. Listening recommendations: Gypsy Blood, Doll by Doll, Fairy Tales For Hard Men, Defending Ancient Springs, Creatures of Light And Darkness. An official obituary in the Telegraph, he says, will follow.

2011-11-16-the-daily-telegraph-jackie-le.kurz: Classic Telegraph obituary. Leven was said to be one of the most colourful and distinctive talents in rock and folk, without the success he deserved; a Telegraph critic (Neil McCormick) is said to have called Doll by Doll “the greatest band you've never heard of”.
inhalt: Classic Telegraph obituary. Leven was said to be one of the most colourful and distinctive talents in rock and folk, without the success he deserved; a Telegraph critic (Neil McCormick) is said to have called Doll by Doll “the greatest band you've never heard of”. Biography: born into a Roma family in Kirkcaldy, father London-Irish, mother from Northumbria; truant, walks in the hills near Kirkcaldy, his mother's love of the blues, folk clubs, hitchhiking through Europe, busking in London, Control in 1971 as John St Field. With themes such as mental illness and homelessness, Doll by Doll set themselves apart from punk and split up after four albums. In 1983 an assault by a group of strangers on the way home from a recording session in north London; Leven says he thought he was going to die. Then separation, withdrawal, heroin, after two years recovery through Chinese treatment and “psychic healing”, co-founding of the Core Trust in Marylebone. Move to Oban, where the material for Mystery of Love (1994) came into being. Overview of the work: Forbidden Songs Of The Dying West (1995, male voice choir, Eddi Reader, Andy White), Fairy Tales For Hard Men (1997), Night Lilies (1998), Defending Ancient Springs (2000, Kathleen Raine, duet with David Thomas), Elegy For Johnny Cash (2005), Lovers At The Gun Club (2008) and the last album with “German Hotel Rooms” in its subtitle.

2011-11-16-the-granville-chambers-jackie.kurz: A short personal obituary on a private blog from Bournemouth. The author, who interviewed Leven several times, describes him as always friendly and talkative in conversation, as generous in listening as in telling stories.
inhalt: A short personal obituary on a private blog from Bournemouth. The author, who interviewed Leven several times, describes him as always friendly and talkative in conversation, as generous in listening as in telling stories. He remembers a tiny concert that Leven let himself be talked into: in the skittle alley of his village pub in Dorset, not far from the farmland where Leven is said to have lived once, in front of 30 people at most. Leven played the full emotional range there and told stories – from life on the road to the claim that Bob Dylan had spat in his Guinness, and about a Great Dane from the neighbouring pub that stole his pie. The post closes with a farewell and links five of his own pieces in the Bournemouth Echo: interviews in 2006 (“Leven it up”, about Dorset and Doll by Doll), 2008 (about Amy Winehouse and *Lovers at the Gun Club*) and 2010 (about Gordon Brown and *Gothic Road*), as well as 2009 reviews of Sir Vincent Lone (*Troubadour Heart*) and of the *Haunted Year – Summer* double CD.

2011-11-16-the-scotsman-obituary-maveric.kurz: Personal obituary by the Scotsman music journalist Colin Somerville, who first met Leven in 1994 in a telephone interview about Mystery of Love and was friends with him.
inhalt: Personal obituary by the Scotsman music journalist Colin Somerville, who first met Leven in 1994 in a telephone interview about Mystery of Love and was friends with him. He describes childhood in the new town of Glenrothes with an Irish-Cockney father and a “Geordie” mother (north-east England), Leven's aversion to his old home (he looked grimly across the Forth from the Old Chain Pier in Newhaven), expulsion from school for drug possession, marriage at 16 and being driven out by youth gangs. There follow years of wandering, Berlin, Spain, Control as John St Field and Doll by Doll, who were said to be neither punk nor New Wave. Somerville moves the assault to Islington: Leven was throttled from behind at a cash machine and permanently lost his falsetto range. Then heroin, healing with a Chinese method, CORE with the Princess of Wales as a supporter. Somerville stresses Leven's closeness to Robert Bly and the Men's Movement, the collaborations with Mike Scott, David Thomas, Robert Fisher and Ian Rankin, and the unusual loyalty between Leven and Cooking Vinyl boss Martin Goldschmidt. Anecdotes: two fans from Teesside, in front of whom Leven did not want to play at a late-scheduled Fringe show and who sat in the front row the following year; the beer glass with a mystery cocktail on stage; the poet Paul Reekie before a Leven festival show. Tenor: affectionate, Leven as an unsung Scottish hero.

2011-11-17-efe-eme-fallece-el-cantante-y.kurz: Short death notice from the Spanish music magazine: Leven died of cancer on 14 November aged 61, founded the punk band Doll by Doll in 1977 (four albums 1979–1982) and afterwards worked solo under his own name and as John St. Field; in 1984, during recording of his first solo album, he was said to have been attacked in the street and almost strangled, lost his speech for two years and became addicted to heroin…
inhalt: Short death notice from the Spanish music magazine: Leven died of cancer on 14 November aged 61, founded the punk band Doll by Doll in 1977 (four albums 1979–1982) and afterwards worked solo under his own name and as John St. Field; in 1984, during recording of his first solo album, he was attacked in the street and almost strangled, lost his speech for two years and became addicted to heroin.

2011-11-17-the-independent-musician-whos.kurz: Obituary by the music journalist Nick Hasted, who had interviewed Leven in 2007 and quotes from that interview.
inhalt: Obituary by the music journalist Nick Hasted, who had interviewed Leven in 2007 and quotes from that interview. He describes Leven's songs as the inner lives of “disappointed hard men” (Rankin's formula), often set in the rough landscapes of his childhood, and as partial self-portraits of a life marked by addiction and exile. Biography: Kirkcaldy, father from London-Irish stock, mother from Northumberland, both Roma according to the text; his mother's blues records, folk clubs at 16, a brief first marriage, prize-winning pupil in the same year as Gordon Brown and allegedly the first Scottish schoolboy expelled for drugs, driven out by a gang. He met the Doll by Doll members in squatted farmhouses in Dorset; in 1975 the band came together in a squat in Bristol Gardens (west London); Leven describes the street full of damaged but funny Scots. The second album, he said, gave him a place in the world. In 1983 he was throttled and cut on the neck, voiceless for over a year, dropped by the label, spending weeks in silence at Marylebone station. 1985 recovery, CORE Trust, meeting with Diana, retreat to the Scottish west coast among fishermen, 1994 fresh start with 24 albums at Cooking Vinyl, Bly's influence, concerts with tall tales (Sting's alleged death on the commuter train to Kirkcaldy), The Haunted Year in 2009 as the best overview of his work.

2011-11-18-jackieleven-co-uk-nachruf-sta.kurz: Unsigned death notice on Leven's official website: death on Monday, 14 November (2011), at 8 pm, after an illness with cancer; with Leven's quotation about “soulful story tellers”, the reference to jackie-leven.com and a biography paragraph (over 400 songs, “Call Mother A Lonely Field” counted by Q among the best…
inhalt: Unsigned death notice on Leven's official website: death on Monday, 14 November (2011), at 8 pm, after an illness with cancer; with Leven's quotation about “soulful story tellers”, the reference to jackie-leven.com and a biography paragraph (over 400 songs, “Call Mother A Lonely Field” counted by Q among the best, humour, storytelling, most recently *Wayside Shrines* with Michael Cosgrave). Below it, the PayPal order buttons for *One Long Cold Morning* and Leven's quotation on the “Code of the Travelling Man” were left in place.

2011-11-18-musiczine-jackie-leven-nous-a.kurz: Dagnies reports Leven's death on 14 November and recalls John St. Field, Doll by Doll and the collaboration with David Thomas.
inhalt: Dagnies reports Leven's death on 14 November and recalls John St. Field, Doll by Doll and the collaboration with David Thomas. He names “Wayside Shrines”, recorded with Michael Cosgrave, as the last album.

2011-11-18-the-times-jackie-leven-obitua.titel: Jackie Leven (obituary; subheading: Scottish singer and songwriter who drew on his wanderings to produce a rich stream of poetic and mysterious anthems)
2011-11-18-the-times-jackie-leven-obitua.kurz: Unsigned Times obituary. It presents Leven as an outsider with a 40-year career, masterly but neglected albums and labels such as “Britain's greatest lost rock star”.
inhalt: Unsigned Times obituary. It presents Leven as an outsider with a 40-year career, masterly but neglected albums and labels such as “Britain's greatest lost rock star”. Biography according to the Times: father an Irish Cockney of Roma descent, mother from Northumbria; Kirkcaldy High School with Gordon Brown, whom Leven briefly outshone when he won the Scottish Round Table's national school essay competition – with an essay about his dream of setting out as a wandering musician. Expelled from school over drugs, from 1967 a decade of wandering through Britain, Ireland and western Europe, Control as John St Field recorded in Madrid “in the mid-1970s”. 1977 founding of Doll by Doll in a London squat; Gypsy Blood is said to have impressed David Gilmour, who then played on Grand Passion (1982). 1983 solo contract with Charisma/Virgin, assault after a night session at a studio in Islington, loss of falsetto, heroin, CORE Trust with Diana as patron. Diana is said to have persuaded him to return to music by urging him to sing backstage at an official engagement; 1994 Cooking Vinyl, over 20 albums, Sir Vincent Lone, Jackie Leven Said with Rankin, who chose Leven on Desert Island Discs. The whisky “Leven's Lament” was named after him by Islay Mist.

2011-11-cooking-vinyl-kommentare-zum-nac.titel: [Comments on the Cooking Vinyl obituary “Jackie Leven June 18th 1950 – 14th November 2011”]
2011-11-cooking-vinyl-kommentare-zum-nac.kurz: 16 reader comments from 15.11. to 01.12.2011 beneath the label's obituary, in English and one in German.
inhalt: 16 reader comments from 15.11. to 01.12.2011 beneath the label's obituary, in English and one in German. Fans from Great Britain, Austria, Germany and Norway mourn and remember: a Viennese learned of the death through Michael Cosgrave's Facebook entry and mentions a cancelled Vienna concert in September 2011; a man from Birmingham describes how, after a Doll by Doll concert in London, Leven gave a friend the lyric sheet he had just sung from; Mike Plumbley (author of the 1997 Winchester concert review) recalls a CORE benefit concert to which he came because of Townes Van Zandt and where Leven played “Men In Prison”, whereupon hard men wept; the Hanover radio presenter Uli Kniep thanks him for many encounters since *The Mystery Of Love*; Jan Myrvold (Norway) promises to pass the legacy on to younger generations; others recall Doll by Doll in north London and in York in 1979, a cancelled Dingwalls concert, a raffle at the 12 Bar Club, Leven's tattered “lucky shirt” and cancelled concerts in 2011 (York, Vienna). A German comment (Leo Lambrecht) mentions performances at the “Lab” in Stuttgart.

2011-11-musikreviews-de-jackie-leven-nac.kurz: Personally coloured short obituary by Jochen König, who later also reviewed Leven. He mentions the knife attack that had robbed him of his voice for almost two years, the heroin addiction that followed and the many albums after his recovery (“true Celtic soul”).
inhalt: Personally coloured short obituary by Jochen König, who later also reviewed Leven. He mentions the knife attack that had robbed him of his voice for almost two years, the heroin addiction that followed and the many albums after his recovery (“true Celtic soul”). He highlights Ian Rankin's appreciation and the live performances: a man with a chair and guitar, latterly mostly with Michael Cosgrave, who often told more than he sang. It ends with thanks and the question of whether the breakthrough had been denied or spared him.

2011-11-pennyblackmusic-jackie-leven-195.kurz: Tribute by the Pennyblack writer Ben Howarth and his brother Charles after Leven's death. Ben recounts how Leven's overrunning set at the Canterbury Fayre festival caught his father's attention and how Leven asked the audience to stay in the tent rather than go and see Robert Plant; the friendship with Robert Fisher of Willard Grant Conspiracy also began there. He learned of the death from a press release and was one of the last journalists to speak to Leven. Charles describes his first Leven concert, at lunchtime in a pub in Bath, and singles out “Museum of Childhood”; the recommended starting point is “Classic Northern Diversions”.
inhalt: Tribute by the Pennyblack writer Ben Howarth and his brother Charles after Leven's death. Ben recounts how Leven's overrunning set at the Canterbury Fayre festival caught his father's attention and how Leven asked the audience to stay in the tent rather than go and see Robert Plant; the friendship with Robert Fisher of Willard Grant Conspiracy also began there. He learned of the death from a press release and was one of the last journalists to speak to Leven. Charles describes his first Leven concert, at lunchtime in a pub in Bath, and singles out “Museum of Childhood”; the recommended starting point is “Classic Northern Diversions”.

2011-12-06-bhcr-real-music-club-18.kurz: Three weeks after Leven's death, Tim Rundall played two tracks from “Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man” on the Brighton community radio programme: “To Live and Die in Levenland” and “Backstage Chelsea Club” (playlist in the archive.org description).
inhalt: Three weeks after Leven's death, Tim Rundall played two tracks from “Wayside Shrines and the Code of the Travelling Man” on the Brighton community radio programme: “To Live and Die in Levenland” and “Backstage Chelsea Club” (playlist in the archive.org description). The programme is available there as audio.

2011-12-09-gaesteliste-michael-weston-ki.kurz: Report from a house concert by Michael Weston King in Cologne on 09.12.2011, which was largely devoted to the memory of Leven, who had died a few weeks earlier.
inhalt: Report from a house concert by Michael Weston King in Cologne on 09.12.2011, which was largely devoted to the memory of Leven, who had died a few weeks earlier. King recalled their collaboration (production of “A Decent Man” in 2003, Leven's pointer to Langston Hughes for King's protest-song album, joint appearances up to Leven's last concerts in August 2011) and sang Ronnie Lane's “She's Leaving” as “He's Leaving”; lines from it were said to have been read at Leven's funeral. No Leven song in the programme.

2011-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-2011-v.kurz: Around 35 genuine entries that reflect Leven's last year from a fan's perspective. In the first half of the year, declarations of devotion dominate (a fan from Leeds saw him in 1994 at the Duchess of York pub and remembers “Gylen Gylen”), along with questions about Australian tours and memories from old acquaintances: a Yorkshireman, now in Saigon, says he stayed overnight in the Doll by Doll flat in Maida Vale and arranged gigs for the band. In summer *One Long Cold Morning* is sent out by post; delivery to Germany takes a long time, and the old resentment about the never-delivered *Cornish Pub* CD flares up again. One guest announces a free concert on 12.08.2011 at Jolly's Bar, Kilmarnock; a Canadian is looking forward to the Halifax Urban Folk Festival (HUFF), a Swede to the Scandinavian tour in October.
inhalt: Around 35 genuine entries that reflect Leven's last year from a fan's perspective. In the first half of the year, declarations of devotion dominate (a fan from Leeds saw him in 1994 at the Duchess of York pub and remembers “Gylen Gylen”), along with questions about Australian tours and memories from old acquaintances: a Yorkshireman, now in Saigon, says he stayed overnight in the Doll by Doll flat in Maida Vale and arranged gigs for the band. In summer *One Long Cold Morning* is sent out by post; delivery to Germany takes a long time, and the old resentment about the never-delivered *Cornish Pub* CD flares up again. One guest announces a free concert on 12.08.2011 at Jolly's Bar, Kilmarnock; a Canadian is looking forward to the Halifax Urban Folk Festival (HUFF), a Swede to the Scandinavian tour in October.

From 10.09.2011 the tone changes: fans from Munich, Hamburg, Lauterbach, Bremen, the Netherlands and Münster write that Leven is in hospital and the entire 2011 German tour has been cancelled; a woman from Münster who had planned to go to the Hot Jazz Club on 22.09. had his CD played there instead. One fan wishes him to “get oot the hospital”, Norwegians still hope in October for the concert at Buddy in Drammen, a man from Burnley regrets the cancelled concert at the Trades Club (October), a Londoner asks for news on 04.10. On 14.11.2011, the day of his death, the first words of farewell appear.
