2012-02-21-jackieleven-co-uk-robberies-o.titel: [Notice] Robberies of the Rain – profits go to Jackie Leven Memorial Fund

2012-03-31-david-belbin-jackie-leven-ran.kurz: Belbin finds in his collection a concert recording from Essen, a year before Leven's death, and puts its announcement about Randy Newman and Joni Mitchell online as audio, together with Mitchell's “Shades of Scarlett Conquering” and Newman's “The Girls in My Life”.
inhalt: Belbin finds in his collection a concert recording from Essen, a year before Leven's death, and puts its announcement about Randy Newman and Joni Mitchell online as audio, together with Mitchell's “Shades of Scarlett Conquering” and Newman's “The Girls in My Life”. He mentions that his diary for early March 2012 still had the rescheduled Leven concert at the Flowerpot in Derby, where he says he had seen him twice.

2012-03-the-word-the-jackie-leven-obitua.kurz: The most literary obituary, written by the music journalist Paul Du Noyer, who met Leven in 1979 and was his friend for 32 years.
inhalt: The most literary obituary, written by the music journalist Paul Du Noyer, who met Leven in 1979 and was his friend for 32 years. Published in The Word (March 2012) together with the cover CD “Heroes Can Be Any Size”, compiled by Du Noyer; the website version contains the track list at the end. Du Noyer asks who Leven actually was, and interprets the persona “Jackie Leven” as a deliberately built house into which Alan Moffatt had moved. He describes the background (English parents with Roma and Irish roots, according to Leven), reading from John Clare to the Russian poets, singing exercises with “Rescue Me”, the squats in north London in the mid-1970s, his own experiences in 1979 (frightening pubs, drugs, conspiracy theories), Doll by Doll and the name after e. e. cummings. Leven is said to have burst into tears when Du Noyer asked him about the closing line of “Main Travelled Roads”. There follow the assault, heroin, CORE (with the expansion of the acronym) and Diana's alleged interest in Leven (his own account), Cooking Vinyl from 1994, the Men's Movement phase after the Robert Bly tape from the Dalai Lama's bodyguard, “Levenland”, bars as places of devotion, Ian Rankin. Deborah Greenwood speaks at length about Leven's restlessness, the “electric fur”, life in the village in Hampshire and some fans' expectation of seeing him suffer. Conclusion: diagnosis in September 2011, death on 14 November, funeral in a country church with “Working Alone / A Blessing”, and Leven's probably last online message about a “Belfast Of The Mind”.

2012-10-06-my-vintage-rock-doll-by-doll-.kurz: Short reminiscence post by a concertgoer from the north-east of England: he saw Doll by Doll around 1979 at the Middlesbrough Rock Garden and thinks he also saw them as support act on the Hawkwind tour at Newcastle City Hall; at the time he did not think them special, but listened to the debut “Remember” often and only in retrospect recognised its uniqueness…
inhalt: Short reminiscence post by a concertgoer from the north-east of England: he saw Doll by Doll around 1979 at the Middlesbrough Rock Garden and thinks he also saw them as support act on the Hawkwind tour at Newcastle City Hall; at the time he did not think them special, but listened to the debut “Remember” often and only in retrospect recognised its uniqueness. Also a Leven quotation about “soulful” rather than “spiritual” storytelling (no source given). In the comments two readers remember Doll by Doll at the Hawkwind concert, at the Reading Festival and at the “Rock on the Tyne” festival in Gateshead Stadium.

2012-10-11-orion-ian-rankin-standing-in-.kurz: Publisher's video of just under two minutes: Rankin explains that the novel's title is a “mondegreen” – for years he heard the refrain of Leven's “Another Man's Rain” as “Standing in Another Man's Grave” and only noticed the mistake when looking at the lyric booklet; Rebus mishears it in the same way at the start of the novel.
inhalt: Publisher's video of just under two minutes: Rankin explains that the novel's title is a “mondegreen” – for years he heard the refrain of Leven's “Another Man's Rain” as “Standing in Another Man's Grave” and only noticed the mistake when looking at the lyric booklet; Rebus mishears it in the same way at the start of the novel. The book is dedicated to Leven, and each section begins with a Leven line. Rankin calls him a great guitarist and storyteller, “not well enough known”. Tenor: tribute shortly after Leven's death.

2012-11-21-the-quietus-crime-plays-write.autor: Luke Turner; conversation with Ian Rankin
2012-11-21-the-quietus-crime-plays-write.kurz: Ian Rankin chooses “Creatures of Light and Darkness” for the “Baker’s Dozen” series. His reasoning leads directly to his writing: Leven's male characters, who are poor at expressing their feelings, seemed to him fitting music for Rebus.
inhalt: Ian Rankin chooses “Creatures of Light and Darkness” for the “Baker’s Dozen” series. His reasoning leads directly to his writing: Leven's male characters, who are poor at expressing their feelings, seemed to him fitting music for Rebus. Rankin recalls that Leven in turn read the novels and got in touch via the publisher after his name was mentioned. From this developed their personal meeting and the joint recording for Cooking Vinyl.

A second focus is “Standing in Another Man’s Grave”, the new Rebus book dedicated to Leven. Rankin explains the title as his own mishearing of a Leven song title. He also describes how he built the misunderstanding into the novel: after a funeral, Rebus listens to Leven in the car and likewise mishears the words. Rankin also says that different Leven songs open the sections of the book.

Finally he connects the album title with the moral ambivalence of human action, which also interests his crime novels. The source thus documents Rankin's own interpretation of the connection between Leven's music and Rebus, a year after Leven's death.

2012-2020-nasjonalbiblioteket-jackie-lev.titel: [Collected finds Nasjonalbiblioteket 2012–2020: short notices, announcements, lists]

2012-jackieleven-co-uk-gaestebuch-2012-2.kurz: About 25 genuine entries, after that almost only spam. In 2012 late condolences continue to arrive: many only learned of the death months later (June 2012 a fan who found Leven through the Rebus novels).
inhalt: About 25 genuine entries, after that almost only spam. In 2012 late condolences continue to arrive: many only learned of the death months later (June 2012 a fan who found Leven through the Rebus novels). An Australian tells how Leven stopped mid-song in Katoomba when his little daughter tipped a drink over his lap. There are short memorial entries for the birthday (18.06.2012) and the first anniversary of the death (14–17.11.2012); in August 2012 a German fan writes a greeting to everyone who has posted here. In 2013 a new listener from Atlanta gets in touch; in 2015 there are only isolated single characters and spam.

2013-07-15-plain-and-fancy-john-st-field.kurz: Collector's blog post on “Control” with credits (including Joe Kucera, Jesse Ballard, Juliet Lawson) and a long biography apparently taken from official Leven materials: childhood in Fife as an outsider, his mother a blues lover (Lightnin' Hopkins), first appearances at the Elbow Room folk club in…
inhalt: Collector's blog post on “Control” with credits (including Joe Kucera, Jesse Ballard, Juliet Lawson) and a long biography apparently taken from official Leven materials: childhood in Fife as an outsider, his mother a blues lover (Lightnin' Hopkins), first appearances at the Elbow Room folk club in Kirkcaldy with encouragement from Archie Fisher and Hamish Imlach, guitarist for Doris Henderson, flight from a gang vendetta, years of wandering (South Bank Centre, County Kerry, Berlin, Madrid), living in squats with mentally ill people. Three short reader comments pay tribute to Leven after his death. Tenor: collector's enthusiasm (“psychedelic underground classic”).

2013-09-26-orion-saints-of-the-shadow-bi.kurz: Publisher's video of a good minute and a half: Rankin says “Saints of the Shadow Bible” is the second book whose title he takes from a Leven line; Leven died while he was planning “Standing in Another Man's Grave”.
inhalt: Publisher's video of a good minute and a half: Rankin says “Saints of the Shadow Bible” is the second book whose title he takes from a Leven line; Leven died while he was planning “Standing in Another Man's Grave”. Their friendship rests on mutual admiration; Leven's songs and his books are about men who cannot show their feelings and make mistakes. The title was one of four or five possible Leven quotations and stands for ghosts, alcohol and Rebus's love of Leven's music; some lines appear in the book as epigraphs.

2013-12-29-the-new-vinyl-villain-big-tea.kurz: Blog post about the only single by Concrete Bulletproof Invisible (1988): at its core Doll by Doll with Glen Matlock on bass.
inhalt: Blog post about the only single by Concrete Bulletproof Invisible (1988): at its core Doll by Doll with Glen Matlock on bass. After a longer Wikipedia quotation on the band's history, the author calls “Big Tears” (Matlock) and “Braid On My Shoulder” (Leven) two strong songs with Matlock's power-pop swing and Leven's powerful voice; he mentions the British 12" with “Good Thing” and the US 12" with “Love Kills”. Finally biographical notes (Botley, Ian Rankin, death in 2011) and a reference to a piece on the discontinued blog “Helpless Dancer” (April 2010). In the comments a reader remembers the B-side about a soldier in Belfast. Tenor: affectionate.

2014-01-25-distorsioni-outsider-di-gran-.kurz: Two-part portrait in the Italian web magazine Distorsioni, a good two years after Leven's death.
inhalt: Two-part portrait in the Italian web magazine Distorsioni, a good two years after Leven's death. Part 1 (Jackie Leven) tells the career: “Control” in 1973 as John St. Field on the Spanish label Movieplay, founding of Doll by Doll in 1975, four LPs 1977–1983, at the end of 1983 a street assault with an attempt at strangling and over two years without the ability to speak or sing, heroin addiction, the band Concrete Bulletproof Invisible with Glen Matlock (single “Big Tears”, good review in Melody Maker), a collaboration with John Foxx, in the early nineties overcoming the addiction with the help of his wife Carol through acupuncture and holistic therapy, then the return in 1994 with “Songs from the Argyll Cycle” and the Cooking Vinyl album “The Mystery of Love…”. Highlighted are, among others, “Fairytales for Hard Men”, “Creatures of Light and Darkness”, the Haunted Year series and “Wayside Shrines…”, collaborations with Michael Cosgrave and Ian Rankin, the pseudonym Sir Vincent Lone and support slots for Willie Nile and Lloyd Cole. Sfondrini compares Leven's vocal range with Demetrio Stratos (Area).

Part 2 (Doll by Doll) describes the band as neither commercial nor compatible with punk, discusses “Remember”, “Gypsy Blood”, “Doll by Doll” (MCA, released late) and “Grand Passion” (Magnet, with Helen Turner, Mel Collins and David Gilmour; Turner is judged disparagingly) and mentions the live CD “Revenge Of Memory” (Sheffield Limits Club 1977, released 2006). Tenor: appeal for rediscovery, Leven as an “outsider” of great class.
zitate_kontext: Closing appeal of the Leven part.

2015-06-16-the-guardian-cult-heroes-jack.kurz: Tribute for his (almost) 65th birthday in the Guardian series on cult musicians. Graeme Thomson recalls Leven's concert at the Cabaret Voltaire in Edinburgh on 11 August 2011, which turned out to be a farewell; three months later Leven died of pancreatic cancer.
inhalt: Tribute for his (almost) 65th birthday in the Guardian series on cult musicians. Graeme Thomson recalls Leven's concert at the Cabaret Voltaire in Edinburgh on 11 August 2011, which turned out to be a farewell; three months later Leven died of pancreatic cancer. Relatively well known in Germany and Norway, under the radar in Britain, but with high-calibre admirers: David Thomas, Johnny Dowd, Ron Sexsmith, Ian Rankin (two Rebus titles taken from Leven songs) and Mike Scott, who gave Thomson a statement of his own. Thomson characterises the songs as poetry of unfulfilled lives with moments of transcendence and recommends “Poor Toun” and “Universal Blue” (live version from The Haunted Year: Winter), as well as the Sir Vincent Lone version of Judee Sill's “When the Bridegroom Comes”. Biography: father London-Irish, mother from north-east England, school in Kirkcaldy like Gordon Brown, Roma heritage; left home at 16, by the early 1970s had left two marriages behind him. Doll by Doll (with Joe Shaw and Dave MacIntosh) in the squat in Maida Vale, contract with Automatic (Warner), thrown off a Hawkwind tour, drug excesses. After the split in 1983 a contract with Virgin, assault on the way home from a session, never regained his falsetto, heroin, recovery, CORE Trust. Return to music in 1992, around 30 releases in two decades. Thomson's stage memories and Rankin's perception of “pent-up energy”.

2015-06-16-the-guardian-kommentare-cult-.titel: [Reader comments on: Cult heroes: Jackie Leven found musical beauty in his wounds]
2015-06-16-the-guardian-kommentare-cult-.kurz: Twenty comments (16–18.06.2015) under Graeme Thomson's “Cult heroes” piece. To one reader's charge that a dead man is being mythologised, fans reply that Leven did most of that himself.
inhalt: Twenty comments (16–18.06.2015) under Graeme Thomson's “Cult heroes” piece. To one reader's charge that a dead man is being mythologised, fans reply that Leven did most of that himself. “Kevin1957”, who followed the band as a fan and was allowed to stay overnight in Maida Vale, reports that co-founder Robin Spreafico died of cancer in early 2015 and his successor Tony Waite a few years earlier; Doll by Doll, he says, did get front covers of Disc and Record Mirror at the time. Another reader remembers that Leven played regularly at the Brighton Folk Club in the early 1970s.

The most detailed is “simonhop”, a songwriter who supported him several times at the 12 Bar Club in the mid-1990s and booked Leven for a series in Bromley. Leven stayed overnight with him and, over vodka and orange juice, explained his storytelling technique: the audience does not want ordinary heroes; the storyteller must have experienced extraordinary things, and the truth must not get in the way. Leven later asked about printing one of simonhop's lyrics on an album cover, which never happened. Another reader was at the 12 Bar concert that was released as *For Peace Comes Dropping Slow*, saw Leven at the release concert for *The Mystery of Love* at the Borderline with an electric guitar, and in the 1990s exchanged letters with him about poetry (recommendation: Sharon Olds, *The Father*; conversation about Kenneth Patchen). TatankaYotanka announces the tribute evenings by Michael Weston King and Michael Cosgrave in Winchester and Birmingham.

2015-06-18-the-afterword-jackie-leven-wo.kurz: Birthday thread (18/19.06.2015) with twelve replies: toasts, favourite songs and links (including “Desolation Blues” live in Glasgow, c. 1997).
inhalt: Birthday thread (18/19.06.2015) with twelve replies: toasts, favourite songs and links (including “Desolation Blues” live in Glasgow, c. 1997). SteveT had a ticket for Leven's last planned Birmingham concert, which was cancelled about a week before his death, and looks forward to an evening of Leven songs by Michael Weston King and Michael Cosgrave in July 2015. retropath2 says Leven lived near his parents' house on the Hampshire coast and that he searched for him in village pubs in vain; Gary recalls that when Leven died in 2011 he had posted the quotation about the warrior who finds beauty in his wounds. duco01 links Graeme Thomson's Guardian blog of 16.06.2015.

2016-06-18-born-to-listen-jackie-leven-w.kurz: The Norwegian operator of the English-language music blog (otherwise mainly about Bob Dylan) recalls a concert about a year before Leven's death: after the show Leven could not pronounce his first name, asked what it meant and signed a CD for him “To my big viking friend”.
inhalt: The Norwegian operator of the English-language music blog (otherwise mainly about Bob Dylan) recalls a concert about a year before Leven's death: after the show Leven could not pronounce his first name, asked what it meant and signed a CD for him “To my big viking friend”. He calls Leven a masterly storyteller in and between songs. There follows an annotated selection of YouTube videos (“Empty in Soho Square” with a 2004 interview, medley “Ancient Misty Morning” Tramway Glasgow 1995, “Kings Of Infinite Space” 23.07.2010, “Poortoun” 25.07.1999, “Single Father” 20.09.2000) and a Wikipedia paragraph.

2016-08-01-fast-n-bulbous-between-the-cr.kurz: Part of a blog series about bands that fell “between the cracks” of rock history; the Doll by Doll section appears alongside Holly and the Italians, Tonio K., Skids and others. Van Dorston places the band as not fitting the post-punk scene, closer to Van Morrison and Springsteen; “Remember” is…
inhalt: Part of a blog series about bands that fell “between the cracks” of rock history; the Doll by Doll section appears alongside Holly and the Italians, Tonio K., Skids and others. Van Dorston places the band as not fitting the post-punk scene, closer to Van Morrison and Springsteen; “Remember” is rough but promising (a bridge from Free to Gang of Four), “Gypsy Blood” an “unsung classic”, the third album smoother and somewhat less passionate, “Grand Passion” effectively a solo album. Then a brief outline of the following years (drugs, CORE Trust, Princess Diana, Concrete Bulletproof, Men's Movement, return in 1994).

2017-02-13-bergensmagasinet-nese-for-det.kurz: Portrait of Frank Nes, concert head at Bergen Live, in which Leven gets a section of conversation of his own.
inhalt: Portrait of Frank Nes, concert head at Bergen Live, in which Leven gets a section of conversation of his own. Nes was Leven's agent in Scandinavia from 1994 and accompanied him until his death; he says he spent a lot of time with him. He describes Leven as every record company's nightmare because he constantly released new albums, and the catalogue as full of great songs. Asked whether Doll by Doll recordings were made under LSD, Nes only confirms that Leven told many stories about it.

Nes calls Leven's solo work “Celtic Soul” and recommends *The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death* (especially “Call Mother a Lonely Field”), *Fairy Tales for Hardmen*, *Shining Brother, Shining Sister* and *Gothic Road*. The journalist recaps the end of Doll by Doll, the assault with two years of voice loss, and heroin. Nes tells of the funeral, where “Main Travelled Roads” was played in the church, and shows the order of service with lines from the Doll by Doll debut that seemed to anticipate Leven's fate.
zitate_kontext: Nes on Leven's flood of releases.

2017-06-28-scotch-whisky-magazine-ian-ra.kurz: Whisky conversation with Rankin in which each dram is paired with a piece of music. With Laphroaig, Leven's *Exit Wound* is heard: if Rebus is not listening to John Martyn, he listens to Leven, and *Fairy Tales for Hard Men* is “that's Rebus”.
inhalt: Whisky conversation with Rankin in which each dram is paired with a piece of music. With Laphroaig, Leven's *Exit Wound* is heard: if Rebus is not listening to John Martyn, he listens to Leven, and *Fairy Tales for Hard Men* is “that's Rebus”. Broom sums up that Leven got in touch after mentions on Rebus's playlist; stage shows and the CD *Jackie Leven Said* resulted. Rankin says Leven's manager cancelled a joint appointment, and three days later Leven was dead; Leven dealt with the diagnosis by going for a walk with a bottle of whisky.
zitate_kontext: Rankin on how Leven dealt with the diagnosis.

2017-08-16-no-more-big-wheels-doll-by-do.kurz: The long retrospective combines an in-depth appreciation of the Doll by Doll albums with the author's recollections and older passages of conversation.
inhalt: The long retrospective combines an in-depth appreciation of the Doll by Doll albums with the author's recollections and older passages of conversation. At its centre at first is “Gypsy Blood”, which the author calls his irreplaceable favourite album. He describes its shift from accessible songs to menacing, many-layered soundscapes and explains its commercial ineffectiveness partly by the band's difficult public image.

Next comes the third album, of the same name as the band: the text emphasises the attempt at the time to write more comprehensible songs without giving up emotional intensity. In the reproduced answers Leven explains his changed idea of entertainment and the relationship between personal experience, psychedelia and song construction. The author describes his own encounters with Leven as friendly and funny, alongside his intimidating stage presence.

The account extends beyond the end of the group to the later solo career. It ends with the note that Jo Shaw and Dave McIntosh played with friends in a pub in Cricklewood in 2012 in memory of Leven. This adds to the existing trail to the tribute evening, but gives neither an exact date nor the name of the pub here. Older interview quotations and retrospectives from 2007 are interwoven with the narrator's present of 2017.

2018-01-17-norman-lamont-jackie-leven-be.kurz: The Scottish singer-songwriter Norman Lamont (self-description: “came of age in the early 70s”) tells how he discovered Leven twice without hearing him first: in 1981, after a press review, he bought Doll by Doll's single “Main Travelled Roads”, and in 1994 likewise the EP *Songs from the Argyll Cycle*, which…
inhalt: The Scottish singer-songwriter Norman Lamont (self-description: “came of age in the early 70s”) tells how he discovered Leven twice without hearing him first: in 1981, after a press review, he bought Doll by Doll's single “Main Travelled Roads”, and in 1994 likewise the EP *Songs from the Argyll Cycle*, which remains among his favourite recordings to this day. In the 1990s he wrote a song inspired by “Main Travelled Roads”, sent Leven a cassette and received a handwritten letter back immediately (as an image in the post, with a note from Leven about a new album “out on Sept 18th”). The song “Touched Again” was later recorded by Lamont's band The Invisible Helpers and can be heard in the post.

The main part is an outline of the work from a fan's perspective: Doll by Doll (with a longer quotation from Neil McCormick), assault and addiction, founding of the CORE Trust with Carol Wolf (now WDP), support from Princess Diana – Leven credited her with getting him singing again. Lamont stresses that he had heard the Diana story in several versions, which grew with the telling; an embedded audio recording gives the best version (backstage at a charity event, with Wayne Sleep). Then follow Robert Bly and the men's movement, Leven's own open guitar tuning, for which there is no tablature, the relationship with Ian Rankin, the pseudonyms and Leven's notebook text on the “code of the travelling man”, which Deborah Greenwood gave to Paul Du Noyer after his death.
zitate_kontext: Lamont on Leven's way of telling stories.

2019-01-20-the-afterword-jackie-leven.kurz: Gary links a short YouTube video in which Leven speaks (first announced as a documentary, then corrected: “just him talking”).
inhalt: Gary links a short YouTube video in which Leven speaks (first announced as a documentary, then corrected: “just him talking”). From this develops a thread of memories with a good 25 posts (Jan.–June 2019). “Artery” owns all the CDs, claims to have seen Leven almost a hundred times and wishes for vinyl or box-set editions from Cooking Vinyl. SteveT describes Leven's stage image – barefoot, in shorts, seemingly indifferent – and relays a statement by Michael Weston King: Leven was a perfectionist, sober before concerts, and expected the same of fellow musicians. retropath2 half disagrees: he says Leven often asked the audience on stage for a large vodka with lime in a pint glass. A debate follows about the pronunciation “Leeven” rather than “Levven” and a running gag with Leven's stage line “Sting is dead”.

retropath2 says Leven drew him into the old blog of The Word magazine, where he met a community of Leven devotees – forerunner of the Afterword community. Kaisfatdad saw Leven in Stockholm, most recently at the club Debaser. Baron Harkonnen says he discovered the band through an NME review of the album *Doll by Doll* in a pub in Wigan, found Leven again through Mike Scott's thanks on *Fisherman's Blues* and bought *The Mystery of Love* in Rhyl in 1994. Nick L says his future wife named Leven as her favourite musician when they met. Feedback_File and Gary name “Main Travelled Roads” as their favourite song; a link leads to the (according to YouTube comments, only) Doll by Doll film footage.

2019-04-10-norman-lamont-drinking-with-j.kurz: Norman Lamont publishes, with permission, the recollections of a reader, “Tom in Glasgow”.
inhalt: Norman Lamont publishes, with permission, the recollections of a reader, “Tom in Glasgow”. Tom knew Doll by Doll only vaguely and discovered Leven in the mid-1990s through the library CD *The Mystery of Love*; “Call Mother A Lonely Field” blew him away. After that he saw him regularly in Glasgow and Edinburgh. In 2000 he got tickets for a recording at the Glasgow club The Ferry, filmed by STV – as he remembers it, for an episode of the programme *Artery* about Leven; on watching it again on YouTube, however, the concert excerpts did not come from the Ferry, possibly because of technical problems.

Through a companion he met the painter Allan there, whose pictures Leven used for Haunted Valley live albums; Allan later introduced him to Leven, and the three of them occasionally sat in the bar after concerts or watched the main act together when Leven was playing as support (named: Caravan at the Ferry). Away from the stage Leven was somewhat milder, but a masterly storyteller, of whom one never knew whether a story was true. Tom says Leven mocked a musician who had asked him about his guitar before a concert as nosy, right there on stage. In 2009 he saw him with his future wife at the Tolbooth in Stirling. The high point was a concert at the Woodend Bowling and Tennis Club in Glasgow in November 2010: Leven talked as much as he played, overran heavily, and a coarse story about a night-time photo shoot behind the central station brought the house down. He missed the summer 2011 gig at King Tut's; tickets for another Woodend concert in autumn 2011 expired because Leven died a few weeks before. He says he knew Leven was ill, but not how seriously.

2020-03-09-fife-today-why-johnny-cash-wo.kurz: Report from the Johnny Cash festival “Cash Back In Fife” at the Woodside Hotel, Aberdour, curated around Dean Owens.
inhalt: Report from the Johnny Cash festival “Cash Back In Fife” at the Woodside Hotel, Aberdour, curated around Dean Owens. In the Saturday afternoon slot Ian Rankin appeared with a handful of Leven CD covers and told Leven's life story along with lyrics – of the “all-too forgotten Fifer” who discovered Cash late. The author points to the approaching tenth anniversary of the death and hopes Rankin won new listeners.

2020-03-13-americana-uk-cash-back-in-fif.kurz: Kerr gives a very positive account of the first Cash Back In Fife weekend and describes a separate programme item in memory of Leven.
inhalt: Kerr gives a very positive account of the first Cash Back In Fife weekend and describes a separate programme item in memory of Leven. Ian Rankin read lyrics and talked about his friend while Dean Owens accompanied him, improvising on acoustic guitar; the announced starting point “Elegy for Johnny Cash” led to a broader look back at Leven.

2020-06-18-the-afterword-remembering-jac.kurz: Opening post by the forum user “Moonidus” for Leven's 70th birthday (18.06.2020): he says he organised a bench in London's Soho Square in his memory, near the bench for Kirsty MacColl – both wrote songs about the square.
inhalt: Opening post by the forum user “Moonidus” for Leven's 70th birthday (18.06.2020): he says he organised a bench in London's Soho Square in his memory, near the bench for Kirsty MacColl – both wrote songs about the square. He calls on people to listen to a song, drink a “wee dram” and visit the square after lockdown.

Eleven replies, all from 18 to 20.06.2020. The regular users (Artery, SteveT, Baron Harkonnen, Vulpes Vulpes, Lando Cakes, retropath2) express admiration, call Leven one of the best British songwriters and storytellers and miss unreleased material at Cooking Vinyl. retropath2 reports Facebook mentions, including at the Wickham Festival – Wickham in Hampshire was Leven's home in his late years; Deborah Greenwood is pleased when his memory is kept alive. Sitheref2409 tongue-in-cheek criticises a lyric line. The most important is the post by “Bogart” (20.06.): on Thursday evening (18.06.2020) there was a virtual concert, organised by Deborah Greenwood and Jinder, with cover versions by musicians from Leven's circle – named are Deborah, Jinder, the former Doll by Doll members Jo Shaw and Kevin Foster, Tom Burgess – as well as Ian Rankin, who read Leven's lyrics. Available in the Facebook group “Burning The Box Of Beautiful Things” and on YouTube. Toasts to Leven were drunk with “toffee vodka”.

2020-06-19-jindersongs-jackie-leven-at-7.autor: Jinder (JinderSongs) with Deborah Greenwood and others
2020-06-19-jindersongs-jackie-leven-at-7.kurz: A video of a good 85 minutes, compiled for Leven's 70th birthday from contributions the participants recorded at home (Covid period).
inhalt: A video of a good 85 minutes, compiled for Leven's 70th birthday from contributions the participants recorded at home (Covid period). The opening is spoken by a woman in Leven's music room in a house built around 1700 in Botley, Hampshire, with Leven's Morgan guitar – from context Deborah Greenwood; she sings “Universal Blue” and tells how the song came about in the kitchen of friendly hosts after a long walk up the Cheviot. Ian Rankin reads song lyrics (“My Spanish Dad”, later “The Innocent Railway” from “Lovers at the Gun Club” and a piece from “Forbidden Songs of the Dying West”). Iona of the Doghouse Roses remembers seeing Leven as a guest of Willard Grant Conspiracy and plays “Elegy for Johnny Cash”. Henry Priestman (The Yachts) reads from his diary of 12 April 1979 about a Doll by Doll concert at Eric's in Liverpool, tells of keyboard recordings in Bryn Derwen with producer David Wrench and of Leven crediting him on later albums for instruments he never played, and plays “Paris Blues”. Further contributions: “Revenge of Memory” in Leven's tuning, a reading of “The Dent in the Fender and the Wheel of Fate”, “Main Travelled Roads”, a poem, Rachel Taylor-Beales with a song of her own about Leven, a duo with Kevin Foster from Cricklewood with a song Leven wrote at 16, a contribution on “Silver Blaze” and, at the end, a song by the host with Jinder as backing voice. Tenor: loving, private memorial event of the inner circle.
zitate_kontext: Priestman relays the producer's explanation for Leven's imaginary credits.

2020-09-04-popklikk-en-musikalsk-helt.kurz: Long conversation from 2007 in the bar of the former Hotel Viking in Oslo, (re)published on Popklikk.
inhalt: Long conversation from 2007 in the bar of the former Hotel Viking in Oslo, (re)published on Popklikk. Occasion: the spring album *Oh What a Blow That Phantom Dealt Me!* (title after Cervantes), Doll by Doll reissues and many concerts in Norway. Leven says he deliberately works with blues ideas in order to become more direct, and keeps around 150 small red notebooks; what goes on an album is decided by intuition. Melancholy is a necessary part of life (he takes up the Greek term “pothos”), music a kind of therapy; Munch's “Scream” runs through as a comparison.

On songs: “Another Man's Rain” goes back to a train journey to Bergen on which he was overwhelmed by memories of youth at a glacier; the same day he saw a defeat of the Norwegian football team in Bergen and heard Bertine Zetlitz in Førde. “The Kings of Infinite Space” was inspired by Bacharach and 70s crime series (Rockford, Columbo), the title by Shakespeare, his hairdresser contributed lines. He praises Judee Sill's *Heartfood*, wrote a song for a Kevin Coyne tribute and says he discovered Böcklin's “Isle of the Dead” (cover of *The Mystery of Love*) in New York; because the painting had belonged to Hitler, the album sold unexpectedly well in Germany – a typical Leven punchline. On the voice he names Fontella Bass's “Rescue Me”; he does not see Doll by Doll as punk but alongside Dexys and The Pop Group; *Gypsy Blood* is the best album, and an album lost by Warner should be released with further material. Norwegian matters: a refused whisky in a pub in Kabelvåg, amazement at Norwegian drinking customs, favourite authors Rolf Jacobsen, Olav Hauge and Hamsun's *Sult*.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his way of working.

2021-05-jackieleven-co-uk-biography-grae.kurz: Essay by the Scottish music journalist Graeme Thomson, dated “Edinburgh, May 2021”, as the official biography of the revived website.
inhalt: Essay by the Scottish music journalist Graeme Thomson, dated “Edinburgh, May 2021”, as the official biography of the revived website. Thomson begins with his first meeting: Leven came back from Norway, shaken by the homeless people and addicts at Oslo bus station, and said he was “too connected to the pain of other people”. He characterises Leven's music as a journey between consolation and despair, and his themes (angry, damaged men, loneliness, violence, but also tenderness, humour, political anger). Life: born Alan Moffat on 18.06.1950, father a London Irishman, mother from north-east England, Kirkcaldy High School like Gordon Brown, feeling of being branded because of Romany background, left home at 16, *Control* in 1971 (he chose the pseudonym, by his own account, to evade the authorities), from 1975 in London, Doll by Doll with Joe Shaw and Dave MacIntosh in the squat in Maida Vale, thrown off a Hawkwind tour, Leven's later admission that he had been episodically “genuinely mentally ill” at the time; split in 1983, Virgin contract, assault in 1984 (colleagues looked for him and rescued him), two years with barely a voice, lost his falsetto, several years of heroin, CORE Trust; from 1994 over 30 albums including fan-club CDs and Sir Vincent Lone. Thomson describes the stage presence (Johnny Dowd: “Jackie was real”) and his own last concert experience at the Cabaret Voltaire in Edinburgh on 11.08.2011; Leven died three months and three days later of pancreatic cancer. Ending with Ian Rankin and the line from “Main Travelled Roads”.

2021-07-20-the-guardian-ian-rankin-jacki.kurz: On the occasion of the compilation *Straight Outta Caledonia*, Ian Rankin (as told to Robin Denselow) recounts his relationship with Leven.
inhalt: On the occasion of the compilation *Straight Outta Caledonia*, Ian Rankin (as told to Robin Denselow) recounts his relationship with Leven. He says he was a late discoverer: Doll by Doll passed him by, and only a review about a songwriter “from Fife” made him curious. While working on a Rebus novel he listened to *Shining Brother Shining Sister* and had Rebus listen to Leven in the next book. Leven read the mention on a plane over Scandinavia and got in touch via the publisher; Rankin then attended a midnight concert at the Edinburgh Fringe in a converted church and at first took the shuffling Leven for the roadie – until he heard the voice.

Rankin sums up Leven's life as a series of reinventions (folk troubadour, Doll by Doll, assault in Camden, heroin, founding an addiction-aid charity, solo career) and describes his themes: fragile masculinity, the ballad tradition, estrangement on tour, provocation (*The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ*). Leven was a “magpie” who played with African, Arab and jazz musicians, and a great Johnny Cash fan.

On the stage show: Leven proposed a joint reading with songs for Celtic Connections; Rankin proposed writing a story specially on Leven themes, to which Leven would respond with new songs – this is how *Jackie Leven Said* came about, performed and recorded several times; Leven wrote *The Haunting of John Rebus* specially for it. The rider anecdote: the first tour stop was the Southbank in London, and Leven ordered “one uncooked haggis for every venue” for Rankin. After Leven's death Rankin named *Standing in Another Man's Grave* after a misheard Leven title and *Saints of the Shadow Bible* after a Leven line. Further collaboration would certainly have come. Rankin laments the ignorance of the British media; in Norway Leven is revered.

2021-07-20-the-guardian-kommentare-ian-r.kurz: Beneath Ian Rankin's piece (as told to Robin Denselow) are 151 reader comments from 20/21.07.2021 – the most extensive publicly readable thread of memories about Leven.
inhalt: Beneath Ian Rankin's piece (as told to Robin Denselow) are 151 reader comments from 20/21.07.2021 – the most extensive publicly readable thread of memories about Leven. It falls into three layers. First, Doll by Doll memories: one reader (“Kevin1957”) claims to have seen the band 58 times and says fans from the Midlands were allowed to stay overnight in the band's squat in Maida Vale; several readers describe the Hawkwind tour around 1979 at the Hammersmith Odeon, where Hawkwind fans shouted down the support band, threw objects and some stormed the stage until the curtain fell; according to others the band was later thrown off the tour (allegedly because of Hawkwind's beer, according to Kevin1957 after sabotage of sound and lights). Further traces: concerts at the Red Cow (Hammersmith), Taboo Club Scarborough (in front of about 20 listeners), Albany Empire Deptford, Dingwalls 1982, The Venue, a cancellation at Futurama 1981 in Stafford and a fight with a heckler in Chesterfield.

Second, memories of the solo artist: appearances at the 12 Bar Club (Leven threw chattering guests out himself; an evening of audience requests only), at The Bell in Bath (Leven is said to have called it “family”), at the Queen's Hall Edinburgh with David Thomas and Linda Thompson, in Sidmouth, Otley, Trowbridge 2010, Exeter, Tavistock, Hebden Bridge, Manchester shortly before his death and several times in Bergen. A former CORE Trust funding officer remembers weekly morning sessions in Leven's kitchen in Ladbroke Grove; a female musician thanks Leven for getting her into a major festival in Bergen. “mikeollier” relays Leven's claim that Princess Diana brought him back to singing – he insisted it was the plain truth. Third, debates about fame, Rebus and the free CDs from Uncut (2000/2001) and The Word.

2021-07-21-at-the-barrier-straight-outta.kurz: Barlass presents Leven as an artist loved by connoisseurs but overlooked by the wider public, quotes Ian Rankin's praise from the liner notes and summarises the biography.
inhalt: Barlass presents Leven as an artist loved by connoisseurs but overlooked by the wider public, quotes Ian Rankin's praise from the liner notes and summarises the biography. He goes through the titles (“The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ”, “Heartsick Land”, “Dagenham Dream”, “Irresistible Romance”, “Live or Die”, “Single Father”) and praises the voice as one of the richest you could hear. Very positive tone, no rating.

2021-07-21-the-afterword-jackie-levens-g.kurz: The occasion is Ian Rankin's Guardian piece of 20 July 2021 on the compilation *Straight Outta Caledonia*.
inhalt: The occasion is Ian Rankin's Guardian piece of 20 July 2021 on the compilation *Straight Outta Caledonia*. The thread (about 35 posts, 21–27 July 2021) first clears up the confusion between the compilation (Leven recordings only, ten tracks, track list posted) and the tribute album *The Wanderer*, announced at the same time; SteveT reports that Michael Weston King had spoken on Facebook of three Leven releases. Several users praise the free CD given away by The Word magazine after Leven's death as their way in.

The question of Leven's best-selling record leads to reminiscences: Kaisfatdad tells (as a retelling of Leven's stage anecdote) of an uninterested US marketing woman in New York and of concerts in Sweden before tiny audiences; retropath2 heard “I Say A Little Prayer” in 1994 on Janice Long's show on Radio Glastonbury. Jaygee links Neil McCormick's Telegraph blog about Leven and Ralph McTell meeting Gordon Brown at 10 Downing Street. Baron Harkonnen describes his path from “Main Travelled Roads” on the radio, via Mike Scott's thanks on *Fisherman's Blues*, to chancing upon *The Mystery of Love* in Rhyl in 1994; SteveT reads Scott's thanks as encouragement in a crisis.

The most personal contribution is Artery's: a fan since about 1995, he says he saw Leven over a hundred times in 15 years and knew him well, though he found him somewhat reserved in conversation; Leven played two sets at his 50th birthday party in 2005 (rider: one bottle of Smirnoff Black Label, untouched), and he was at the funeral – a deeply spiritual experience. SteveT tells the Midlands Arts Centre anecdote: during the interval he requested “Wrapped Up In Blue”, and Leven announced the song crudely as an audience request; Artery and retropath2 were at the same concert (audience about twelve). Artery also remembers a woman in the audience demanding her money back over his language while Leven was supporting the Oyster Band.
zitate_kontext: Artery on the concerts he attended.

2021-07-23-god-is-in-the-tv-straight-out.kurz: Jupp takes the term “cult artist” as his starting point and recommends the ten tracks as an ideal introduction to Leven's work.
inhalt: Jupp takes the term “cult artist” as his starting point and recommends the ten tracks as an ideal introduction to Leven's work. He praises the voice, which he says is neither too rough nor too smooth, and singles out “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” (produced by David Thomas), “Irresistible Romance” (“like Celtic Hall & Oates”), “Snow in Central Park” and “Poortoun”. Thanks go to Michael Kasparis of Night School, who released the record out of enthusiasm. No rating, very positive.

2021-07-23-the-wee-review-straight-outta.kurz: Maxwell praises Leven for being able to sing about heroin addiction, single parenthood and Jesus's sexual loneliness without sounding gloomy.
inhalt: Maxwell praises Leven for being able to sing about heroin addiction, single parenthood and Jesus's sexual loneliness without sounding gloomy. The selection is slim (fans would miss “Call Mother a Lonely Field”, for example) but wise; he places “Poortoun” alongside Billy Joel's “Allentown” and Springsteen's “Youngstown”. Verdict: an intelligent cross-section for newcomers. The page shows no visible star rating.

2021-07-24-the-courier-jackie-leven-the-.kurz: Feature by the Scottish music journalist David Pollock on the compilation Straight Outta Caledonia.
inhalt: Feature by the Scottish music journalist David Pollock on the compilation Straight Outta Caledonia. Deborah Greenwood, Leven's partner for the last 15 years, describes how much his origins mattered to him: he always had himself announced as “Jackie Leven from the Kingdom of Fife” and opened concerts with a joke about the wind in Fife. Michael Kasparis (Night School Records, Apostille) says Molly Nilsson played him Leven on a car journey to Manchester; “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” was a revelation to him, the compilation is a personal selection from around 35 albums, and the title is a nod to NWA. A short biography follows (Control 1971, Doll by Doll, Gilmour recordings discovered later, Concrete Bulletproof Invisible with Glen Matlock). Greenwood relates that a school librarian led the boy, who was often banished to the library, to the Russian poets; his imagery (sky, reservoirs, hills) and characters such as “Jim o' Windygates” came from Fife. Kasparis compares Leven's devotion with soul (Otis Redding) and his kinship with Big Country, the Waterboys and Bert Jansch.

2021-08-04-backseat-mafia-album-review-j.kurz: Gannon welcomes the ten-song selection as an excellent introduction to Leven's catalogue. He particularly admires the narrative range, the vulnerability of the characters and the fusion of music and conflicting emotions; he gives no numerical rating.
inhalt: Gannon welcomes the ten-song selection as an excellent introduction to Leven's catalogue. He particularly admires the narrative range, the vulnerability of the characters and the fusion of music and conflicting emotions; he gives no numerical rating.

2021-09-09-the-scotsman-album-reviews-th.kurz: Lead item of a round-up review (four stars): Shepherd hails the tribute album curated by Michael Weston King for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death as a heartfelt homage that casts fresh light on Leven's “underrated” catalogue.
inhalt: Lead item of a round-up review (four stars): Shepherd hails the tribute album curated by Michael Weston King for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death as a heartfelt homage that casts fresh light on Leven's “underrated” catalogue. She highlights the contributions, mostly recorded in stripped-back form during the pandemic – James Yorkston (*Empty in Soho Square*), Kathryn Williams, Boo Hewerdine, Ralph McTell, Eliza Carthy, The Membranes (*More Than Human* by Doll by Doll), Tom Robinson, Rab Noakes (*Poortoun*) and Ian Rankin, who recites *Edinburgh Winter Blues* with Dean Owens. She names Deborah Greenwood's *Universal Blue* as the strongest contribution.

2021-09-10-uncut-straight-outta-caledoni.kurz: Rating 9/10. Dale recounts how the compilation came about: Night School boss Michael Kasparis got to know Leven through label artist Molly Nilsson, who in the liner notes calls “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” the best song ever.
inhalt: Rating 9/10. Dale recounts how the compilation came about: Night School boss Michael Kasparis got to know Leven through label artist Molly Nilsson, who in the liner notes calls “The Sexual Loneliness of Jesus Christ” the best song ever. He warns against reading the songs only through Leven's biography and highlights the different sides (troubadour, folk singer in the line of Dick Gaughan, soul in “Irresistible Romance”). The 1990s production, he says, gives the songs a peculiar “spectrality”.

2021-09-15-the-telegraph-strong-on-the-o.kurz: The major retrospective for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death, published in the week of the tribute album The Wanderer.
inhalt: The major retrospective for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death, published in the week of the tribute album The Wanderer. Graeme Thomson notes that Leven's death in 2011 went almost unnoticed but that his reputation has been rising since (the compilation Straight Outta Caledonia, a tribute album with Rankin, Kathryn Williams, Tom Robinson, James Yorkston, Eliza Carthy, Ralph McTell). Michael Weston King explains his initiative for the album. Kathryn Williams, who supported Leven in Aberdeen in 2000, stresses his love of experimentation. Biography: Alan Moffatt, father London-Irish, mother from north-east England, Kirkcaldy High School in Gordon Brown's time, left home married at 16, Control 1971, Doll by Doll at Automatic/Warner, thrown off a Hawkwind tour. Tom Robinson describes Leven at the Reading Festival in 1979, staring down the booing crowd and draining a can of beer. Mick Houghton tells how Nick Kent disappeared into a squat in Maida Vale for an NME cover story. After the split, a contract with Virgin, the 1984 attack after a night session, heroin, withdrawal in 1985, the Core Trust with Carol Wolf in Victorian cottages in Marylebone, now part of the Westminster Drug Project and recipient of half the proceeds of The Wanderer. Diana, as patron, urged Leven to sing at a charity lunch; he sang “The Bonnie Earl of Moray”. Over 30 albums from 1994. Rankin reads the songs as a dissection of Scottish machismo; anecdotes about raw haggis as Rankin's rider and kalimotxo as Leven's drink. Verdict: a decade on, Leven's music seems more urgent than ever.
zitate_kontext: Ian Rankin on Leven's male characters.

2021-09-20-cover-me-review-the-wanderer-.kurz: Detailed track-by-track review of the tribute album by a self-declared fan who saw Leven live several times.
inhalt: Detailed track-by-track review of the tribute album by a self-declared fan who saw Leven live several times. By way of introduction the author sketches Leven's biography (Doll by Doll, the attack, heroin, CORE Trust; half the proceeds to the Westminster Drug Project) and his output, which Martin Goldschmidt at Cooking Vinyl is said to have supported against commercial good sense; he assigns the alter ego Sir Vincent Lone to the Glitterhouse label and *Chip Pan Fire* to the pseudonym Jackie Balfour. He describes Leven's solo performances (guitar technique, microphoned foot-stomping, stories between the songs).

On the project: Michael Weston King, whose album *A Decent Man* (2003) Leven produced and whose live band he is said to have led, always praised Leven and played Leven tribute nights of his own. The two CDs are titled “Gentle Man” and “Hard Man”. The author praises Disc 1 almost throughout (Eliza Carthy's Brecht/Weill-like *The Garden*, Jeb Loy Nichols, James Yorkston, Lou Dalgleish, Ian Rankin's spoken *Edinburgh Winter Blues* with Dean Owens, which sounds eerily like Leven, Deborah Greenwood's *Universal Blue*). Disc 2 is said to be more uneven; highlights are Dog House Roses (*Elegy for Johnny Cash*), Johnny Dowd's *Farm Boy* and Michael Cosgrave's own composition *The View from Shit Creek*; he is less convinced by Tom Robinson, Rab Noakes, Levi Henriksen's *Just Like Jackie Leven* and Liam Carson's spoken *I Weep*. Verdict: largely very good, a little too long; the booklet contains reminiscences from almost everyone involved.

2021-09-30-the-afterword-seeing-double.kurz: retropath2 is giving away duplicate Bandcamp CDs he received, including the Leven tribute album; this turns into an exchange about Leven-related activity in autumn 2021. Kaisfatdad quotes a post on the official Facebook page about the new website jackieleven.co.uk and the new official YouTube channel (JLeven.lnk.to/youtube).
inhalt: retropath2 is giving away duplicate Bandcamp CDs he received, including the Leven tribute album; this turns into an exchange about Leven-related activity in autumn 2021. Kaisfatdad quotes a post on the official Facebook page about the new website jackieleven.co.uk and the new official YouTube channel (JLeven.lnk.to/youtube). Bogart mentions the reissue of *The Mystery of Love* (CD with the EP *The Right To Remain Silent*), two memorial concerts in London (11 November 2021) and Glasgow (9 December 2021) with Deborah Greenwood, bootleg videos in circulation, and the track “Finest Hour” by Alan Moffatt on a 1971 folk compilation. He also mentions the original Facebook group “Burning The Box Of Beautiful Things” as a refuge for many members of the old Yahoo group (“Levenites”).

2021-10-06-the-afterword-atm-jackie-leve.kurz: “ATM” stands in the forum for a request for recommendations (“Ask The Members”): fitterstoke, who has just been given the tribute album, asks where a newcomer should start.
inhalt: “ATM” stands in the forum for a request for recommendations (“Ask The Members”): fitterstoke, who has just been given the tribute album, asks where a newcomer should start. Around 25 replies (6/7 October 2021) add up to a kind of collective fan discography. Mentioned are *Oh What A Blow That Phantom Dealt Me* (a way in via Ian Rankin), *Defending Ancient Springs* (for “Single Father” and the cover of “You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'”), *Lovers at the Gun Club*, *Shining Brother Shining Sister*, *Fairytales for Hard Men*, *Night Lilies*, *Creatures of Light and Darkness*, *Forbidden Songs*, *Gothic Road* (with Ralph McTell), the four double CDs of the *Haunted Year* series as an entry to the Haunted Valley fan-club releases, and *Wayside Shrines* with Michael Cosgrave. retropath2 recommends the LP-length version of *Songs From the Argyll Cycle* and warns that Robert Bly's narrating voice on *The Mystery of Love* may put people off.

Bogart relays Leven's own story, expressly given with a caveat, that there was meant to be a video for “You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'” in which Leven and David Thomas dance in women's clothes on the beach at Brighton; he points to *Chip Pan Fire* (as Jackie Balfour) with the stage speech “Sting Is Dead” and to the whisky “Leven's Lament – The Lonely Spirit of the Glen”. retropath2 explains that the first CD edition of *The Mystery of Love* was a double jewel case with an empty second tray, which he only filled with the “Mystery Supplement EP” (promo). Vulpes Vulpes came to Leven by buying Doll by Doll's *Grand Passion* from a bargain bin.

2021-10-09-dagsavisen-jackie-leven-var-e.titel: [Print version] Jackie Leven var en av verdens beste kulthelter
2021-10-09-dagsavisen-jackie-leven-var-e.kurz: Fully legible print version of the Plus article. Double-page spread with photos (Leven in Norway in 1998, Doll by Doll in 1981, the whisky “Leven's Lament” – with the note that it has been claimed these were his own labels on other people's bottles –, Levi Henriksen).
inhalt: Fully legible print version of the Plus article. Double-page spread with photos (Leven in Norway in 1998, Doll by Doll in 1981, the whisky “Leven's Lament” – with the note that it has been claimed these were his own labels on other people's bottles –, Levi Henriksen).

Rakvaag reviews the tribute album *The Wanderer – A Tribute to Jackie Leven* and the compilation *Straight Outta Caledonia* (both Cooking Vinyl) and recalls Leven's Norwegian connection: *Fairy Tales for Hardmen* reached number 40 on the VG chart in 1997, which a British magazine noted as a near-improbable event; the album ends with Rolf Jacobsen's “Sunflower” in Robert Bly's translation. Leven had already played in Norway in 1966 as guitarist for the blues singer Doris Henderson (his own statement to Dagsavisen: his first trip abroad as a professional musician), and later liked playing in small places on the periphery. Mentioned are “Rainy Day Bergen Women”, the live album *Men in Prison* from Bergen's county prison, and the discovery, on a flight from Bergen to Tromsø, that he appears in a Rankin novel as John Rebus's favourite artist; Leven said at the time that he and Rankin wrote about men who experience their inner lives as a mystery. The compilation shows him from the crooner side, at times like a Roy Orbison of our time.

The second focus is Levi Henriksen, who discovered Leven late through an Uncut interview with a CD, listened to nothing else for a month and sensed a kinship in background and view of humanity. His contribution to the tribute, “Just Like Jackie Leven”, is a translated version of his Babylon Badlands song “Jackie Leven sier det snart skal snø”, the first song he wrote for the band, about the healing power of music. Other tribute contributors: Ralph McTell, Kathryn Williams, James Yorkston, Tom Robinson.

2021-10-09-el-pais-jackie-leven-belleza-.kurz: Major Babelia article for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death, prompted by the compilation “Straight Outta Caledonia” and the tribute album “The Wanderer”.
inhalt: Major Babelia article for the tenth anniversary of Leven's death, prompted by the compilation “Straight Outta Caledonia” and the tribute album “The Wanderer”. It opens with Ian Rankin's farewell tweet of 2011; Leven, it says, was ignored by the public (apart from Scandinavian and German fans), not by the critics. Fernández Escobar describes the stylistic breadth (rock, British folk, Celtic soul, Americana, sixties pop) and opens with “The Sexual Loneliness Of Jesus Christ”, which contains the voices of laid-off shipyard workers.

Biographically the text largely follows Leven's own account of himself: he felt pushed to the margins by his mixed background (Irish and Roma blood) and led a nomadic life between Cornwall, Glasgow, Dublin, Berlin and Madrid; in Franco's Spain his debut “Control” appeared in 1973 on Movieplay (Madrid) as John St. Field, the pseudonym being due to a police matter. Doll by Doll came from the London squatting scene, four studio albums, “Gypsy Blood” as the high point; thrown off tours with Devo and Hawkwind, John Peel turned away; the last album effectively a Leven solo project with David Gilmour. Then a Virgin contract for a solo album, then the attack, loss of voice, heroin. After withdrawal, the founding of the CORE Trust; Leven says the visit of Princess Diana brought him back to music; the band attempt Concrete Bulletproof Invisible with Glen Matlock. On “The Wanderer”: contributions from Rankin (spoken word), Johnny Dowd, Michael Cosgrave, Ralph McTell, Eliza Carthy, James Yorkston and others; David Thomas and Ron Sexsmith are absent. Three song boxes: “Main Travelled Roads”, “The Sexual Loneliness Of Jesus Christ”, “Single Father”. Tone: a passionate rehabilitation.
zitate_kontext: Mishima quotation from “Main Travelled Roads”, giving the title.
Leven quotation about his life path (Spanish translation).

2021-10-19-blabber-n-smoke-the-wanderer-.kurz: The Glasgow Americana blogger Paul Kerr reviews the tribute album as a “labour of love”: 22 tracks, all Leven songs except Weston King's own homage *The Final Reel* and contributions from Levi Henriksen & Babylon Badlands and from Liam Carson with Knut Buen.
inhalt: The Glasgow Americana blogger Paul Kerr reviews the tribute album as a “labour of love”: 22 tracks, all Leven songs except Weston King's own homage *The Final Reel* and contributions from Levi Henriksen & Babylon Badlands and from Liam Carson with Knut Buen. He misses Leven himself; Weston King and Ian Rankin (with Dean Owens, *Edinburgh Winter Blues*) come closest. Highlighted are Deborah Greenwood, Boo Hewerdine, Kathryn Williams, Arksong, James Yorkston, Lou Dalgleish, Andy White, Johnny Dowd's “unhinged” *Farm Boy* and Rab Noakes' *Poortoun*. Positive overall; refers to *Straight Outta Caledonia* and the reissue of *The Mystery of Love* (November 2021).

2022-03-25-americana-uk-interview-michae.kurz: Weston King explains how “The Struggle”, his first solo album in ten years, came about.
inhalt: Weston King explains how “The Struggle”, his first solo album in ten years, came about. For Leven research the conversation about “Theory of Truthmakers” is the most productive. King says their mutual friend Alan Black had kept an unpublished handwritten lyric by Leven. Leven had written it during a train journey they made together and left it with Black. When King approached the artist about the cover of the tribute record “The Wanderer”, he learned of this text.

King wanted to set it to music and release it on the memorial record but did not finish in time. So he recorded the piece for “The Struggle”. By his account the handwriting is reproduced in the booklet. The string-like sounds were contributed by Michael Cosgrave; King had expressly asked him for a sound reminiscent of Leven's records. For the brightening in the chorus King also had Scott Walker in mind.

The rest of the interview deals with King's orientation towards songwriters of the late sixties and early seventies and the recordings with Clovis Phillips in Wales. The story of the Leven lyric is King's recollection; the manuscript itself was not examined here.

2022-05-18-say-it-with-garage-flowers-mi.kurz: Telephone interview with Michael Weston King about his first solo album in ten years, *The Struggle* (2022, recorded in Newtown, Wales, mixed with Colin Elliot in Sheffield).
inhalt: Telephone interview with Michael Weston King about his first solo album in ten years, *The Struggle* (2022, recorded in Newtown, Wales, mixed with Colin Elliot in Sheffield). Two songs concern Jackie Leven directly.

*The Final Reel* was written about Leven, in the style of a “Celtic soul singer” who was strongly influenced by Van Morrison. Weston King tells how it came about: in the week before Leven's death he was on his way to a concert in Perth, drove past Loch Leven, stopped, walked along the shore and phoned Leven, who by then was in hospital and was not to leave it. They chatted and laughed; it was their last conversation. The song draws on that scene and their years together as wandering singers – they played “hundreds” of concerts together. (The song had previously also appeared on the tribute album *The Wanderer*, 2021.)

*Theory of Truthmakers* is based on unpublished Leven lines: Leven wrote them on a journey they made together and gave them to the Glasgow painter Allan Black, whose picture he had also used for an album. Black kept them as a souvenir and sent them to Weston King, who set them to music. The song was originally meant for the tribute album he curated but was not finished in time. Musically, for the chorus he aimed at something “big” like *Heroes* or a Scott Walker song.

2022-06-02-the-afterword-jackie-levens-7.kurz: Moonidus invites people to an informal gathering at Leven's bench in Soho Square (south side of the gardens) for his 72nd birthday (Saturday, 18 June 2022), at midday, possibly followed by the Nellie Dean pub in Dean Street.
inhalt: Moonidus invites people to an informal gathering at Leven's bench in Soho Square (south side of the gardens) for his 72nd birthday (Saturday, 18 June 2022), at midday, possibly followed by the Nellie Dean pub in Dean Street. The replies (2–6 June 2022) are mostly apologies because of distance, combined with toasts and reminiscences. Gatz relates that in the Facebook group “London Urbanist Oddities” a cousin of Leven's responded to a photo of the bench; he had not known about it. Razor Boy and others only came to Leven through the free CD from The Word magazine. SteveT again mentions his ticket for a Birmingham concert that was cancelled shortly before Leven's death.

The most productive strand concerns the second bench, on Paxos: Bogart was on Corfu in 2022 and wanted to visit the bench and the taverna that Leven is said to have frequented there; Moonidus had read that the bench had been damaged. Bogart then relays a notice (translated from Greek) from the Paxos municipality: the bench designed by Sam Khaleq and paid for by Deborah Greenwood, at the entrance to the Old Customs House in Loggos, suddenly disappeared in early November 2021; a fisherman from Gaios found the backrest on the shore; the residents wanted to restore it at their own expense. Chrisf finally quotes from an Ian Rankin interview in The Times (4 June 2022) in which Rankin calls Leven underrated and points to *Straight Outta Caledonia*.

2022-08-01-noejesguiden-manadens-baesta-.kurz: Forshage emphatically recommends the vinyl reissue as a chance to discover Leven belatedly.
inhalt: Forshage emphatically recommends the vinyl reissue as a chance to discover Leven belatedly. He compares Leven's literary rock songs with Warren Zevon and explains the low public profile partly by the large number of releases and the pseudonyms; there is no score.

2022-10-mojo-jackie-leven-the-truth-is.kurz: Aizlewood's retrospective accompanies the reissue of “The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death”.
inhalt: Aizlewood's retrospective accompanies the reissue of “The Mystery of Love Is Greater Than the Mystery of Death”. The freely readable opening presents Leven as a well-read songwriter and impressive stage presence whose stories shaped his songs as much as his voice and guitar playing. Aizlewood visits Deborah Greenwood and describes the literary surroundings of Leven's work; Rilke is expressly named.

Greenwood comments on several of Leven's self-presentations. The well-known train encounter with Bob Dylan and the false news of Sting's death appear in the context of his invented stories. The legends on records and in side projects are also put into perspective: “Leven’s Lament” was ordinary Bell’s whisky with his own label. “Elegy for Johnny Cash” was recorded in Wales, contrary to the information on the sleeve; according to Greenwood, the involvement of Lebanese musicians explains the Beirut reference. Henry Priestman did in fact play on “Defending Ancient Springs”, but other corresponding album credits are inaccurate.

The opening section thus already offers concrete starting points for checking Leven's stories. These are statements by Greenwood in conversation with Aizlewood, not production records independently verified here. The later questioning of further companions in the full article remains unread.

2023-01-17-the-sunday-post-he-just-soake.kurz: Jamieson traces Leven's life from a conversation with Deborah Greenwood and links her retrospective with the announcement of the memorial evening “Leventime”.
inhalt: Jamieson traces Leven's life from a conversation with Deborah Greenwood and links her retrospective with the announcement of the memorial evening “Leventime”. The starting point is Greenwood's view that recognition of Leven could still grow after his death. She estimates his output at more than 300 songs and reports on the plan to compile song lyrics into a volume of poems. The article documents a plan in January 2023, not a publication that had already appeared.

Greenwood recalls her first personal meeting with Leven at London's 12 Bar Club in the mid-1990s. Before that she had sent him a fan letter. She describes a well-read, nature-loving person of very varied temperaments; the text sets admiration and difficult sides side by side. The details are her recollections, not an independently established chronology.

A separate section contains Stuart Maconie's appreciation of Leven's voice and his portrayal of male vulnerability. The announced tribute evening is to take place on 4 February 2023 at Òran Mór, with Ian Rankin, Boo Hewerdine, Jinder, Malcolm Lindsay and Greenwood, among others. The report also explains that the event was postponed from the previous year, when it was cancelled because of the pandemic.

2023-03-13-cd-junkie-215-doll-by-doll.kurz: 14-minute collector's video by the US journalist Stephen Schnee on the four Doll by Doll albums, with a medley at the end.
inhalt: 14-minute collector's video by the US journalist Stephen Schnee on the four Doll by Doll albums, with a medley at the end. He tells how in 1979/80, as a record buyer in Los Angeles, he came across “Remember” and “Gypsy Blood”, describes the band as uncategorisable between new wave and rock, calls “Gypsy Blood” the emotional masterpiece and entry-point album, the self-titled third album the most melodic (released in the US on MCA) and “Grand Passion” the weakest, with its dated production. Tone: enthusiastic recommendation.

inhalt: 19-minute overview of Leven's studio albums from “Control” (as John St. Field) through the 1983/84 singles, Concrete Bulletproof Invisible (1988) and the Cooking Vinyl years to “Wayside Shrines” (2011), including the pseudonyms Sir Vincent Lone and Jackie Balfour; ends with a medley. Schnee above all praises the warmth, tenderness and variety of the late work and Leven's generosity in giving label colleagues room on his albums. Tone: fan homage.

inhalt: On the 12th anniversary of Leven's death, Bogart points to the evening “Levenland” on Saturday, 18 November 2023, at the Betsey Trotwood pub in London, where Deborah Greenwood and Jinder celebrate Leven's songs and stories; he invites people to join the “Church of Leven” and drink toffee vodka. 2023-12-01-obladada-revisio-john-st-fiel.kurz: Detailed review of the Guerssen reissue of “Control” (2023) in the “Revisio” section.
inhalt: Detailed review of the Guerssen reissue of “Control” (2023) in the “Revisio” section. The album is uneven but at its best one of the most unusual, twisted works the editors have come across in a long time: pop and prog with lysergic lyrics. Highlighted are “Soft Lowland Tongue” (about the Border Reivers, with place references to the border region where the magazine is based), the almost eleven-minute “The Problem”, the sound collage “Dune Voices” and “Raerona”; “Ruins”, “I'm Always A Prinlaws Boy” and the more commercial pieces fall short. The background story (recorded in 1971 in an LSD haze, pseudonym because of trouble with the police, delayed release in Spain, rearrangement by Leven in the 1990s, Guerssen in the original sequence) is retold. Tone: enthusiastic (“imperfect perfection”).

2024-05-07-musikreviews-de-live-or-die-l.kurz: Very personal, rapturous review by editor-in-chief Thoralf Koß of the 4-CD box (MIG, 26 April 2024) with a 1999 solo concert and the 2004 concert with Michael Cosgrave in the Radio Bremen Sendesaal. The text begins with three quotations: a comment under the theArtsDesk obituary (with the closing line of “Main Travelled Roads”), the Tagesspiegel obituary of 17 November 2011 and the musikreviews comments of 2011, including Jochen König's criticism of the FAZ obituary. Koß praises Leven as one of the most likeable and honest musicians ever, compares him with Bob Dylan, Frank Zappa, Elvis Presley and above all Scott Walker, describes his “tramp outfit” and his refusal to give encores (“only idiots like Robbie Williams”). He praises the guitar playing, voice and sound quality. In a postscript he tells of a lengthy conversation with Leven at the Beatpol in Dresden about 15 years earlier and a signed CD “For Peace Comes Dropping Slow”. Tone: hymn, highest praise.

2024-06-20-eats-drinks-and-leaves-doll-b.kurz: Short profile of the journalist Tim Cooper (wrote for British daily newspapers, own punk fanzine “Cliché”) prompted by the song “Butcher Boy” from the debut.
inhalt: Short profile of the journalist Tim Cooper (wrote for British daily newspapers, own punk fanzine “Cliché”) prompted by the song “Butcher Boy” from the debut. Doll by Doll were a cult band of the punk/new wave era, carried by Leven's larger-than-life personality; live, Leven and guitarist Jo Shaw often physically menaced audience members. The band was thrown off tours with Devo and Hawkwind. An outline of Leven's life follows, with many familiar anecdotes (the attack, heroin, CORE Trust, a girlfriend lost to the Dalai Lama's bodyguard, Robert Bly). Tone: admiring.

2024-07-07-rocktimes-live-or-die-live-in.kurz: Positive review of the MIG box: CD 1–2 solo from the Bremen club Moments (1999), CD 3–4 with Michael Cosgrave (2004).
inhalt: Positive review of the MIG box: CD 1–2 solo from the Bremen club Moments (1999), CD 3–4 with Michael Cosgrave (2004). Praise for the fingerpicking, soft dark voice, audience interaction and stories that can be understood even with little English; comparison with Townes Van Zandt. Verdict: a “very successful affair”, three and a half hours of entertainment.

inhalt: Jaygee, who only discovered Leven around 2006 and never saw him live, recommends the 4-CD box *Live or Die* (radio recordings from Bremen, solo in 1999 and with Michael Cosgrave in 2004; attributed in the thread to Proper Records) as the “best bargain of the year”, with “Jim O'Windygates” and “Classic Northern Diversions” as highlights. In the replies SteveT repeats his Midlands Arts Centre anecdote (“Wrapped Up In Blue” as an audience request commented on crudely) and his ticket for the Kitchen Garden Cafe shortly before Leven's death; he relays Michael Weston King saying that Leven seemed relaxed but was the most professional musician he had ever worked with on stage. inhalt: Epstein pays tribute to Leven as a great songwriter and storyteller who never played the same thing twice live; the two Bremen concerts (Club Moments, May 1999, solo; Sendesaal Radio Bremen, March 2004) prove it. 2024-12-28-toppermost-doll-by-doll.kurz: Toppermost piece presenting Doll by Doll through ten selected songs, written by a fan who often saw the band and Leven as a solo artist live (short biography at the end: lives near Brighton).
inhalt: Toppermost piece presenting Doll by Doll through ten selected songs, written by a fan who often saw the band and Leven as a solo artist live (short biography at the end: lives near Brighton). He sketches the origin of the band name (E. E. Cummings), the line-up, Leven's earlier history (duo Saint Judas with Colin Soutar around 1969, album “Control” as John St Field) and his literary sources (James Wright, Blake, Rilke, Robert Bly, Anna Akhmatova). Discussed are, among others, “More Than Human” and the B-side “The Fountain Is Red, The Fountain Is White” (presumably inspired by Baudelaire) from “Remember”, “Hell Games”, “Stripshow”, “The Human Face” and “Highland Rain” from “Gypsy Blood”, “Those In Peril” and “Main Travelled Roads” from the third album, and “Lonely Kind of Show” and “So Long Kid” from “Grand Passion”. The author recalls often seeing Leven in the late 1970s with friends at the Warwick Castle pub in Maida Vale – the loudest group at the bar, occasionally brawling. He mentions a German TV recording of “Main Travelled Roads” (1981), the unreleased fifth album “The Last Flick of the Golden Wrench” (possibly identical with “The Robberies of the Rain”, which according to the author came out in 2009) and the tribute concert “Two Tiny Selves” in 2012 at The Castle pub. In Leven's memory he had a memorial bench placed in Soho Square. Tone: affectionate, very personal, a plea for an underrated band. In the comments further witnesses of the time come forward (concerts in Liverpool, Camden Lock, Farnborough, Blandford Forum) and a relative of Jo Shaw.
zitate_kontext: on Leven and friends at the Warwick Castle.

2026-07-10-ruta-66-sir-ian-rankin-el-pun.kurz: Agudo asks Ian Rankin about the relationship between rock music, his own writing and the character John Rebus.
inhalt: Agudo asks Ian Rankin about the relationship between rock music, his own writing and the character John Rebus. The introduction describes how the Spanish translations, from “Black & Blue” onwards, also made musical discoveries possible. Leven appears expressly as one of the musicians readers became aware of through the novels.

Rankin explains that music is so often central in his books partly because he himself would have liked to be a musician. The mentions in turn made musicians into readers and made personal meetings and joint appearances possible; as an example he names the collaboration with Leven on “Jackie Leven Said”. Asked about this mediating effect, he replies that he is pleased when readers thereby discover Leven, Mogwai or Blue Rose Code.

The conversation also covers punk as encouragement to write, Rankin's earlier band, Van Morrison and instrumental background music while working. It provides no new chronology of the relationship with Leven and names no first Rebus novel with a Leven reference. Its value lies in the reception continuing into 2026: a Spanish rock magazine asks Rankin specifically about Leven's discovery through the crime novels.

2026-07-26-lifo-jackie-leven-astypalaia-.kurz: Long essay by the Greek music critic Fontas Troussas introducing Leven to Greek readers by two routes: music and literature.
inhalt: Long essay by the Greek music critic Fontas Troussas introducing Leven to Greek readers by two routes: music and literature. First the connection with Ian Rankin (shared origin in Fife; Rankin discovered Leven through a record review, “Shining Brother Shining Sister” impressed him), the Crossing Border evening in The Hague in November 2003 and “Jackie Leven Said”; Troussas traces Rebus novel titles back to Leven songs (“Standing in Another Man's Grave” to “Another Man's Rain”, “Saints of the Shadow Bible” to “One Man One Guitar”, “A Heart Full of Headstones” to “Single Father”).

Greece is central: Leven lived on Astypalea in May and September of each year from 1991 to 1997 (about 14 months in all); Troussas translates Leven's booklet text for “Greek Notebook” (Haunted Valley, 1999; 33 pieces, 52:29) at length, including a cave-like house on a mountain top and about 40 hours of Walkman recordings. Later Leven described himself as a resident of Paxos; according to posts by Paxiots he loved Loggos, spent months there and sat on an old iron bench by the sea. After his death Deborah Greenwood had a memorial bench (backrest with a guitar body and strings, plaque) made by a local carpenter and placed at the entrance to the old customs house; in 2021 unknown persons threw it into the sea, it was fished out, repaired and put back. On 23 June 2022 a memorial concert took place in the old school of Loggos, with Greenwood, Jinder, Michael Weston King and the Paxiots Ilias Dendias and Spyros Kavvadas.

A personal section describes how Troussas knew “Control” as a Spanish Movieplay rarity and only learned from the Korean vinyl reissue of 2002 (Merry-Go-Round/Beatball, 500 copies, four-page liner notes) that John St. Field was Leven; he translates Leven's liner note (LSD phase 1971, pseudonym because of problems with the police). Finally, short reviews of “The Haunted Year / Spring” (2009) and “Lovers At The Gun Club” (2008), which he says he had earlier reviewed for the magazine “Jazz & Τζαζ”. Tone: knowledgeable, warm appreciation.
zitate_kontext: Caption/leitmotif: a wandering artist with an eventful life.

undatiert-god-save-the-sex-pistols-concr.kurz: Factual text on Concrete Bulletproof Invisible from the perspective of the Glen Matlock biography. The group came about because all members lived close to one another and drank in the same pub; first gig at a benefit concert at the Camden Palace for the bereaved of the late actor …
inhalt: Factual text on Concrete Bulletproof Invisible from the perspective of the Glen Matlock biography. The group came about because all members lived close to one another and drank in the same pub; first gig at a benefit concert at the Camden Palace for the bereaved of the late actor and singer Gary Holton, where encouraging words from Robbie Coltrane tipped the balance. Only release in 1988 on RadioActive: “Big Tears” (Matlock) / “Braid On My Shoulder” (Leven), 12" with “Good Thing” (Jo Shaw); keyboards James Hallawell, harmonica Mike Spencer, production Matlock and Dave Goodman. The US 12" (Dimension) contained “Love Kills”, recorded for the film “Sid & Nancy” but not used – according to Leven, speaking to Wavelength magazine, because it was “too well played”. Concerts in Scandinavia and Oban, among other places, no proper tour. Shaw meanwhile played with the Pretty Things, McIntosh with Test Dept and The Hit List (cf. Music Week, 25 May 1985: Hitlist with ex-members of Doll by Doll and Darts).

undatiert-gristlepop-jackie-leven-night-.kurz: American webzine review that contrasts Leven's reputation in Scandinavia, Germany and Scotland with indifference in the USA.
inhalt: American webzine review that contrasts Leven's reputation in Scandinavia, Germany and Scotland with indifference in the USA. Tone: benevolent but detached, a recommendation for folk listeners.
