undatiert-stv-artery-jackie-leven-dokume.autor: STV (editorial team unknown); upload by Ian Rodgers
undatiert-stv-artery-jackie-leven-dokume.kurz: TV portrait of about 24 minutes, according to the upload description an STV documentary, “ripped from my personal VHS recording” (uploaded 12 September 2018 by Ian Rodgers).
inhalt: TV portrait of about 24 minutes, according to the upload description an STV documentary, “ripped from my personal VHS recording” (uploaded 12 September 2018 by Ian Rodgers). According to the automatic transcript, the opening titles read “Musician – Jackie Leven, the man and his music” and apparently the STV arts magazine “Artery”. Leven speaks at original locations in Fife: on the old railway line in the Leven valley between Leslie and Markinch, where the little steam train stopped in front of his parents' house and showed him that there was life elsewhere; at Ravenscraig Castle near Dysart, where he sat alone as a teenager. He describes Leslie in the 1950s (father Cockney, mother “Romany Geordie”), gang rivalry with the new town of Glenrothes, his mother's blues records and his father's remark about the “screaming black men” in the house, the first guitar at about twelve in Kirkcaldy and his own invented tuning. Then Dorset in the mid-1970s, Doll by Doll from 1977 (“fierce on stage but beautiful on record”), drugs as a result of waiting for tours, an aggressive phase towards the end of the band. In detail: the attack after a night in the studio near Pentonville Road, almost two years without a voice, life in silence, heroin for pain, quitting after a defaced advertising poster of his then girlfriend, acupuncture and “psychic healing”, the founding of the CORE Trust with Princess Diana's support. Finally the return to Scotland's west coast (Kilchurn Castle, Oban), first singing in bars, thoughts on cadence in poetry and song, the press formula “Celtic Soul”. Interspersed are excerpts from “Call Mother a Lonely Field”, “Single Father”, “Marble City Bar” and Doll by Doll material. Tone: a serious, carefully filmed portrait with Leven as the narrator of his own life.
zitate_kontext: Leven's formula for Doll by Doll.

inhalt: Besides the dedicated Leven threads, Leven turns up in passing in many Afterword discussions: in “Encore Etiquette” (14 July 2026) JustTim praises Leven for having made it clear there were no encores; in “Scotland – the home of the rain song?” (3 June 2026) “Another Man's Rain”, “The History of Rain” and Sir Vincent Lone's “Feels Like Rain But Isn't” are named, with a pointer to Rankin's novel title; “A Heart Full of Headstones” (10 October 2022) notes that Rankin's book title comes from “Single Father”; in a thread of 26 September 2019 someone links a clip of the “Jackie Leven Band” at the Greyhound in 1983, and Kaisfatdad compares Leven with Michael Marra; “Who do you collect?” (2017), “Colin Hay” and “Honky Tonking with Marcel Proust” (2026) name him as a collectable or as a benchmark for storytelling on stage. The tone: in this forum Leven is a fixed point of reference.

undatiert-waatsveen-no-jackie-leven-et-l.kurz: Extensive memorial page by a Trondheim fan (URL slug “til minne 1950–2011”, last edited on 30 November 2025).
inhalt: Extensive memorial page by a Trondheim fan (URL slug “til minne 1950–2011”, last edited on 30 November 2025). The larger part is a biography in Norwegian compiled from familiar sources: childhood in Fife as a bullied outsider, early fatherhood at 16, Saint Judas recordings for the BBC in 1969, London years, Doll by Doll (Joe Shaw, David McIntosh, Helen Turner; producers and guests such as Tom Newman and David Gilmour), the attack in 1984 with loss of voice and record contract, heroin addiction, CORE Trust and the Diana episode, the solo career from 1994 with pseudonyms and fan-club albums, Ian Rankin and *Jackie Leven Said*, the last concert in Edinburgh in August 2011 and death on 14 November 2011. The author notes that band members and a producer dispute Leven's version of the attack, and calls the Dylan encounter disputed.

Personally: Waatsveen saw Leven live several times, describes him as a great storyteller and warm-hearted person, received signed CDs (dedication “Svein, we are the men”) and reproduces two friendly emails from Leven of 2008 as scans. Asked about his favourite place to play, Leven is said to have named the Polish Club in Kirkcaldy. He lists Norwegian venues (Røros, Stokkøya near Åfjord, Kabelvåg, Bergen, Oslo, Drammen), in Trondheim usually the Credo Bar in autumn; at the Credo concert in 2008 Leven told the story of “The Bonnie Earl of Moray”.
zitate_kontext: Leven on his audience (in Norwegian rendering).
